Welcome aboard — two ways to use the wiki

This wiki was created by sailors for sailors, to share what we’d like to find when entering a new roadstead. You can use it freely, without signing up, without limits and without adverts: browse the sheets, compare ports, download charts and waypoints, print what you need. It will stay that way.

Signing up is only if you wish, for two reasons:

  1. Receive the alerts that matter — only if you choose them: safety critical (L3 🚨), important warnings (L2 ⚠️) and general weather updates for the areas you follow. One email only when needed, never spam. Without signing up you receive nothing, but you can still browse the entire pilot.

  2. Contribute to the pilot — if you’ve been on site and want to add a verified price, a new buoy or a useful tip, with an account you can propose the update in your name (tracked and moderated).

In short: without signing up you read everything; with an account, if you wish, you stay updated and help others. The choice is yours, in one click. See Sign Up or Log In — or stay here and start exploring.

📥 Offline download per country: each country is downloadable as a ZIP (11 sheets + GPX WGS84 waypoints for OpenCPN/Navionics) — find the ⬇️ ZIP button next to the country name in the left sidebar and inside each 08-anchorages page. Full guide in Offline & GPX.

🔐 Sign up or browse without signing up — your choice: the pilot is always freely consultable without an account. If you wish, you can Sign up to receive safety alerts (L3/L2 for your areas, one email only when needed) or Log In to contribute. Browsing without signing up is perfectly fine.

Offline & GPX

Last checked: 28/08/2026

📥 Offline Download Per Country — ZIP + GPX

Every country has its own local ZIP with all pilot files + GPX WGS84 waypoints for your plotter. Download it before departure and keep it aboard: it works without internet.

What You Download Where to Find It Contents
Country ZIP On every 08-anchorages page → ⬇️ Country ZIP + ⬇️ GPX button · or zip/<country>.zip and gpx/<country>.gpx 11 files 00-10 + anc-*/rist-* sheets + gpx/<country>.gpx + README.txt
GPX waypoints gpx/<country>.gpx (also inside the ZIP) All verified anchorages for the country, datum WGS84, <sym>Anchor</sym>

ZIP/GPX files are regenerated at every pilot build. Coordinates are always in the water in the roadstead (never ashore), verified on satellite imagery. See also each country’s 08-anchorages for direct download buttons.

🧭 How to Load Waypoints on Your Plotter

OpenCPN (PC / Mac / Raspberry, free)

  1. Download gpx/<country>.gpx or zip/<country>.zip (extract the .gpx).
  2. Open OpenCPN → Route & Mark Manager → Import GPX (or drag the file onto the chart).
  3. Waypoints appear as yellow anchors with name and description anc-*. You can create a route: select waypoints → Create Route.
  4. Transfer to plotter/tablet if needed (e.g., via OpenCPN → Export or copy the GPX to SD).

Navionics Boating (iOS / Android)

  1. On your phone/tablet download gpx/<country>.gpx (or extract from the ZIP).
  2. Open Navionics → Menu → Routes & Tracks → Import GPX / Import File → select the GPX.
  3. Waypoints appear on the chart. Navionics imports name/desc/sym=Anchor — ideal for planning the approach into the roadstead.
  4. Tip: keep the GPX in the Navionics folder to re-import offline while underway.

Other Plotters (Garmin, B&G, Raymarine, Expedition)

  • All read GPX 1.1: import the file via SD card / USB or via Garmin ActiveCaptain / B&G Link. If the plotter expects rte instead of wpt, use the GPX as is (waypoints are already <wpt>) or convert with GPSBabel (gpsbabel -i gpx -o gpx -f in.gpx -F out.gpx).

⚠️ Warning

Coordinates are indicative (WGS84, approximate roadstead, not a precise fix). Always verify with official chart + sounder + visual observation before anchoring. See disclaimer on the home page.

About Us

SailTropics is an independent, collaborative, non-profit nautical pilot — community-driven, made by sailors for sailors.

It began as a shared logbook: the information we’d like to find when we enter a new roadstead, written by those who have actually been there.

What You'll Find

Entry, Documents & Visas · Yacht Customs Clearance · Cost of Living · Ports & Marinas · Services, Boatyards & Maintenance · Seasonality & Weather · Safety & Security · Provisioning · Anchorage Pilot with charts · Marine Trades & Chandlers · Restaurants.

Every country follows the same layout, for a like-for-like comparison.

How We Work

  • Ranked sources: every item carries a reliability rank ★★★★★ (official government source) down to ★ (dockside rumour), with verification date.
  • Periodic review: scheduled monthly check + automatic critical verification on what matters (safety, weather, visas, tariffs, regulations).
  • Never invented: if something is not verified, you’ll read DATA MISSING. That is our most important promise.
  • Conflicts disclosed: when sources contradict each other, we show you both versions with sources — we don’t choose for you.

Not a Commercial Site

No bookings, no adverts, no tracking, no profit. Just shared knowledge among people who go to sea.

© Open Licence

All original SailTropics content (texts, tables, layouts) is free to share: you may copy, reuse and adapt it for non-commercial purposes, with simple attribution (“SailTropics”). External sources cited (Cruising sources aggregate, Waterway Guide, government sites and others) remain the property of their respective authors: we report only the reference and reliability rating, never the third-party text.

⚠️ Disclaimer

Information and coordinates are indicative: they may be inaccurate, outdated or wrong and do not replace official charts, official pilots or direct verification on site. Anchorages, approaches, regulations and sea conditions must always be verified by the Skipper before and during the passage. Every decision and responsibility rests solely with the Skipper. The authors accept no liability for damage, loss, penalties or incidents arising from the use of this content.

📴 Offline

From the side menu you can download the complete pilot with offline charts as a ZIP per ocean. Download it before departure, unzip it on your device and open index.html: it works entirely offline.

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 25/08/2026

Status (EU/Italian citizens)

British Overseas Territory: British-style immigration policy, controls carried out directly by the local authorities on arrival.

EU Citizens — no visa, 90 days

For tourism, Italians/EU enter without a visa: on arrival a stay of 90 days is normally stamped. Passport recommended valid for 6 months (standard practice for British Overseas Territories). ivisitanguilla.com ★★★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★

Important note for those arriving by sea

  • Single port of entry: Road Bay (Sandy Ground). You must proceed there immediately and only the skipper goes ashore to the combined Customs & Immigration offices; Blowing Point clears only passenger ferries. ★★★★★
  • Office open daily 08:30–12:00 and 13:00–16:00. About 5 copies of the crew list and the clearance from the previous port are required. For stays under 24 h, entry and exit can be done in a single procedure. ★★★
  • Pre-arrival: no mandatory online form. SailClear appears in regional lists but is not used here (confirmed 2026). Caribbean Compass ★★★
  • Boat documents: vessel registration, crew passports, zarpe from previous port. Explicit request for radio CRC: DATA MISSING.

After the 90 days?

Procedure for extending your stay at the local Immigration office: DATA MISSING.

The boat

Item Cost
Entry+exit, yacht up to 20 tons (2 people) ~US$50 total
Cruising permit outside Road Bay required and EXPENSIVE, even for the tender
Passenger departure tax US$28 per adult

Temporary import regime for non-EU boats: DATA MISSING. Tariff source: Cruising sources aggregate ★★★

Vaccinations

No mandatory vaccination for those arriving from Europe; yellow fever certificate is only required when coming from at-risk countries (common rule for British Overseas Territories). Primary health source dedicated to Anguilla: DATA MISSING.

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 25/08/2026

Status (cittadini UE/italiani)

Stato indipendente del Commonwealth: due islands (Antigua e Barbuda) con un'unica giurisdizione migratoria e doganale.

EU Citizens — nessun visto, 90 giorni

Turisti italiani/UE senza visto fino a 90 giorni. visitantiguabarbuda.com ★★★★ · immigration.gov.ag ★★★★★

Important Note for Arrival by Sea

  • Pre-arrivo ONLINE su eSeaClear (dal 2026 compare anche SailClear come opzione aggiuntiva). Poi: bandiera gialla Q, tutto l'equipaggio a bordo, SOLO il capitano a terra. ABYMA ★★★
  • Sequenza: Dogana (clearance ultimo porto + General Declaration) → Immigrazione (ED card firmate per ciascuno, passaporti, CREW LIST IN 6 COPIE, dichiarazione salute) → ritorno in Dogana → Port Authority (pagamenti). Uscita: crew list in 4 copie, partenza entro 24 h dalla clearance out.
  • Porti d'ingresso: English Harbour (uffici a Nelson's Dockyard, validi anche per Falmouth), Jolly Harbour, Heritage Quay, Deep Water Harbour St John's, Crabbs. Barbuda: dogana a Codrington, ma quasi sempre conviene sdoganare ad Antigua; verificare PRIMA al +1268 460 0085. antiguanice.com ★★
  • Orari Nelson's Dockyard/Jolly: lun–ven 8–17, sab–dom 8–16 (bassa stagione metà mag→metà nov: 8–16). immigration.gov.ag ★★★★★

E dopo i 90 giorni?

Extension presso l'Extensions Unit dell'Immigration HQ: modulo dedicato, rilievo biometrico, biglietto di ritorno e pagamento di tasse. immigration.gov.ag ★★★★★

The Yacht

  • Cruising permit obbligatorio per navigare tra gli approdi (es. EC$85 segnalato a Jolly Harbour).
  • Tariffe variabili per lunghezza/stazza/equipaggio; in English/Falmouth Harbour e nelle marinas del National Park si sommano fee National Parks Authority e Port Authority.
  • Pagamenti in USD, EC$ or carta Visa/Mastercard; conservare le ricevute anche se si esce da un altro porto.
  • Documenti: registro nave e assicurazione (sempre richiesta in marina); eventuale richiesta doganale di patente/CRC: DATA MISSING.

Sources: ABYMA ★★★ · customs.gov.ag ★★★★★ · noforeignland ★★

Vaccinations

Nessuna vaccinazione obbligatoria dall'Europa; febbre gialla solo da paesi a rischio (standard CARICOM). Fonte sanitaria primaria dedicata: DATA MISSING.

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 27/08/2026

Status

Aruba is an autonomous constituent country of the Kingdom of the Netherlands (status land), with its own government and its own immigration and visa rules, separate from the European Netherlands and from the other Dutch Caribbean countries (Curaçao, Bonaire). It is outside the EU and outside the Schengen Area: EU/Schengen rules do not apply to entry into Aruba. [netherlandsworldwide.nl — Caribbean visa ★★★★★; visitaruba.com ★★★★★]

EU Citizens — No Visa Required

Item Rule Source
Visa Not required for EU citizens (including Italy) among the visa-exempt countries for the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom; the official exempt list includes Italy, France, Germany etc. netherlandsworldwide.nl “Do I need a visa for the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom?” — list of exempt countries ★★★★★
Required documents Passport not older than 10 years, valid for the entire stay; return or onward ticket; approved ED Card; proof of accommodation or ownership (including a pleasure yacht ≥14 m at the waterline); proof of sufficient means and medical insurance if required; documents for re-entry (residence permit/visa if needed for the country of return) netherlandsworldwide.nl “Requirements for travelling without a visa” ★★★★★; visitaruba.com “Required entry documents” ★★★★★; edcardaruba.aw ★★★★★
Standard stay 30 days on first admission as a tourist (the officer notes the days on the ED card); maximum total 180 days per calendar year as a tourist visitaruba.com “Duration of admission” ★★★★★; aruba.com immigration regulations ★★★★★
Linked visa exemptions Those holding a valid residence permit for the USA/Canada/Schengen/UK/Ireland or a multiple-entry Schengen/USA/UK visa (for certain nationalities: Bolivia, China, Cuba, Dominican Republic, Haiti, India, Jamaica, Peru etc.) are exempt from the Caribbean visa even if their nationality would otherwise require it netherlandsworldwide.nl ★★★★★; visitaruba.com “Visa required persons exempted” ★★★★★

⚠️ Caution: final admission is always at the discretion of the border officer at the port of entry; even with an approved ED card and no visa, entry may be refused or limited to fewer days if requirements are not met or in case of a blacklist. Holding a visa does not guarantee entry. [visitaruba.com ★★★★★]

Important Note for Arrival by Sea

  • People (IASA — Immigration) and yacht (Customs/Douane) controls are separate but both mandatory at the same port of entry: Immigration first, then Customs. The people formality requires the ED Card online for every crew member (not a visa, to be completed within 7 days before arrival at edcardaruba.aw and not by itself a guarantee of admission); for the yacht, Customs uses SailClear (sailclear.com) as a recommended pre-notice. [edcardaruba.aw ★★★★★; arubaports.com Yachting ★★★★★; Cruising sources aggregate Aruba ★★★]
  • Single port of entry for yachts: Barcadera (about 3 NM SE of Oranjestad). While the basin is under works, the Authority may temporarily divert to the northern basin of Oranjestad (Customs Quay / H Pier) — in any case always call Aruba Port Control on VHF 16/11 before entering and follow the tower's instructions; hoist a clearly visible yellow Q flag. [arubaports.com Yachting ★★★★★; Cruising sources aggregate Barcadera ★★★; aruba-cruisingguide.com ★★★]
  • Useful coordinates (WGS84): Barcadera entrance buoy 12°28.834' N 70°00.430' W; Barcadera customs quay 12°28.855' N 70°00.014' W; SE entrance Oranjestad 12°30.317' N 70°02.153' W; “Hans dock” Oranjestad 12°31.285' N 70°02.709' W. ⚠️ Shoal <1.2 m off the NW quay: stay in the ship channel (≥36 ft) until abeam the customs quay, then turn in — do not aim directly at the quay. With draught >3 m call Port Control for instructions (possible diversion to the container terminal). [arubaports.com ★★★★★; Cruising sources aggregate ★★★; aruba-cruisingguide.com “Clearing in Barcadera harbor” ★★★; blue-joline.com 2024 ★★★]
  • Alongside: berth at the customs quay (fenders to port on entry), only the skipper goes ashore with documents; crew remain on board in the “yellow” area (H Pier) until clearance is completed. After formalities officers come on board for inspection (rifles/spear guns seized). Arrival after 22:00: designated anchorage possible with Coast Guard permission, clearance the next morning. [arubaports.com ★★★★★; varaderoaruba.com Entry Procedure ★★★; aruba-cruisingguide.com ★★★]
  • Paper forms (printable in advance to speed up): Immigration 3 copies, Customs 2 copies (EN/ES/NL forms on arubaports.com). If not printed, available in the offices on the quay. Have ready: passports, approved ED cards, crew/passenger list, zarpe from the previous port (recommended). [arubaports.com Yachting — Download Forms ★★★★★; varaderoaruba.com ★★★]
  • See also the full yacht procedure in 01 — Clearance.

Staying Beyond 3 Months? (Italian/EU Citizens)

There is no unlimited tourist stay in Aruba as in the French Antilles: the regime is in stages with an annual cap.

Situation Rule Source
First 30 days Standard admission at the border for up to 30 days (the ED card stamp is decisive) visitaruba.com ★★★★★
Extension to 90 days Within the first 30 days you may request an extension to 90 days total: you need travel medical + liability insurance valid for the extended period and sufficient financial means (MFA guidance: 150–200 USD/day in a hotel, 100 USD/day with private hosts; local sponsor if guaranteed). Apply at the border or immediately after entry visitaruba.com “Extension of stay upon entry” ★★★★★; netherlandsworldwide.nl “Requirements … without a visa” (150–200 USD hotel / 100 USD private, insurance ≥15,000 USD covering hospital/emergency/repatriation) ★★★★★
Extension to 180 days Citizens of the Kingdom of the Netherlands may apply for up to 180 consecutive days. Visa-exempt nationals (EU/Italy included) and those exempt via a third-country visa/residence may apply for up to 180 consecutive days if: they own property in Aruba (house/apartment/timeshare or a pleasure yacht moored in Aruba ≥14 m at the waterline, with proof of ownership) OR they present a guarantee declaration from an Aruban resident (guarantor for all costs, to be legalised and sent via the guarantor to IASA: garantie@dga.aw). Without property, in practice an extension beyond 90 days requires a guarantor visitaruba.com ★★★★★; netherlandsworldwide.nl ★★★★★
After admission (already entered) If you wish to stay beyond the days granted on entry, apply to IASA — Vondellaan 25, Oranjestad, tel. +297 523-7402 (Mon–Thu 14:30–16:00 for extension requests). Documents: original extension form + copy of bio and stamped pages of passport (remaining validity ≥3 months), copy of ED card, copy of return ticket, copy of medical/liability insurance, guarantee declaration if applicable visitaruba.com “Extension of stay after admission — IASA” ★★★★★; gobierno.aw DIMAS/IASA ★★★★★
Annual cap Maximum 180 days per calendar year as a tourist (even adding multiple entries). Beyond that you need a DIMAS residence permit (Paardenbaaistraat 11, Oranjestad, tel. +297 522-1500). Staying beyond the granted days without an extension may lead to refusal of future admissions visitaruba.com ★★★★★; netherlandsworldwide.nl (90 days/180 days standard; 180 days/365 days for NL/US/Schengen in Aruba) ★★★★★
Extension fee No fee for a tourist extension application visitaruba.com (DIMAS letter) ★★★★★

The Yacht: No Unlimited Stay

No unlimited free circulation: a foreign yacht is admitted under temporary import with a cap.

Yacht Rule Source
Temporary import ≤180 days Temporary permit required if stay >7 days; maximum 180 days on the island, then the yacht must leave Aruba. No deposit if ≤180 days. Practice: declaration via customs broker to be started within day 2 (broker fee US$65–100). On expiry, before a new permit the yacht must stay outside for at least 15 days allatsea.net “NEW Aruba Customs Procedures” 2012 (still cited by local guides) ★★★; aruba-cruisingguide.com “Clearance Procedure” (yachts can stay up to 180 days) ★★★; blue-joline.com 2024 ★★★
Beyond 180 days up to 1 year Temporary permit with security deposit or bank guarantee equal to the duties due allatsea.net — excerpt of the rules ★★★
Beyond 1 year Definitive import (customs clearance) required allatsea.net ★★★
Ashore in entrepôt At Varadero Aruba (entrepôt area): the 180-day count is suspended while the yacht is stored ashore. Local operational reference aruba-cruisingguide.com “Varadero … entrepot area” ★★★; varaderoaruba.com ★★★
Environmental levy for yachts DATA MISSING — no government source found for a specific environmental levy for yachts; the Sustainability Fee US$20 is collected via the ED card (see below) —
Sustainability Fee US$20 Introduced 1 July 2024, collected via ED Card at edcardaruba.aw (Visa/Mastercard/Discover, line “Aruba Wastewater”). Exempt: residents, <8 years, transit <24h, serving crew, repeat visitors within 1 year (from 07/07/2025 automatic recognition via passport) and Aruban students abroad. For arrivals by sea the fee is due if you complete the ED Card and clear Immigration (yacht case); cruise passengers in transit <24h normally do not complete an ED card — check with the carrier awss.aw FAQ ★★★★★; aruba.com Sustainability Fee ★★★★★; edcardaruba.aw ★★★★★

Vaccinations

Item Rule Source
Yellow fever requirement Mandatory (International Certificate ICVP — “yellow booklet”) for all passengers arriving from endemic areas since 1 March 2018, on WHO/IHR recommendation. Validity: single lifetime dose, at least 10 days before arrival; if the certificate is lost it must be redone (no additional risk). To be shown to IASA officers on entry gobierno.aw “Gele Koorts vaccinatie” (Ministry of Health Aruba) ★★★★★; airportaruba.com Yellow Fever FAQ ★★★★★
Countries at risk (official Aruba list) Central/South America and Caribbean: Argentina, Bolivia, Peru, Ecuador, Colombia, Brazil, Venezuela, Paraguay, Panama, French Guiana, Guyana, Suriname, Trinidad and Tobago. Africa: Angola, Benin, Burkina Faso, Burundi, Cameroon, Central African Republic, Chad, Congo, DRC, Ivory Coast, Equatorial Guinea, Ethiopia, Gabon, Gambia, Ghana, Guinea, Guinea-Bissau, Kenya, Liberia, Mali, Mauritania, Niger, Nigeria, Senegal, Sierra Leone, South Sudan, Sudan, Togo, Uganda. Not considered at risk: Chile and Uruguay gobierno.aw ★★★★★
Yellow fever exemptions Transit <12h in an airport/port of a country at risk; transit in Aruba <24h (air/cruise) including airport exit/re-entry <24h; previous stay ≥6 days in a non-risk country without fever; <9 months and ≥60 years (vaccine not recommended) and other contraindications (pregnancy, immunosuppression, severe allergy to components) airportaruba.com FAQ (exceptions) ★★★★★; gobierno.aw DVG 29/07/2025 (vaccine not advised <9 months, >60 years, pregnancy etc.) ★★★★★
Other vaccines No other vaccine mandatory for arrivals from the EU/Italy. Mosquito protection recommended (dengue) — DATA MISSING on a specific requirement for yachtsmen: no government source found beyond yellow fever —
Where to get vaccinated in Aruba DVG Infectious Diseases Section, Avicenastraat 1, Oranjestad — appointment tel. +297 522-4200 at least 10 days before; cost Afl. 31 (debit card/bank transfer only), duplicate booklet Afl. 10 gobierno.aw DVG “Het is raadzaam … gele koorts” 29/07/2025 ★★★★★

Yacht Customs Clearance

Last checked: 27/08/2026 · Main source: Aruba Ports Authority — Yachting (arubaports.com) ★★★★★ + Varadero Aruba Entry Procedure ★★★ + edcardaruba.aw ★★★★★

Who Must Clear

All pleasure craft, regardless of flag and nationality, that: - enter Aruban waters arriving from a foreign port/foreign territorial waters or from the high seas; - depart for a foreign port/foreign waters or the high seas. Clearance is mandatory even if you intend only to transit or make a brief stop: anchoring or heading to a marina before completing immigration and customs at the port of entry is prohibited. [arubaports.com Yachting — ENTRY PROCEDURES ★★★★★; varaderoaruba.com "ALL BOATS must go clear … at Barcadera" ★★★; aruba-cruisingguide.com ★★★]

Crew must remain on board until clearance is completed (yellow area / H Pier). [arubaports.com ★★★★★]

Online Procedure

Aruba has no single portal like the French Antilles' "démarche-simplifiée": the digital part is advance notice + ED Card for persons, the rest is paper on the quay.

  1. Advance notice for the yacht — SailClear: Customs uses SailClear — complete it online before arrival (yacht details, owner, crew, last/next port, ETA, flag, MMSI, dimensions, engines, fuel). It does not replace the physical presence on the quay but speeds up processing. [Cruising sources aggregate Aruba "Customs use SailClear" ★★★; aruba-cruisingguide.com ★★★]
  2. Advance notice for persons — ED Card: every person on board (including infants) must complete the ED Card at edcardaruba.aw within 7 days before arrival, entering passport details, flight/vessel, accommodation (for yachts: yacht name/port). The ED Card is not a visa and does not by itself guarantee admission, but it is a mandatory entry requirement and must be shown to Immigration (IASA). Any Sustainability Fee of US$20 is integrated into the ED Card (see Fees). [edcardaruba.aw ★★★★★; visitaruba.com ★★★★★; aruba.com immigration ★★★★★]
  3. Paper forms (optional but recommended to save time): print Immigration 3 copies + Customs 2 copies (PDF EN/ES/NL on arubaports.com). If not printed, they are available in the offices on the quay. [arubaports.com Download Forms ★★★★★]
  4. Approach: about 30 minutes before arrival call Aruba Port Control on VHF 16 (switch to 11 or 14 as instructed by the tower) and request permission to enter for clearance; follow instructions to the berth and hoist the yellow Q flag. [arubaports.com ★★★★★; aruba-cruisingguide.com ★★★]
  5. Berthing: berth at the Barcadera customs quay (or, if diverted, at the Customs Quay / H Pier in Oranjestad on Port Control instructions). Only the skipper goes ashore: first Immigration (yellow stamp), then Customs/Douane (purple stamp). Crew remain on board. After signing, officers board for inspection (firearms/spear guns seized). [varaderoaruba.com ★★★; arubaports.com ★★★★★; blue-joline.com 2024 ★★★]
  6. Temporary yacht declaration (broker): by the next day and no later than day 2, a customs broker must start the temporary import procedure (see 00 — The Yacht). The broker files the declaration with Customs. [allatsea.net 2012 ★★★; aruba-cruisingguide.com ★★★]
  7. Departure (clearance out): always notify Aruba Port Control on VHF 16 to agree berth and timing with customs/immigration; once formalities are complete you must depart immediately. [arubaports.com "CLEARANCE PROCEDURES OUT OF PORT OF ORANJESTAD" ★★★★★]

Useful Tip (★★★)

Complete SailClear and the ED Card a few days in advance and bring 3+2 pre-filled copies plus a separate crew list: the offices at Barcadera are small and the queue moves faster with forms ready. Also print the Sustainability Fee payment receipt if applicable.

Stamped Paper Copy

  • In Aruba there is no electronic "attestation" printable from a portal: the stamped receipts are the paper copies issued on the quay by Immigration (IASA) and Customs after the skipper's signature. Keep them on board: they serve as the zarpe (clearance) for the next port and as proof of temporary import. [varaderoaruba.com ★★★; arubaports.com — Customs clearance form (fields Rotation Ref. No., Date Customs, Signature Master) ★★★★★]
  • Until you are stamped, you have not legally entered: remain on the quay/yellow area; for arrivals after 22:00 a designated anchorage with Coast Guard permission is provided, with formalities completed the next morning. [arubaports.com ★★★★★]

Official Ports of Entry in Aruba (official list Aruba Ports Authority ★★★★★)

Aruba has a single port of entry for yachts: Barcadera (with temporary diversion to Oranjestad on Port Control instructions). There is no extensive network like the French "points agréés".

Location Point Coordinates (WGS84) Contacts Hours
Barcadera Customs quay NW (quay with wooden bulkhead) — Immigration + Customs offices on the quay Entrance buoy 12°28.834' N 70°00.430' W; quay 12°28.855' N 70°00.014' W Aruba Port Control VHF 16/11; APA tel. +297 523-4300 (office hours) · Marine Traffic Control Tower +297 523-4336/37 (24/7) · info@arubaports.com / KustStation@arubaports.com DATA MISSING — no government source found with Immigration/Customs office hours at Barcadera; to be verified on site/VHF (arrivals after 22:00 with Coast Guard permission)
Oranjestad (diversion) Customs Quay / H Pier — second basin W of cruise quay ("Hans dock") — as assigned by Port Control SE entrance 12°30.317' N 70°02.153' W; Hans dock 12°31.285' N 70°02.709' W Same APA/Port Control contacts VHF 16 DATA MISSING — hours not published; operation on Port Control call (Immigration must come down from Barcadera) ★★★

Nautical notes for Barcadera (verified from three sources): stay in the ship channel until abeam the quay (white buoy/white tanks as reference), then turn in keeping two round bollards to port and two square bollards to starboard; draught up to 2.1 m can go to the end of the wooden quay keeping one beam off the quay; 3 m only to the corner of the black tug; >3 m call Port Control for alternative instructions (container terminal or Oranjestad). [aruba-cruisingguide.com "To get to the customs dock" ★★★; Cruising sources aggregate Barcadera ★★★; blue-joline.com ★★★]

Cruisers' Experiences

  • Barcadera offices described as friendly and efficient once berthed, although the area (industrial zone, landfill to NW) is not scenic — berth with fenders and lines ready on the berthing side (usually port). ★★★ (aruba-cruisingguide.com; cruiserswiki.org)
  • At Barcadera the cross-wind manoeuvre requires preparation; have helpers ashore ready for lines. ★★★ (blue-joline.com 2024)
  • Calling 30 min before arrival speeds up the Immigration officer's arrival (who must come down from Barcadera if you are diverted to Oranjestad). ★★★ (aruba-cruisingguide.com)
  • Oranjestad Customs Quay criticised because the quay is not designed for small boats and is close to cruise traffic — Barcadera is preferable when available. ★★ (Cruising sources aggregate cruisers' comments)

Penalties

  • Remaining in Aruban waters without immigration consent is an offence ("It is considered an offense to remain in Aruban waters without the prior consent of the immigration authorities"). [arubaports.com Yachting — REQUIREMENTS ONCE IN ARUBAN WATERS ★★★★★]
  • Overstaying the granted days without an extension may result in refusal of future admissions and a blacklist entry at border control. [visitaruba.com "Staying longer … can have negative consequences for future admission ; Admission can be refused if … blacklisted" ★★★★★]
  • Undeclared / not surrendered weapons and spear guns: immediate seizure on inspection and possible customs penalties — DATA MISSING on fine amount: no published penalty table found on arubaports.com or gobierno.aw; to be verified with Customs on the quay. [varaderoaruba.com / Fonti diportiste aggregate — "rifles and spear guns will be seized" ★★★]
  • Details of customs/immigration fine amounts: DATA MISSING — no government source with a penalty tariff for failure to clear a yacht found on overheid.aw / dimasaruba.aw as of 27/08/2026; verify with APA/Douane before your cruise.

To Verify Before Your Cruise

  • Immigration/Customs office hours at Barcadera / Oranjestad (not published on arubaports.com as of 27/08/2026) — ask Port Control VHF 16/11 or Varadero Aruba (+297 588-3840).
  • Possible marina pre-notification requirement (some local guides indicate Varadero/Wind Creek must notify authorities 3 days in advance — rule not confirmed by a government source ★★★, to be verified with your chosen marina).
  • Changes to Barcadera ↔ Oranjestad diversion: basin works may shift the clearance point — confirm with Port Control on approach.
  • Updated penalty tariff and list of authorised customs brokers (Landseair +297 582-9284, Ashley Broker +297 593-8305 / ashleybroker@setarnet.aw cited only on allatsea.net ★★ — to be confirmed with Customs).

Last updated: 27/08/2026

Currency: Aruban florin (AWG, Afl.) pegged at 1 USD = 1.79 AWG (1.80 in shops/taxis); US dollars are accepted everywhere, change is often given in florins. Ports & Marinas

Last checked: 27/08/2026 · Coordinates WGS84 in decimal degrees and N/W as per source · VHF 16 for Port Control

Leeward West Coast — Oranjestad, Lagoon and Beaches

This is the leeward side sheltered from the trade winds, where almost all yachting infrastructure is concentrated. Shallow waters with barrier reef, sandy bottoms; beware of reefs and marine areas with anchoring bans on the windward coast.

Renaissance Marina / Oranjestad ⚓ Main Harbour

  • 12°31'05" N 70°02'20" W (12.518°N 70.039°W) · VHF 16/14 (Port Control) ★★★ Navily Renaissance Marina 12°31.08' N 70°02.33' W ★★★
  • In the heart of Oranjestad, next to the Renaissance Marketplace and the cruise quay. About 100 berths for yachts up to 60 m and draught 4.5 m, sheltered and guarded; water, electricity, fuel and resort facilities (pool, private island with shuttle). The island's only "urban" marina: advance booking mandatory in high season. ★★ SailJournal; MailASail Dora Mac 2025; Wind Creek Marina +297-588-0260 ★★★
  • Adjacent Wind Creek Marina (Renaissance Marketplace, LG Smith Blvd 9 · +297-588-0260): 40 berths with fresh water, electricity, telephone and 24h security; promenade pontoon. ★★★ windcreekmarina.com ★★★
  • Clearance: not at the marina. Yacht customs is at Barcadera (see 01) — call Port Control VHF 16 30' before arrival, Q flag, await instructions. ★★★★★ Aruba Ports Authority
  • Shelter: excellent protection from NE trades; ground swell from N/NW during winter swells — check local forecast before entering. ★★

Varadero Aruba Marina & Boatyard — Technical Hub and Hurricane Storage

  • 12°29'53" N 70°01'02" W (12.498°N 70.017°W) · Bucutiweg 34, Oranjestad · +297 588-3850 · varaderoaruba.com ★★★ Marinas.com; HarbourGuides ★★★
  • Well sheltered inside the lagoon, main business is dry storage "off customs" for hurricane season. 70+ berths afloat with 110/220 V electricity and free drinking water; fuel (diesel and RON 95) on the quay, Wi-Fi, laundry, CCTV, night guard, travelift/crane, boatyard. Water berths are charged per calendar day, not per night; book by email. ★★★ HarbourGuides; Navily Varadero ★★★
  • Fuel on the quay recorded: diesel 2.56 AWG/l · RON 95 2.66 AWG/l (indicative, from community reviews). ★★★ Navily Varadero Fuel
  • Arashi Bay and the lagoon off it: excellent sand anchorage before entering the marina — many crews anchor off then enter for haul-out. ★★ MailASail Dora Mac 2025

Eagle Beach / Palm Beach — Fair-Weather Anchorages

  • Tourist coastline N of Oranjestad, sandy bottom 3–8 m, good holding but exposed to W/NW swell; anchor only in settled weather and never overnight without a watch. Hotel private buoys/moorings — do not use without permission; respect swim zones. ★★
  • Dinghy dock: beach landing; beware of surf when swell is up — bow up and stern anchor. Always lock dinghy and outboard. ★★

North-West Coast — Malmok, Arashi, California Lighthouse

  • Arashi / Malmok roadstead (NW tip): sand with some rock patches, 4–10 m; fair shelter from the trades but open to the N. Very busy by day for snorkelling, quiet at sunset — good staging point before jumping to Curaçao/Bonaire. ★★ [Cruising sources aggregate/Cruisers reports] ★★
  • Approach from W: low coast with drying reef — keep >0.5 NM off the rocks and follow the 10 m contour to the anchor spot; at night enter only with verified waypoints and echo sounder. ★★

Windward East and South Coast — Barcadera, Spanish Lagoon, Baby Beach

  • Barcadera: commercial harbour and only clearance point for yachts (see coordinates in 01: entrance buoy 12°28.834' N 70°00.430' W; customs quay 12°28.855' N 70°00.014' W). Dredged channel but busy with ships and tugs — stay in the channel until abeam the quay, then turn in on Port Control VHF 16/11 instructions. Not a leisure stop. ★★★★★ [Aruba Ports Authority] ; ★★★ [Cruising Guide Aruba]
  • Spanish Lagoon / Savaneta / Mangel Halto: shallows and mangroves, uneven depths — dinghy or shoal-draught boats only with local knowledge; many areas closed to anchoring to protect reef. ★★
  • San Nicolas Bay / Baby Beach (SE tip): semi-circular bay sheltered by reef, white sand, 2–5 m — popular day anchorage, overnight only in settled weather with light E wind. Keep clear of the buoyed swim zone. ★★

Seasonality & Weather

Last checked: 27/08/2026

Climate

  • Average temperature 28.5 °C (annual mean), 27.3 °C Dec–Feb and 29.5 °C Aug–Oct; hot semi-arid steppe BSh/BW climate of the southern Dry Zone, moderate to fresh E trades. ★★★★★
  • Average rainfall ~498 mm/year highly variable (years <200 mm and >1000 mm); sea temperature 25.9 °C Feb–Mar and 28.2 °C Sep–Oct; daily range greater than seasonal range. ★★★★★

Seasons

Period Characteristics
February – June Dry season, steady trades and mostly clear skies: best period for cruising
September – January Rainy season with brief showers in the morning/early evening; peak Oct–Dec; Jul–Sep transition

★★★

Hurricane Procedures (official ★★★★)

Aruba has no French-style cyclone plan; follow alerts from the Meteorological Department Aruba (DMA) and instructions from the harbour master/Port Control VHF 16; Varadero in the lagoon is the preferred shelter but no berth is 100% guaranteed in a cyclone.

Hurricanes

Season 1 June–30 November, peak mid-August–mid-October. Aruba lies on the southern edge of the hurricane belt: major damage from a cyclone passing to the south about once in 100 years; effects possible from systems to the north (erosion, heavy swell, coastal flooding). Hurricanes with trailing impact: Hazel (1954), Ivan (2004, waves and flooding), Felix (2007, centre 80 km away). [DMA meteo.aw ★★★★★; meteo.cw ★★★★★; aruba.com ★★★]

Local Winds

  • Trades from E/ENE 12–20 kt, average 7.6 m/s stronger in the dry/transition season and lighter in the wet season; acceleration gusts between the ABC islands and in the lee of low hills. ★★★★★
  • Saharan dust (SAL) and Atlantic high pressure can reduce visibility and bring seas from E–NW 4–7 ft with small-craft warnings on exposed coasts. ★★★★

Typical Weather Windows

Short passages Aruba–Curaçao (~68 NM) or Aruba–Bonaire (~105 NM) feasible with trades ≤18–20 kt, best departing at dawn; for long passages to Colombia/Venezuela wait for a window after a tropical wave with stable pressure. Inter-island channels: confused seas — avoid wind >20 kt. ★★

Safety & Security

Last full check: 27/08/2026 · Next monthly check: 27/09/2026

Safety Rating: 4 / 5

Aspect Rating Reason
Personal safety (tourists/cruisers) 4/5 Canadian/US/UK advisories at the lowest level (normal precautions); violent crime against visitors rare and not targeted
Theft from yacht 3/5 Dinghy/outboard and cockpit items: 5 CSSN incidents in the last 5 years within 10 km of Oranjestad — limited but real risk if not locked
General island context 4/5 Overall crime moderate-low, heavily patrolled tourist island with rapid response in hotel areas

Scale: 0 = terrible → 5 = very safe. Our rating, synthesising the sources below; updated at each monthly check.

Why not 5: recurring opportunistic theft on beaches, in rental cars and from dinghies (even in the marina and at anchor), plus slightly higher risk in San Nicolas and on isolated roads/areas after dark; armed robbery reported by advisories as possible against cash-heavy businesses or activities linked to drug transit. No wave of targeted violence against yachtsmen in the last 5 years of sources.

General Overview

  • Canadian government advisory (updated 29/07/2026 ★★★★): "Take normal security precautions" — the lowest of four levels. Petty crime (pickpocketing, bag snatching, theft from cars and hotels/apartments) and residential burglary; peak at Carnival (Jan–Mar); avoid sparsely populated areas and unsupervised beaches after dark and always secure documents and valuables.
  • US advisory — Department of State (Level 1 of 20/08/2026 ★★★★): "Exercise normal precautions". Aruba is generally considered safe; the most likely crimes are in tourist areas with theft of unattended goods and car break-ins; overall rates low; armed robbery possible against businesses holding large amounts of cash or drug/gang-related activities; importing firearms, ammunition and even cartridge cases without written authorisation is prohibited — prolonged detention is provided for.
  • UK advisory FCDO (updated 07/07/2026 ★★★★): risk of petty theft and occasional street incidents; recommendations: do not walk in remote areas at night, do not leave valuables or bags in cars, do not take much cash/valuables to the beach, keep bags closed and not grabbable; Aruba is a transit corridor for drug trafficking South America → Europe/North America with possible related crime; terrorism with no recent history on the island but not excludable.
  • Government of Aruba (gobierno.aw ★★★★★): single emergency number 911 for police/fire/ambulance; police stations Oranjestad 100, San Nicolas 104, Noord 107, Santa Cruz 105; hospital 527 4000.
  • Operational context: compact island (~30 km) with constant presence of the Korps Politie Aruba (KPA) in tourist areas and often rapid response under 15 minutes in Oranjestad, Palm Beach and Eagle Beach; widespread private security in resorts/marinas. ★★

Theft Against Cruisers

Data from Caribbean Safety and Security Net (thecssn.org ★★★), check 27/08/2026:

  • 5 incidents in the last 5 years within 10 km of Oranjestad (Renaissance/Surfside radius): no episode with violence against persons.
  • Details: Renaissance Marina 26/09/2022 — dinghy/outboard stolen at night from charter catamaran on davits, not locked (later found in mangroves without engine) ★★★; Surfside Beach Anchorage 01/10/2022 — unlocked dinghy stolen while crew slept ★★★; Surfside 11/07/2023 — Highfield + Yamaha 25 HP stolen unlocked ★★★; Renaissance Marina 20/02/2025 — binoculars stolen from cockpit between 06:00 and 08:00, yacht alongside ★★★; Eagle Beach 02/08/2025 — 2 fishing rods + snorkelling gear stolen from cockpit at night, catamaran at anchor ★★★.
  • Recurring hotspots: quays and anchorage of Renaissance/Surfside and roadstead of Eagle Beach; even unlocked tenders were taken; in one case cable cut.
  • Effective countermeasures reported: short chain + padlock through outboard and to the yacht, engine always secured with dedicated lock, tender hoisted in davits or on board at night, nothing left visible in cockpit/dinghy, alarm/lighting.
  • Reporting: police 100 / emergency 911, coast guard 913, marina and VHF 16; online CSSN report; local VHF groups for rapid alerts.

Rescue & Emergencies

  • Control centres: 911 routes to police/ambulance/fire; 100 direct police; 913 Dutch Caribbean Coast Guard for rescue at sea; VHF 16 always monitored by Port Control and Coast Guard.
  • Main hospital Dr. Horacio E. Oduber Hospital in Oranjestad, 24h A&E on +297 527 4000; serious cases may require medical evacuation with dedicated insurance (air ambulance/transfer to Curaçao/Colombia/USA) — also cover for divers (no hyperbaric chamber on site) ★★★.
  • Consular assistance: no Canadian office on site — reference Embassy of Canada in Bogotá (+57-601 657-9800) covering Aruba/Bonaire/Curaçao; USA via Consulate General in Curaçao (+599 9 461-3066, after-hours emergency +599 9 433-2200) ★★★★; United Kingdom via FCDO London 020 7008 5000 (24h).
  • Under way: call Aruba Port Control VHF 16/11 before entering Barcadera (30' before), show Q flag and await instructions; for emergencies at sea call 913 in addition to VHF 16.
  • Hurricanes: island south of the main belt (season Jun–Nov), direct hits rare but passing tropical systems can bring strong wind, swell and rain — monitor NHC and local media in season ★★★★.

Provisioning

Last checked: 27/08/2026

General Price Level

  • Groceries more expensive than in mainland Europe/USA because almost everything is imported (USA, Netherlands, Spain); fresh fish and tropical fruit locally are better value. Currency: Aruban Florin (AWG, ƒ) pegged at 1 USD ≈ 1.80 AWG; USD accepted everywhere and ATMs plentiful. ★★★
  • Compared with other ABC islands and the Grenadines, wide "American-style" choice but at "island" prices: it pays to do a full provisioning if staying long or departing for long passages to Colombia/Panama. Local produce: fishermen's catch at the quay, fruit/veg from trucks and stalls, bread/bakery inside supermarkets. ★★

Super Food Plaza and Kong Hing are the references for those anchored at Eagle/Palm Beach or Surfside: frequent bus Oranjestad–Noord (15–30 min), fare 1–2 USD; for heavy loads better to agree a taxi in advance. ★★★

San Nicolas / Savaneta

Southern town with small supermarkets, minimarkets and fruit trucks in the central streets; limited provisioning: for a big shop head to Oranjestad/Noord. Savaneta has small residential groceries — convenient if anchored at Spanish Lagoon/Mangel Halto with dinghy + taxi. ★★

Markets

  • Oranjestad fishermen's quay: fresh catch in the morning (tuna, wahoo, mahi) — arrive early and light haggling; daily availability varies. ★★
  • Fruit/veg stalls and trucks: along the Oranjestad–San Nicolas corridor and at Noord; mango, papaya, plantain in season. No large daily covered market — main provisioning remains the supermarket. ★★
  • Fisheries / occasional markets: stalls and vendors on Caya Betico Croes and at San Nicolas, especially in carnival season and at weekends. ★★

Service Where Notes

Practical Tips

  • Folding trolley on board: Ling & Sons is walkable from the marina; Super Food needs taxi or bus — with heavy loads a taxi at a fixed fare agreed in advance (not metered) is best, or supermarket delivery by arrangement (Super Food has delivered to the marina on request) ★★★.
  • Holiday hours: large stores Mon–Sat 08:00–20:00/21:00, Sun 09:00–18:00/13:00 depending on chain; local mini-marts often 07:00–21:00 daily — check before long passages and stock up on bottled water where mains is not guaranteed drinkable.
  • Ice and fresh produce: available in all mega-supermarkets (bagged ice, in-store bakery and fish counter); for large galleys order online 24h ahead (shop.superfoodaruba.com, lingandsons.com) with collection or agreed delivery. ★★★
  • Payment: Aruban florins AWG and USD 1:1.80 accepted everywhere; Visa/MC everywhere, ATMs at 50+ locations; keep cash for fruit trucks and taxis. ★★★★

Anchorage Pilot

Last checked: 27/08/2026 · indicative coordinates, navigate with official chart

General Anchoring Rules (First and Foremost)

  • Free anchoring is permitted on the leeward side (west-south coast) only on sand, EXCEPT the prohibited zones below and the coral/seagrass bottoms protected by Parke Marino Aruba (anchoring on coral prohibited, use only sand or buoys where present). ★★★★
  • IALA-B throughout the Caribbean: red to starboard when entering harbour (reversed vs. Europe). Always call Port Control VHF 16 for entry into the Oranjestad channel and for any movement inside the basin. ★★★★
  • Barrier reef: always keep >0.5 NM off the drying reef at the north-west (Malmok/Arashi), enter only in good light following the 10 m contour; at night only with verified waypoints and echo sounder. ★★

⛔ Absolute No-Go Zones (Official)

Area Prohibition Source
Parke Marino Aruba — MPA Arikok, Mangel Halto, Sero Colorado, Oranjestad Reef Islands Anchoring prohibited on coral/seagrass and shallows; in many areas buoys mandatory once installed (AB 2018 no.77) FPNA ★★★★
Barrier reef and reef islets Anchoring or laying chain on coral prohibited; tying to mangroves prohibited AB 2018 no.77 art.9c ★★★★
Oranjestad channel and basin Anchoring prohibited in the dredged channel and cruise basin; berthing only on Port Control instructions Aruba Ports Authority ★★★★★
Barcadera channel Anchoring prohibited in the commercial channel; transit only with authorisation VHF 16/11 Aruba Ports Authority ★★★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
Private buoys and swim zones Charter/hotel buoys and beach swim corridors not usable without permission; respect swim markings aruba-cruisingguide.com ★★★
Bucuti Shoal Shoal 1.9 m between charter buoys and Bucuti Yacht Club — do not cross outside the channel aruba-cruisingguide.com ★★★

Full texts: FPNA — Management Plan Marine Park and Ramsar sheet Parke Marino Aruba (no-anchor policy). ★★★★

  • The depths of the Oranjestad (12.5' entrance) and Barcadera (2.2 m for Varadero) channels must be verified with Aruba Ports Authority NtMs before entering. ★★★★★
  • For day-to-day navigation: official electronics on plotter + local guides as backup; IALA-B buoyage everywhere. ★★★

Not Included (For Now)

  • Rodgers Beach / San Nicolas (SE tip): semi-circular bay sheltered by reef, 2–5 m, popular day stop but without verified coordinates in the water — to be verified with satellite check ★★
  • Spanish Lagoon / Mangel Halto / Savaneta: mangroves and shallows, uneven depths, dinghy/shoal-draught only and Parke Marino bans — to be verified ★★
  • Arashi / California Lighthouse (NW): roadstead open to N with drying reef, fair holding but exposed to winter swell — only in settled weather, not for overnight without a watch ★★

Anchor Checklist for Aruba

  1. Clearance at Barcadera done? → 01 Clearance · VHF 16 30' before arrival
  2. Waypoints for Oranjestad channel (SE buoy 12°30.317' N 70°02.153' W) and Varadero Channel (12°29.577' N 70°01.133' W) loaded on plotter
  3. BA/NV chart up to date + IALA-B (red to starboard when entering) in mind
  4. Bottom: only sand — never coral (Parke Marino), check good holding after dropping
  5. Charter/hotel buoys avoided (do not use 09:00–17:00 at Antilla, others only with permission)
  6. Dinghy padlocked, outboard secured — theft possible on docks at night

Marine Trades & Chandlers

Technical hub concentrated between Varadero Aruba Marina & Boatyard (Bucutiweg 34) and Wind Creek Marina / Renaissance Marketplace (LG Smith Blvd 9). For major works always ask for a written quote and confirm lead times in high season (Dec–Apr), when yards are full for hurricane-season storage outside the hurricane belt. Contact typically by phone/WhatsApp; English and Dutch (Papiamento) spoken.

Where to Find What

  • Engine/fridge/welding: freelancers operating at Varadero (Certified list above) + mobile network on call at the marina; ask at Wind Creek/Varadero harbour office. ★★★
  • Sails: no resident sailmaker — Aruba Rigging + itinerant sailmakers in season; major jobs at Antigua/St. Martin/Trinidad. ★★
  • Electronics/on-board power: Raffi Solar4Me (Varadero) + ordering via Budget Marine / EWMS; spares from Miami via Wind Creek "Yacht in Transit". ★★★
  • Antifouling/careening: Varadero only (Roodberg 20/60 t, max 80'/42' beam) — the only hydraulic trailer in the ABCs with >35 ft beam capacity. ★★★★

Practical Notes

  • Payments: bank transfer/cash/card; for small jobs often cash. Always ask for an invoice (useful for customs/insurance). At Varadero external contractors pay 15% commission to the yard — include it in the quote.
  • Lead times: spares from Europe/US = 1–3 weeks via DHL/Colissimo; workshops often order via Miami. Common practice: order online and ship "Yacht in Transit — YACHT NAME" c/o Wind Creek Marina, LG Smith Blvd 9, Oranjestad with tracking.
  • Overwintering: Varadero offers 150 "Entrepot" off-Customs places (180-day count suspended) — book well in advance (Jul–Nov full). Dredged channel access 2.20 m; for marginal draughts request Navionics file "Follow the Navionics path" (Jul 2024) from Varadero. ★★★★
  • On-board power: lithium/solar components on order (Budget Marine/EWMS); installation with Raffi Solar4Me at Varadero.
  • For specialist work: consider regional hubs Antigua (English Harbour), Sint Maarten (Simpson Bay), Trinidad (Chaguaramas) with dozens of professionals and travelifts up to 300 t.

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 24/08/2026 · Bahamas — Commonwealth, former British colony independent since 1973

Status

The Bahamas are an independent island state (700 islands and cays). For Italian/EU citizens, tourism is visa-free. ★★★★★

Italian / EU Citizens — Visa-Free Tourism

Item Rule Source
Tourist visa Not required for Italian/EU citizens: entry permitted for up to 90 days with stamp on arrival Bahamas Immigration ★★★★★
Passport Passport with ≥6 months remaining validity from date of arrival — mandatory Bahamas Immigration ★★★★★
Return/onward ticket Return air ticket or proof of onward departure required within the granted period Bahamas Immigration ★★★★
Proof of funds Proof of sufficient financial means for the stay may be requested Bahamas Immigration ★★★★
Immigration Card Immigration card issued on arrival (former Bahamas Customs Declaration / Immigration Card) — keep it Bahamas Immigration ★★★★
Minors If travelling with only one parent or with third parties: notarised consent letter from the other parent/guardian + possible proof of custody Bahamas Immigration ★★★★

Extension of Stay

Situation Rule Source
Stay beyond 90 days Request for extension up to 8 months total at the Department of Immigration in Nassau or district offices (Freeport, etc.) — apply before expiry, approval at discretion Bahamas Immigration ★★★★
Work / residence Not permitted on a tourist entry — specific permit required before arrival Bahamas Immigration ★★★★★
Yacht stay The yacht with a valid 12-month cruising permit may remain even if the crew must extend or exit/re-enter — see 01 — Clearance Bahamas Customs ★★★★★

The Yacht: Cruising Permit & Documents

Foreign pleasure vessels must obtain a cruising permit / FDCC on arrival via Click2Clear (digital only since 22/02/2021). Standard validity 12 months for the Temporary Cruising Permit, 2 years for the Frequent Digital Cruising Card (FDCC) for frequent returners — see costs and options in 01 — Clearance. Keep on board: vessel registration/ownership document, insurance (recommended), crew list. ★★★★★

Health & Vaccinations

Item Rule Source
Mandatory vaccinations from EU/Italy None required for direct arrivals from Europe/Italy/USA Bahamas Ministry of Health / WHO ★★★★★
Yellow fever Mandatory only if arriving (even transit >12h) from an endemic area: 34 African countries + South America + Panama. In that case an International Certificate of Vaccination is required WHO / Bahamas Health ★★★★★
COVID-19 No restrictions, no test/certificate required on entry Bahamas Health ★★★★★
Recommended vaccinations Routine vaccinations up to date (tetanus, hepatitis A/B as per medical advice) — no requirement on entry WHO ★★★

⚠️ Always check before departure on the official Bahamas Immigration and Bahamas Ministry of Health websites: rules on minors and yellow fever are strictly enforced at the border.

← Bahamas

Clearance

Last checked: 24/08/2026 · Main source: Bahamas Customs & Bahamas Maritime Authority — Click2Clear portal (besw.gov.bs) ★★★★★

Who Must Clear

All pleasure vessels entering Bahamian waters from abroad must clear at a designated Port of Entry. The procedure has been digital only since 22/02/2021 via Click2Clear. No paper form at the dock any more. ★★★★★

Click2Clear Procedure — Online Only

  1. Register at https://besw.gov.bs (Bahamas Electronic Single Window) and create your Click2Clear account before arrival. ★★★★★
  2. Fill in the Pleasure Craft Declaration: vessel details (name, registration, flag, LOA, draught), owner/skipper, complete crew manifest (passports), weapons and pets on board (if any), previous/next port, ETA. ★★★★★
  3. Submit the declaration: the system generates a Rotation Number. ★★★★★
  4. Online payment by Visa (only card accepted online) or declaration of cash payment on arrival — WARNING: approval is not issued until payment is credited; if you choose "cash on arrival" you must pay at Customs and wait for release. ★★★★★
  5. Print/save to your phone the approved Cruising Permit with QR/Rotation Number.

Useful tip: your Click2Clear profile saves vessel and crew — for subsequent exits/re-entries simply duplicate the previous application and update only dates and port. ★★★

Arrival — What to Do at Sea and Ashore

Phase Rule
Approaching Fly Q flag (yellow) and call the chosen Designated Port of Entry on VHF 16; ask for instructions for the customs berth ★★★★★
Ashore Skipper only goes ashore — crew stays on board until clearance is completed ★★★★★
Documents to present Passports for all crew, cruising permit / Click2Clear Rotation Number, vessel registration/ownership document, insurance (if available), any weapons/pets permits, printed crew list ★★★★★
Departure (outbound clearance) Outbound clearance mandatory if required by the authorities of the next country (zarpe) — fee $75 ★★★★

Weapons on Board — Strict Rules

Item Rule Source
Declaration Mandatory on Click2Clear and to the officer — weapons kept locked on board, not to be taken ashore Bahamas Customs / Police ★★★★★
Quantity limits Max 3 firearms per vessel, calibre ≤ .308, max 250 rounds total Bahamas Police ★★★★★
Prohibitions Automatic weapons prohibited, assault weapons, open center console with weapons — possession forbidden in that case Bahamas Police ★★★★
Consequence of violation Seizure of weapon + vessel, arrest, fine Bahamas Police ★★★★★

Pets

Item Rule Source
BAHFSA import permit Pre-approved permit mandatory from the Bahamas Agriculture Health and Food Safety Authority (BAHFSA) — fee $11.20 per application BAHFSA ★★★★★
Requirements Microchip, valid rabies vaccination, veterinary certificate within 48h of departure, up-to-date vaccinations BAHFSA ★★★★★
Banned breeds Pit Bull, Presa Canario, Cane Corso, American Bully and crosses — entry banned BAHFSA ★★★★★
On board Pet declared, stays on board until authorised; inspection possible BAHFSA ★★★★

Designated Ports of Entry (Updated Selection)

Area Ports / Marinas of Entry
Abacos Green Turtle Cay, Marsh Harbour, Spanish Cay
Berry Islands Chub Cay
Bimini Alice Town (Bimini North), Cat Cay
Andros Congo Town / Fresh Creek (Andros Town)
New Providence (Nassau) All Nassau marinas — Harbour Control VHF 16, H24
Grand Bahama Freeport Harbour, Lucayan Harbour, Old Bahama Bay (West End)
Eleuthera Governor's Harbour, Harbour Island
Exumas George Town (Great Exuma), Staniel Cay, Highbourne Cay
Long Island Stella Maris

Typical Customs hours: 09:00–17:00 Mon–Fri, weekends overtime on call — confirm via VHF 16. ★★★★

Fees — Update 01/04/2026 (After Doubling on 01/07/2025) ★★★★★

Fees were doubled on 01/07/2025 and updated by circular 01/04/2026. Currency: BSD = USD 1:1.

Frequent Digital Cruising Card (FDCC) — 2 Years, Multiple Entries

LOA FDCC Cost 2 Years
≤50 ft $1,500
50–100 ft $2,500
>100 ft $8,000

Temporary Cruising Permit — 12 Months

LOA Cost 12 Months
≤50 ft $500
50–100 ft $1,000
>100 ft $3,000

Short Options (If You Don't Want 12 Months)

Duration ≤50 ft >50 ft / upper band
30 days $150 up to $600
6 months $300 up to $2,000

Other Mandatory Charges

Item Cost Notes
Anchorage fee (if not in marina, 12 months) $200 for ≤50 ft · $1,500 for >100 ft Collected with the permit ★★★★
Fishing permit 30 days $100 for ≤50 ft · $300 for >50 ft Mandatory if fishing
Passenger Tax $30 per passenger >3 pax Beyond the first 3 on board
Tender >25 ft $500 If tender exceeds 25 ft LOA
Outbound clearance / zarpe $75 Only if required
Charter fee 14% On commercial charters in the Bahamas

AIS & Penalties

  • AIS mandatory for vessels ≥50 ft (15.24 m) — must remain on in Bahamian waters. Fine $1,000 if non-compliant. ★★★★★
  • Penalties for failure to clear / non-payment / AIS off: fines, vessel seizure, possible arrest. ★★★★★

To Check Before Your Cruise

  • Click2Clear portal working and Visa card enabled for foreign payments.
  • Chosen port of entry on VHF 16 and Customs/Immigration hours — weekend = overtime.
  • Weapons/pets permits requested before departure.
  • Latest FDCC/Anchorage fee circular (frequent updates since 2025).

Cost of Living

Last updated: 24/08/2026

Currency: Bahamian dollar (BSD) — fixed parity 1:1 with USD; USD accepted everywhere (change often given in BSD). VAT 10% on almost everything, 12% on some higher-end services/restaurants. Price level: +20–80% vs the USA (everything imported, + VAT and island logistics). ★★★★

Services, Boatyards & Maintenance

Last checked: 24/08/2026

Main Hubs — Where the Yard Is

The Bahamas are not a cheap boatyard hub like Florida or Martinique: few travelifts, high prices, almost all spares imported from the USA. Useful hubs are Freeport (Grand Bahama), Nassau (New Providence) and Spanish Wells (Eleuthera) for haul-out; for complex work many owners return to Florida. ★★★★

Grand Bahama — Industrial Hub

Bradford Marine — Freeport ★★★★★

  • Dry dock 1,200 T, Travelift 150 T, full yard for superyacht and sailing refit, painting, mechanics, electrics. Contact via bradford-marine.com — quote mandatory. ★★★★★

Grand Bahama Shipyard — Freeport ★★★★★

  • Dock 27,600 T for ships and mega-yachts (3 floating docks), hull/steel work, propellers, engines — industrial scale, shipyard pricing. ★★★★★

Eleuthera — Traditional Storage

R&B Boatyard — Spanish Wells ★★★★

  • Railway / slip 90 ft (27 m), 120 T — historic yard for dry storage, bottom jobs, paint, small wood/fibreglass repairs. Family-run, more reasonable prices than Nassau. ★★★★

Nassau — Afloat Services & Light Bottom Work

Brown's Boat Basin — Nassau ★★★★

  • Travelift 40 T — haul-out, bottom, antifouling, basic mechanics. East Bay Street, Nassau. ★★★★

Brown's Boat Basin — Exuma (Satellite) ★★★

  • 10,000 lbs (4.5 T) — tenders / small boats only at George Town. ★★★

Compass Marine — Nassau ★★★★

  • 24/7 emergency, dealer MTU / Cummins / Volvo Penta / Yanmar — diagnostics, engine spares, electrics. Onboard interventions at marina or at anchor via workboat. ★★★★

Other scattered artisans: electricians, refrigeration technicians and riggers freelance between Nassau, Marsh Harbour and George Town — ask at the marina office; always get a written quote before work starts. ★★

Gas & Bottles

  • LPG/Gas: US standard bottles — refills possible at some points (DATA MISSING per individual cay), otherwise bottle swap like US Blue Rhino. US↔EU adapters needed for European boats. ★★
  • Check fitting compatibility before departure from Florida. ★★

Fresh Water

  • RO desalinated water everywhere: $0.10–0.25 / gal at Nassau/Georgetown, $0.40–0.50 / gal at Highbourne/Staniel (see zone details in 07 Provisioning). No structural rationing like in Martinique, but in remote cays (Exumas) availability depends on the marina watermaker — keep a reserve. Water marina tel: Hurricane Hole VHF 11, Highbourne 242-355-1009, Staniel 242-355-2024. ★★★★

Strategic Notes

  • Spares: order from USA (West Marine, Defender, Amazon US) shipped to Nassau (freight forwarder) or Florida — Bahamas customs + VAT 10% + duty 10–45% by category. Lead time 1–3 weeks. ★★★
  • Antifouling: available in Nassau/Freeport — US brands (Interlux, Pettit) — prices +30% vs USA. ★★
  • Sails / Standing Rigging: no major permanent loft — DATA MISSING for local sailmaker; rely on Florida for new sails. ★★
  • For work under 50 ft, R&B Spanish Wells is the best value for money in the central Bahamas. ★★★

Seasonality & Weather

Last checked: 24/08/2026

Climate

Subtropical archipelago — dry cool winter, hot humid summer. Sea temperature: 26–27 °C in winter, 28–30 °C in summer. ★★★★

Seasons

Period Characteristics Wind / Sea
Dry / Cool — Nov–Apr High sailing season: cool, dry, NE trades 10–20 kt steady. Best Dec–Apr for cruising. Air temp 21–26 °C, sea 26–27 °C NE trades, moderate swell, occasional cold fronts from NW (Dec–Feb) ★★★★★
Shoulder — May–Jun Warming, weaker trades, less crowded. Good window. Temp 27–29 °C SE–E 10–15 kt, calms possible ★★★★
Wet / Hot — 01/06–30/11 Hurricane season — hot humid, afternoon showers and thunderstorms. Peak Aug–Oct, annual rainfall ~44" (1,100 mm). Temp 28–32 °C, muggy Calms + storms, cyclone risk ★★★★★
Hurricane peak August–October — maximum cyclonic activity Requires hurricane plan (see below)

NOAA 2026 forecast: 8–14 named storms, 1–3 major hurricanes — average/above-average season. ★★★★

Best Window for Cruising

Late March – early June: trades still present but less strong, pleasant temperatures, hurricane risk still low, marina prices falling after high season. Also December–April excellent but windier and more crowded (US charter high season). ★★★★

Hurricanes — Mandatory Plan

Official season 01/06–30/11. The Bahamas are among the most hit areas in the Atlantic (Hurricane Dorian cat.5 on Abacos/Grand Bahama in 2019). No guaranteed hurricane hole like Le Marin — the only recognised shelter is Hurricane Hole, Nassau (14.5 ft MLW, hurricane moorings) but with limited spaces and early booking required.

Instructions: - Have a written hurricane plan with your insurer (navigation limits often imposed 01/06–30/11). - Monitor NHC Miami every 6h in season. - Plan to return to Florida or haul-out at Bradford Marine/Freeport if a warning is issued.

Local Winds & Currents

  • Gulf Stream along the western edge (Florida Strait / Bimini): north-setting current up to 5 kt — watch your Miami–Bimini course (east correction). ★★★★★
  • Tide: range 0.8–1.0 m — modest, but in the cuts between Exuma Banks and Exuma Sound it generates 2–4 kt current — transit only at slack water. ★★★★★
  • Banks: Exuma Banks and Grand Bahama Banks — extremely shallow (2–3 ft outside channels), navigate only by day with high sun and good charting (Explorer Chartbook). ★★★★★

Security

Last full check: 24/08/2026 · Next monthly check: 24/09/2026

Safety Rating: 3.5 / 5 — Weighted Average

Aspect Rating Reason
Exumas / Out Islands (remote cays) 4–4.5 / 5 Very low crime, tiny communities, calm anchorages
Nassau / New Providence 2.5–3 / 5 Petty crime and robberies, especially at night in run-down areas
Archipelago average for cruisers 3.5 / 5 Safe if normal precautions are applied, but Nassau requires caution

Scale: 0 = terrible → 5 = very safe. Our own assessment, synthesis of sources below; updated at each monthly check.

Why not 4.5: the national figure is weighted down by Nassau, where 80% of the population and crime is concentrated; the outer cays are much safer than the capital.

General Picture

  • US State Dept. Level 2 — Exercise Increased Caution (upd. 28/07/2026 ★★★★★): Bahamas at level 2 of 4 — "increased caution" for crime, especially in Nassau (New Providence) and Freeport (Grand Bahama).
  • CSSN (Caribbean Safety and Security Net) 2025: 124 violent incidents recorded in the Caribbean, few in the Bahamas — archipelago not among hotspots (2025 hotspots: St. Vincent, St. Lucia, Grenada). ★★★★
  • Nassau — Over the Hill: neighbourhoods south of Shirley Street concentrate gang-related shootings — victims almost always locals, but risk of robbery for tourists at night. ★★★★
  • Theft from cruisers: the main problem is tender/outboard theft — in the Caribbean region it accounts for 81.5% of thefts against yachtsmen (CSSN 2025) — Bahamas included, especially in Nassau and crowded marinas. ★★★★

Theft Against Cruisers

CSSN data upd. 2025: - Bahamas hotspots: Nassau Harbour / Paradise Island dinghy dock, Marsh Harbour (Abacos) — sporadic episodes, not systematic as in Martinique/Antilles. - Modus: tender left unattended at dinghy dock, night theft of outboard, rare burglaries at anchor in Nassau. - Countermeasures: short chain + stainless padlock through the transom, engine locked with dedicated lock, tender hoisted aboard at night, nothing visible, outboard alarm; in Nassau prefer a guarded marina. ★★★★

Exuma Cuts Current 2–4 kt at tide change — transit only at slack Explorer ★★★★★

Local Markets

  • Potter's Cay (Nassau): daily fresh fish — best for conch/grouper. Recommended arrival 7–9 am. ★★★★★
  • Fruit/veg markets: small stalls at Nassau (Fox Hill, Arawak Cay), Marsh Harbour, George Town — local seasonal produce (mango, papaya, banana, lime). ★★
  • Direct fishing: ask fishermen at Georgetown Fish Dock or Staniel — conch cleaned on the spot, lobster (in season).

Practical Tips (Martinique Standard)

  • Strategic provisioning: bulk in Florida or Nassau (Solomon's/Super Value/Cost Right Harbour Bay), fresh at Potter's Cay and cays (Pinder's, Maxwell's, Exuma Markets). Don't leave under-provisioned for central Exumas. ★★★★
  • Taxi vs Jitney: with heavy loads always agreed taxi; jitney only for light reconnaissance in Nassau. Keep small USD notes ($1, $5) for jitney and markets.
  • Water: carry extra jerry cans 20–40 L for central Exumas — between Highbourne and George Town water points are sparse and expensive.
  • Delivery aboard: Solomon's Harbour Bay/Old Fort and Exuma Markets offer delivery — order 24h ahead by phone/online shop and have delivered to marina (check time and minimum). Sawyer's inside Hurricane Hole is already aboard — no delivery needed.
  • Cash: in remote cays many shops take only cash USD/BSD — keep small notes; Visa/Mastercard ok at Nassau/Atlantis/Marsh Harbour/Georgetown ★★★.
  • Hours: Sunday many shops closed or half-day outside Nassau — plan; Solomon's Harbour Bay Sunday 7–18, Old Fort 7–20.
  • Trolley: folding trolley essential from Bay Street Marina to Potter's Cay and from Boat Harbour to Maxwell's.

Pilot of Anchorages

Last checked: 24/08/2026

General Anchoring Rules (First of All)

  • Anchorage fee mandatory if anchoring outside a marina: $200 / 12 months for ≤50 ft, $1,500 / 12 months for >100 ft (intermediate DATA MISSING) — collected with the cruising permit (see 01 Clearance). Those staying in a marina do not pay the anchorage fee for the days at the dock. ★★★★★
  • Absolute prohibition on anchoring on coral and seagrass beds — damage punishable by fine. Always use visible light sand. ★★★★★
  • Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park (Warderick Wells): mooring only — anchoring forbidden throughout the park. Book via Bahamas National Trust. ★★★★★
  • Tide 0.8–1.0 m but current in cuts 2–4 kt — anchor away from tidal channels. ★★★★

⛔ Absolute Prohibition / Restriction Zones

Area Prohibition Source
Exuma Cays Land and Sea Park — Warderick Wells and park cays Anchoring forbidden — mooring only $35–40 / night Bahamas National Trust ★★★★★
Reef and seagrass everywhere Anchor and chain must not touch coral/seagrass Bahamas Environment ★★★★★
Nassau Harbour / Freeport Harbour port areas Anchoring forbidden in channels and ship manoeuvring areas Harbour Control ★★★★
Private areas (e.g. Baker's Bay) Access/anchoring reserved to members — forbidden for passing yachts Resort ★★

Full texts: Bahamas National Trust (bnt.bs) for the Exuma park; Harbour Control VHF 16 for Nassau.

  • IALA-B reversed vs Europe — watch buoys. ★★★★★
  • Reference charting: Explorer Chartbook — Bahamas (de facto standard for the Banks) + electronic charts Navionics/Garmin. ★★★★★

Anchoring Notes

  • Clear water: always anchor on white sand clearly visible — if you see dark (coral/weed) move. ★★★★★
  • Trade shelter: the Exumas offer excellent shelter from E/NE behind cays — but exposed to W/NW with winter cold fronts (Dec–Feb) — check forecast. ★★★★
  • Crowding: Dec–Apr very high in central Exumas (Warderick, Staniel) — arrive early to secure mooring/anchorage. ★★★
  • Useful app: Bahamas Marinas + Explorer Charts + Navionics for the Banks — essential. ★★★★

Official Charting

Chart Coverage Notes
Explorer Chartbook — Near Bahamas Bimini / Berry / Nassau / Northern Exumas ~$40–50 — the Banks bible ★★★★★
Explorer Chartbook — Exumas Highbourne → Great Exuma / Long Island ~$40–50 ★★★★★
Explorer Chartbook — Far Bahamas Abacos / Eleuthera / Long Island / Ragged ~$40–50 ★★★★★
BA Charts (UKHO) Bahamas — British Admiralty charts Official but less detailed on Banks ★★★
Navionics / Garmin / C-MAP All Bahamas Electronic, verify with Explorer ★★★★
  • Explorer charts show routes, waypoints and actual surveyed depths — more reliable than official on the Banks. Buyable in Nassau (Harbour Chandler), Florida or online. ★★★★★
  • For daily navigation: plotter + paper Explorer as backup — never trust only electronics on the Banks. ★★★★★

  • Ragged Islands / Jumentos: remote, beautiful but zero services → to be verified

Bahamas Anchor Checklist

  1. Anchorage fee paid with Click2Clear (if anchoring outside marina) ✓
  2. Explorer charting aboard + updated electronics ✓
  3. Light anchor but lots of chain — excellent holding on sand, terrible on coral
  4. Watch water colour: white = sand ok, dark = coral no
  5. Slack water for cuts between Banks and Sound ✓
  6. Booking for Warderick Wells mooring if heading to the park ✓

Marine Artisans & Chandlers

The main hub is Nassau (New Providence): the few serious marine dealers are concentrated between East Bay Street and the harbour. For the rest you need Freeport or Florida (48 NM from Bimini). Typical contact via phone/WhatsApp; English spoken. For major work always ask for a written quote and confirm timing in high season (Dec–Apr), when workshops are saturated.

Nassau — Arawak Cay (Fish Fry) — The Bahamian Classic

  • Drifters, Oh Andros, Goldie's, Twin Brothers: row of colourful shacks on the waterfront 5 min taxi from Bay Street Marina. Potter's Cay — Under Paradise Island Bridge

  • Fishermen stalls: conch salad prepared knife-fresh in front of you ($10–15), fritters, take-away. Perfect for quick lunch returning from provisioning. ★★★★

  • Chat 'N' Chill — Stocking Island: sailors' institution opposite George Town — dinghy beach, conch burger $15, Sunday pig roast, Kalik/sky juice bar, volleyball. $15–30. ★★★★½

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 28/08/2026

Status

Barbados is an independent parliamentary republic since 30 November 2021 (former Commonwealth realm), a member of the Commonwealth, outside the EU and outside the Schengen Area: it has its own customs and immigration and is not part of the OECS. EU/Schengen rules do not apply. immigration.gov.bb ★★★★★ · gov.bb — Immigration Department ★★★★★

EU Citizens — No Visa for Short Stays

Item Rule Source
Visa Not required for Italian/EU citizens and many other nationalities for tourism/visit; the visa-required list only includes certain countries (e.g. Dominican Republic, Haiti, Cuba, China etc. — not the EU) barbados.org — Documents Required ★★★ · immigration.gov.bb — Requirements ★★★★★
Required documents Passport valid for the entire stay (must still be valid on departure); return or onward ticket; accommodation address (hotel/apartment or yacht with anchorage/marina); proof of sufficient funds; completed online Immigration & Customs Form with receipts saved/printed immigration.gov.bb — Visitor Information ★★★★★ · travelform.gov.bb ★★★★★
Mandatory online form Immigration and Customs Form at travelform.gov.bb available within 72 hours before arrival; must be completed online (including pre-registration of vessels) and the Immigration + Customs receipts must be saved to your phone or printed for inspection on arrival immigration.gov.bb ★★★★★ · travelform.gov.bb ★★★★★ · barbados.org ★★★
Tourist stay Typically up to 3 months on entry for EU/visa-exempt nationals, at the discretion of the border officer; the stamp in your passport is decisive [Cruising sources aggregate ★★★ · barbados.org — Duration ★★★
Minors <18 If not accompanied by a parent/legal guardian: notarised letter of consent stating the period, the adult authorised to receive the minor and contact details; original + copy. If with an adult other than the parent/guardian: same notarised letter identifying the accompanying adult immigration.gov.bb ★★★★★

⚠️ Caution: final admission is always at the discretion of the border officer at the port of entry; even when no visa is required, entry may be refused or curtailed if requirements are not met.

Important Note for Arrival by Sea

  • People (Immigration) and yacht (Customs + Port Health + Port Authority) controls are separate but linked: the yacht must be presented at an official Port of Entry and the crew must have completed the online Immigration & Customs Form. Yacht clearance is mandatory on entry and on exit → see 01 — Clearance.
  • Ports of Entry (POE) for yachts: Bridgetown (Shallow Draught dedicated to yachts + Deep Water Harbour on instruction) and Port St. Charles Marina (NW, clearance directly in the marina at the end of the breakwater). Do not approach the cruise/commercial wharf with a vessel <20 m: dangerous, no dinghy dock — better to stand off and proceed by dinghy to the Passenger Terminal on the instructions of the Signal Station. Barbados Port Inc. — Vessel Documentation ★★★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  • Approaching Bridgetown: call Bridgetown Signal Station on VHF 12 (callsign "8P") before entering; a berth will be assigned; fly a clearly visible yellow Q flag on entry. Usual anchorage after clearance is Carlisle Bay (5–10 m over sand), then dinghy/taxi to the offices. The vessel is normally boarded by Port Health + Customs + Immigration (~10 min for Free Pratique); the vessel's own forms are accepted. Required: ship's particulars, list of the last 10 ports visited, crew and passenger lists, zarpe from the previous port.
  • Approaching Port St. Charles: anchor outside over sand off the marina, then dinghy to the inner pontoon; officers are in the same building at the end of the breakwater (customs/immigration/coast guard/police) — procedure described as quick and friendly (Cruising sources aggregate report 30/11/2025). Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  • Digital pre-arrival: SailClear (sailclear.com) is recommended as a customs pre-notification (Barbados has been a SailClear CCLEC country since 2013); it does not replace presenting in person at the dock but speeds up the paperwork; SailClear has charged an annual fee of US$25 since 01/05/2024. SailClear ★★★ · CCLEC — SailClear ★★★

Yellow fever requirement Not required for direct arrivals from the EU/Italy/USA. Required only if you have come from or transited >12 h in a country at risk of transmission (Amazon basin, sub-Saharan Africa — WHO list). Exemption for Guyana and Trinidad unless there is an urban outbreak according to a secondary source (relevant for routes from South America) CDC — Barbados Traveler View ★★★★★ · NaTHNaC — Barbados ★★★★★ · IAMAT / traveldoctor.network ★★★
YF certificate validity Lifetime from 11/07/2016 (WHO): it cannot be refused for being >10 years old NaTHNaC / WHO ★★★★★
Age Required from 12 months of age where applicable traveldoctor.network ★★★
Other vaccines No others mandatory for arrivals from the EU; mosquito protection recommended (dengue present) CDC ★★★★★
