Yacht Customs Clearance

Last checked: 28/08/2026 · Main source: Barbados Port Inc. (BPI) – Vessel Documentation ★★★★★ + Barbados Immigration / travelform.gov.bb ★★★★★ + Cruising sources aggregate / Barbados (upd. 05/12/2025) ★★★

Who Must Clear

All pleasure craft, regardless of flag and nationality, that: - enter Barbadian waters from a foreign port/territorial sea or the high seas; - exit to a foreign port/sea or the high seas. Residents returning from foreign passages must also report. It is forbidden to anchor or head for a marina/anchorage before completing Customs/Immigration/Port Health at the port of entry. Barbados Port Inc. ★★★★★

The crew must remain on board until clearance is completed; fly the yellow Q flag. Cruising sources aggregate ★★★

Online Procedure

Barbados has no single portal like Aruba or the French Antilles: the digital part is yacht pre-notice (SailClear) + people's Immigration & Customs Form (travelform.gov.bb); the rest is done dockside with an on-board inspection.

  1. Yacht pre-notice — SailClear: Customs is a SailClear CCLEC country (sailclear.com) — complete it online before arrival (yacht details, owner, crew, last/next port, ETA, flag, MMSI, dimensions, engines, stores). It does not replace presenting in person but shortens the paperwork. SailClear fee US$25/year since 01/05/2024. CCLEC — SailClear ★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  2. People pre-notice — Immigration & Customs Form: every person on board completes the Immigration and Customs Form at travelform.gov.bb within 72 hours before arrival (for yachts you can also pre-register the vessel); Immigration + Customs receipts must be saved/printed on your phone for arrival. immigration.gov.bb ★★★★★ · travelform.gov.bb ★★★★★
  3. Paper forms (optional): Barbados Port Inc. provides Vessel Documentation with forms and a checklist; if not printed, they are available in the offices on the wharf. Have ready: passports, crew/passenger list, ship's particulars, list of last 10 ports visited, zarpe from the previous port, registration/nationality, proof of ownership/insurance. Barbados Port Inc. ★★★★★
  4. Approach: call Bridgetown Signal Station on VHF 12 ("8P") (Bridgetown) before entering and request a berth/instructions; at Port St. Charles report directly to the inner pontoon. Follow instructions to the berth / outer anchorage and hoist Q. BPI ★★★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  5. Berthing/anchoring: at Bridgetown do NOT go to the customs wharf with boats <20 m (dangerous, no pontoon — Cruising sources aggregate report Dec 2022): better to anchor outside in Carlisle Bay and proceed by dinghy to the Passenger Terminal, or berth at the Shallow Draught as assigned by the Signal Station. At Port St. Charles anchor outside over sand off the marina, then dinghy to the inner pontoon (officers in the same building at the end of the breakwater). Cruising sources aggregate ★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  6. Dockside / on board: presentation of the whole crew (Immigration headcount) + Port Health + Customs; the vessel is boarded (Free Pratique ~10 min). Declare stores and weapons. After signing, permits are issued and the yacht may move to Carlisle Bay or the marina.
  7. Outbound clearance: return to the same Customs/Immigration office before casting off, with passports and yacht papers; request a zarpe/outward declaration for the next port; then depart promptly.

Handy Tip (★★★)

Complete SailClear + travelform 24–48 hours in advance and take aboard printouts/receipts + separate crew list + list of 10 ports + previous zarpe in a folder: the Bridgetown offices are small and the queue moves faster with forms ready. Keep Q flying until you are stamped.

Stamped Paper Copy

  • Barbados has no electronic "attestation" printable from a portal: the stamped paper receipts issued dockside by Immigration, Customs and Port Health after the skipper signs are the legal proof. Keep them on board: they serve as the zarpe for the next port and as proof of regular entry. Barbados Port Inc. ★★★★★
  • Until you are stamped you have not legally entered: remain at the assigned berth/anchorage; for night arrivals follow the instructions of the Signal Station / Coast Guard.

Cruisers' Experiences

  • Port St. Charles described as quick and friendly: anchor outside and dinghy to the "superyacht marina" — officers all in the same room at the end of the breakwater, 6 berths for mega-yachts (water/power) but no toilets/showers/laundry, high-end restaurant on site. ★★★ (Cruising sources aggregate 30/11/2025 Lionheart)
  • Bridgetown Customs Wharf criticised as dangerous for boats <20 m, no pontoon for landing — do not present at the cargo wharf: better to dinghy to the passenger port on VHF. ★★ (Cruising sources aggregate 31/12/2022 olcdlm)
  • Calling 30 minutes ahead speeds up the officer coming out and the berth assignment. ★★★

Penalties

  • Remaining in Barbadian waters without immigration consent is an offence (general Caribbean practice — as in Aruba/ABC: remaining without clearance is treated as an offence). BPI — Vessel Documentation § Customs ★★★★★
  • Staying beyond the days granted without an extension may lead to refusal of future entry / adverse notation. immigration.gov.bb ★★★★★
  • Undeclared weapons/spearguns: immediate seizure on inspection and possible customs penalties — DATA MISSING on amount: no table of fines published on gov.bb/BPI as of 28/08/2026; to be verified dockside with Customs.
  • Detail of customs/immigration fine amounts: DATA MISSING — no government source with a tariff of penalties for failure to clear a yacht found on gov.bb as of 28/08/2026; check with BPI/Customs before your cruise.

To Verify Before Your Cruise

  • Immigration/Customs counter hours at Bridgetown Shallow Draught and Port St. Charles (not published in detail on gov.bb/BPI as of 28/08/2026) — ask BPI/Signal Station on VHF 12.
  • Whether pre-notification via the marina is required and berth availability at Shallow Draught in high season (Dec–Apr).
  • Updated penalty tariff and list of customs brokers if needed (not documented for short leisure stays).
  • Current BBD 100 exit fee — confirm with Customs (Cruising sources aggregate 2025 data).

Cost of Living

Last updated: 28/08/2026

Currency: Barbados dollar (BBD, Bds$) — pegged at 2 BBD = 1 USD; prices are shown in BBD everywhere, US dollars are accepted almost everywhere at the fixed rate; the island is heavily import-dependent, groceries are 30–50% more expensive than in mainland Europe/continental USA, tourist restaurants are pricey in marina areas (as local guides put it: "comparable to New York/London"). skiptomalouuu.com — Barbados Food Guide 2025 ★★★ · barbados.org ★★★

Cash & Payments

BBD pegged 2:1 to USD: prices are shown in BBD; almost everyone accepts US cash at the fixed rate (change in BBD). Cards (Visa/Mastercard) are accepted in marinas, supermarkets and tourist restaurants; cash is essential for buses/markets/fish fries/Oistins. ATMs in Bridgetown (Broad Street, Harbour Road), Holetown (Limegrove), Oistins and the airport. High fees for withdrawals with foreign cards.

At the Oistins fish fries and beach stalls many vendors prefer cash in BBD/USD — keep small notes.

Ports & Marinas

Last checked: 28/08/2026 · Coordinates in decimal degrees / N-W as per source · datum WGS84 · VHF 12 Bridgetown Signal, VHF 16 Port Control

Barbados has very little yachting infrastructure compared with the French Windwards: the only sheltered area is the leeward west coast (Carlisle Bay → Six Men's Bay). The Atlantic east coast is not tenable at anchor in normal conditions (surf, continuous swell). The cruisers' preferred anchorage is Carlisle Bay off Bridgetown; the marinas are Bridgetown Shallow Draught / Careenage (town centre) and the two resort marinas of the north-west (Port St. Charles — POE + Port Ferdinand — non-POE). Cruising sources aggregate ★★★ · Barbados Port Inc. ★★★★★

Leeward West Coast — Bridgetown and Carlisle Bay ⚓ main area

Bridgetown — Shallow Draught & Careenage (main harbour) ⚓

  • 13°06.07' N 59°37.62' W (Shallow Draught, yacht basin) · 13°06.00' N 59°37.18' W (inner Careenage) · VHF 12 Signal Station ("8P") + VHF 16 · Barbados Port Inc. — Vessel Documentation ★★★★★ · Marinas.com — Careenage ★★
  • Shallow Draught: sheltered basin inside the commercial harbour but separate, dedicated to yachts (~40 fully serviced berths, water/power, security). The only basin with yacht-dedicated Customs/Immigration and the recommended POE at Bridgetown. Depth adequate for yachts ("shallow" only for ships). Book via Harbour Master tel +1 246 434-6100. BPI news 2024-12 ★★★★ · BPI Yacht Masters Guide ★★★★
  • Careenage (inner UNESCO channel): historic channel in the heart of Bridgetown with ~50 stern-to berths on alongside quays, limited depth (shallow draught), inner lifting bridge (opening on request), Molehead light Fl R 10s 2M. Town atmosphere, walkable to the centre/markets. Book via Marine Services/Harbour Master +1 246 434-6100. BPI Yacht Masters Guide ★★★★ · Yachting World 2017 ★★★
  • Carlisle Bay (open roadstead off Bridgetown): not a marina but the official post-clearance anchorage over sand (4–14 m). Exposed to westerly swell during frontal passages, but sheltered from the ENE trades. Watch for jet skis by day and the marine park wrecks (6 snorkelling wrecks 12–55 m immediately to the south). Tariff for yachts <50 m BBD 110 flat at Carlisle Bay per 2026 guides (to be confirmed). BPI Yacht Masters Guide ★★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  • Clearance on site (Shallow Draught or Passenger Terminal — see 01). Call Signal Station VHF 12 before entering, berth will be assigned; Q flag. Hours 06:00–22:00 daily at the Passenger Terminal according to reports — verify on VHF.
  • Shelter: good lee from the trades; ground swell with N/NW swell during winter swells or a passing hurricane — check the local forecast before entering. Dinghy landing on sand: beach the tender, padlock it. ★★

Carlisle Bay — Public Anchorage

  • 13°04.69' N 59°37.66' W (centre of the bay, ~13.078 -59.627) · sand, 5–14 m, good holding. See card anc-carlisle-main. This is where almost all cruisers stay after clearance, a few minutes by dinghy from the boatyard and town centre.

North-West Coast — Port St. Charles & Port Ferdinand (resort, sheltered)

Port St. Charles Marina — Northern POE ⚓

  • 13°15.83' N 59°38.79' W (lagoon entrance, outer anchorage 13°15.50' N 59°38.47' W) · VHF 16 (calling) · Port St. Charles · Marinas.com — Port St. Charles ★★ · Navily — Port St. Charles ★★★
  • Official northern POE (second POE of the island): customs/immigration/coast guard/police in the same building at the end of the breakwater; procedure quick and friendly per report 30/11/2025 (anchor outside, dinghy to the inner pontoon). 6 mega-yacht berths up to 250 ft / 76 m, max draught ~4.1 m (13.5 ft) on the outer breakwater; duty-free fuel on clearance (cash); no toilets/showers/laundry on the mega-yacht quays, but resort pool/restaurant at the end of the breakwater. Cruising sources aggregate ★★★ · Minty Yachts — Barbados ★★
  • Outer anchorage over 3–4 m sand, good holding, calm except for occasional swell; watch for turtles in the area. See card anc-psc-anch. Practical: enter the marina only on berth assignment; for clearance just tie up at the customs pontoon.

Port Ferdinand Marina (St. Peter) — Luxury Resort, NOT a POE

  • 13°15.51' N 59°38.70' W (inner basin, outer anchorage Six Men's Bay) · Port Ferdinand ★★ · Yachting World 2017 ★★★ · Marinas.com — Port Ferdinand ★★
  • NOT a POE: formalities at Bridgetown or Port St. Charles; a coastal permit from the Customs Boarding Officer (tel +1 246 430-2355, VHF 16) is needed to move along the coast without fresh clearance if already cleared in. BPI Yacht Masters Guide §8 ★★★★
  • Basin cut into the rock, 120–126 berths, suitable for superyachts, entrance via Six Men's Bay under a lifting bridge (watch your air draught). Large yachts often anchor outside in the roadstead. Full resort facilities (13°/59° restaurant, beach club, spa). See card anc-port-ferdinand.

Central West Coast — Speightstown, Holetown, Paynes Bay (open roadsteads)

  • Speightstown (13°15.18' N 59°38.70' W) — roadstead over sand off the town, roll present, dinghy landing limited; no customs; coastal permit as above. Shops/supermarket walkable. See anc-speightstown. noforeignland ★★
  • Holetown / Paynes Bay / Sandy Lane — long leeward bays, anchoring over sand 3–8 m, good holding but open to westerly swell. Busy with day charters, possible private hotel buoys — do not use without permission. Dinghy landing on the beach, watch the surf when a swell is running. ★★

South Coast — Oistins, Silver Sands (exposed, conditional)

  • Oistins Bay (13°03.93' N 59°32.47' W) — bay open to the south with a roadstead over 3–8 m sand, exposed to south Atlantic swell; tenable only in calm conditions (Dec–Apr best). Famous for the Friday Fish Fry and fish market, but not a reliable refuge in fresh trades. Many local fishing boats. See anc-oistins. Navily — Oistins ★★
  • St. Lawrence Gap / Worthing / Hastings — tourist shoreline with fringing reef, sand/coral bottom, anchoring only in settled weather and never overnight without a watch; respect swimming corridors. ★★

Atlantic East Coast — NOT Tenable (Bathsheba, Tent Bay, Consett Bay)

  • Bathsheba / Tent Bay (13°14.82' N 59°32.17' W) and Consett Bay — to be excluded as anchorages in normal conditions: windward coast with continuous Atlantic swell, depths 4–10 m but no shelter. Only local fishing boats; marked only as to be AVOIDED. See anc-bathsheba. safetyanchoralarm.com — South & East Coast ★★

Services, Boatyards & Maintenance

Last checked: 28/08/2026

Main Hub — Bridgetown / Shallow Draught

  • Services are concentrated in the Bridgetown harbour/marina (Shallow Draught + Careenage); for major work the marina/Bay Street area is the reference. Barbados is not a Caribbean technical hub: infrastructure is limited compared with Antigua, St. Martin or Trinidad. ★★
  • Travelift / crane / haul-out: DATA MISSING for verified capacity in Barbados — ask the Harbour Master +1 246 434-6100 or Port St. Charles +1 246 419-1000. For structural refits many owners rely on Antigua (English Harbour/Jolly Harbour), Sint Maarten (Simpson Bay) or Trinidad (Chaguaramas) with 70–300 t travelifts and dozens of trades. Yachting World 2017 — Barbados ★★★
  • Chandlery: basic range locally (hardware, anchors, rope, paint); for specific spares (Volvo Penta, Yanmar, NKE/Raymarine electronics) allow 1–3 weeks lead time via Miami/St. Martin/UK. Shipping: DHL/Colissimo; duty payable on arrival. ★★
  • Hull care: scrubbing and painting is possible in the Bridgetown basins according to local reports, but DATA MISSING for a certified travelift/crane in Barbados — check with the harbour offices before planning. ★★

Other Useful Operators (regional hubs recommended for a serious refit)

  • Antigua — English Harbour / Jolly Harbour: 70 t travelift, dozens of trades (mechanics, composites, North/Sanders sails), the nearest hub east of Barbados for major work. ★★★
  • Sint Maarten — Simpson Bay Lagoon: Budget Marine, FKG, multiple yards, 100 t+ travelifts, duty-free. ★★★★
  • Trinidad — Chaguaramas (Peakes, Power Boats, Coral Cove): travelifts up to 300 t, the best-equipped hurricane hub in the southern Caribbean. ★★★★
  • Locally in Bridgetown: basic chandlery + town hardware stores; for composite/fibreglass work ask in the harbour — limited availability.

Gas & Bottles

  • Gas/LPG: often bottle exchange only for local/US standards (e.g. Campingaz 904/907 or US 20 lb). Cylinders are not refilled, they are exchanged at LPG points or hardware stores; check US vs EU regulator compatibility (adapter required). Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  • Supermarkets/chandlery in Bridgetown stock adapters and Campingaz cylinders; for a true refill you need to move to a larger hub. ★★

Fresh Water

  • Dock water: potable according to the BWA (Barbados Water Authority), desalinated in the Bridgetown area; however DATA MISSING on certified potability at the Shallow Draught pontoon — ask in the marina and consider carbon filtering or a watermaker. Mains pressurised but pressure drops possible in high season — keep reserves. ★★
  • Water cost: DATA MISSING rate/m³ in Barbados as of 28/08/2026 — ask in the harbour offices → 03 Ports.

Strategic Notes

  • Barbados is not a refit island: if the job can be planned (standing rigging, sails, engine, osmosis), schedule it in Antigua/St. Martin/Trinidad before or after the Barbados stop; keep the Barbados call for stores/clearance/light technical stops. This is confirmed by all guides 2017–2025 describing it as "basic yachting facilities, good repair facilities but improving" — not a hub. Cruising sources aggregate ★★★ · Yachting World ★★★
  • Spares: have them shipped to the marina stating yacht name, berth and phone; confirm arrival via email/phone with reception; duty payable online or dockside. Lead time EU/USA → Barbados 7–14 days by courier; allow for customs. ★★

Climate

  • Average temperature 26–28 °C year-round, moderate tropical maritime climate with ENE trades 12–20 kn; small diurnal range. ★★★ Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  • Sea temperature 26–29 °C year-round (peak 28–29 °C August–October); humidity 75–85%, brief showers even in the dry season. ★★
  • Barbados lies 100 km east of the Windward chain, directly exposed to the Atlantic: it catches more ocean swell than the leeward islands (Saint Lucia, the Grenadines) — windward seas build more often. Cruising sources aggregate ★★★

Seasons

Period Characteristics
December – April/May Dry and cooler, steady trades: best period for cruising; regular trades 15–20 kn, brief showers, flat water on the west side
June – mid-November Wet + hurricane season: lighter trades, tropical waves, afternoon thunderstorms; many insurers impose hurricane limits/shelter requirements; check the marina's hurricane plan

★★★

Official Hurricane Instructions

Barbados has no guaranteed "hurricane hole" like Le Marin (Martinique): Bridgetown harbour and the northern resort marinas have securing and evacuation procedures on alert, but no shelter is 100% guaranteed. Document: National Hurricane Preparedness Plan (Barbados DEM — Department of Emergency Management) and BPI/Harbour Master instructions on VHF/tel. The port cannot be held liable for damage from parted moorings/anchors caused by a cyclone.

Hurricanes

Season June–November, peak August–October. Barbados is exposed to the trades and Atlantic waves and, although south of the most-hit belt, has been hit directly in its history: historic hurricanes 1780 (Great Hurricane), 1898, 1955 (Janet, Cat.3 on the island), 2024 (Beryl, Cat.1 passing 40 M south with significant damage in Bridgetown/Oistins). Hurricane plan: instructions from the Barbados DEM and harbour offices publish securing procedures; many insurers require you to leave the area or haul out by 1 June. [NOAA NHC ★★★★★; Barbados DEM ★★★★; NHC — Beryl 2024 ★★★★★]

  • Yacht shelters: the lagoon at Port St. Charles/Port Ferdinand is more sheltered than Carlisle Bay but is not classed as a certified hurricane hole; for real protection consider Trinidad (Chaguaramas, outside the belt) or southern Grenada per your policy. Check with your insurer.

Local Winds

  • Trades ENE 12–20 kn typical of the Windwards; acceleration in the lee of high ground (e.g. St. John escarpment) and between the bays of the west coast with local gusts. At night the trades ease, light land breeze. ★★
  • Atlantic swell: even with moderate trades, the east and south coasts take a long E/SE swell (period 8–12 s) — which is why Oistins/south is often choppy while Carlisle/west stays flat. Care with the dinghy on exposed beaches. ★★
  • Inter-island channels (Barbados ↔ Saint Lucia ~95 M, Barbados ↔ Grenada ~135 M, Barbados ↔ Tobago ~160 M): confused seas and currents (Equatorial Current west-setting, 0.5–1.5 kn to the NW). Best window early morning with trades <18–20 kn and swell <1.5 m; avoid departures with a tropical wave passing. ★★

Typical Weather Windows

  • Short inter-island passages (Barbados ↔ Saint Lucia/Grenada, 90–140 M): feasible with trades ≤18–20 kn, best departure 04:00–06:00 for a daylight arrival; course 20–40° off the trades — allow for a tack. ★★
  • Long passages (to Antigua ~240 M, to Trinidad 210 M): wait for a post-tropical-wave window with stable pressure and no Invest 90L; check NHC Tropical Weather Outlook 2/7 days. Barbados → Trinidad is slightly against the current but with the trades on the beam — best window December–April. ★★★
  • Day vs night: the ARC and cruisers arriving on the transatlantic from Cape Verde often make landfall in Barbados in December–January with fresh trades — arrive in daylight to identify Carlisle Bay and Bridgetown commercial traffic. ★★

  • Barbados DEM — Department of Emergency Management ★★★★★ — hurricane instructions and shelter list.
  • NOAA National Hurricane Center ★★★★★ — hurricane bulletins and tracks for the Atlantic (June–November) + Tropical Weather Outlook.

Safety & Security

Last full check: 28/08/2026 · Next monthly check: 28/09/2026

Safety Rating: 3 / 5

Aspect Rating Reason
Personal safety (tourists/cruisers) 3/5 US/UK/Canada advisories Level 1 "exercise normal precautions" — petty crime is common, targeted violence against tourists is rare but opportunistic theft is frequent in tourist areas
Theft from yacht 2/5 Dinghy/outboard and cockpit items are a recurring problem in the roadstead and at dinghy docks (CSSN: 37 incidents in 5 years within 10 km of Le Marin, Martinique as benchmark; similar pattern at Carlisle/Bridgetown in Barbados)
Overall island context 3/5 50 homicides in 2024 (17.7/100k), overall crime slightly down (-4% 2024→2025) but firearms offences +60%; gang-related violence, concentrated among locals and in certain parishes — tourists are not the primary target

Scale: 0 = terrible → 5 = very safe. Our rating, synthesising the sources below; updated at each monthly check.

Why not 4/5: besides opportunistic theft (pickpocketing, bag-snatching, car break-ins, dinghy theft) documented by the advisories, Barbados has homicide rates among the highest in the eastern Caribbean proportionally (~17.7/100k in 2024, 50 cases) with a recent surge in firearms and robberies; resorts/marinas remain guarded, however, and physical attacks on cruisers have been rare in sources over the last 5 years.

General Overview

  • US Advisory — Travel.State.gov (upd. 10/04/2026 ★★★★): Level 1 — "Exercise normal precautions" — the lowest of four levels. Crimes most likely against tourists: purse snatching, pickpocketing, burglary, vehicle break-ins in tourist areas; occasionally armed robbery, sexual assault, shootings, drug-related crime. Advice: do not leave valuables unattended on the beach/in the car/hotel, do not walk alone at night on beaches/poorly lit areas, extra vigilance downtown and on evening party cruises, do not leave drinks unattended, watch out at isolated ATMs. travel.state.gov — Barbados ★★★★
  • OSAC — Barbados Country Security Report (01/05/2025 ★★★★): Bridgetown rated HIGH threat for crime vs US interests (overall), LOW for terrorism. Crime emergency 211 or (246) 430-7100. 50 homicides in 2024 (17.7/100k) up on 2023; Barbados still below the regional average but violence is concentrated between rival gangs and rarely spills over to tourists; greatest risk to travellers = petty theft; robberies and car theft possible; avoid non-tourist areas at night, unlit roads, isolated beaches. osac.gov — Barbados CSR 2025 ★★★★
  • UK FCDO advisory (07/07/2026 ★★★★) + Canadian (29/07/2026 ★★★★): petty crime and occasional street crime; do not walk in remote areas at night, do not leave valuables in the car/on the beach, keep bags out of grab-reach; Barbados is a South America → Europe/North America drug-trafficking corridor (UK) with possible associated crime; no recent history of terrorism but cannot be ruled out.
  • Local press 2025–2026 ★★★: Q1 2025 crime near record levels with spikes in homicides and vehicle theft (Barbados Today 23/05/2025); overall crime -4% 6,301→6,063 (2024→2025) but major crimes +41% and firearms +60% per Criminal Justice Research Unit (03/2026); InSight Crime 2025 homicide round-up: 50 homicides in 2024, steady at 50 in 2025, rate 17.7/100k — among the highest in the ARC.
  • Government of Barbados ★★★★★: emergency number 211 police · 511 ambulance — see Numbers below; U.S. Embassy (Wildey Business Park) +1 246 227-4000 for assistance.
  • Operational context: compact island (34 km) with a strong tourist presence on the west/south coasts (Holetown, St. Lawrence Gap, Hastings, Carlisle) and fast response times in hotel areas; private security widespread in resorts/marinas. Outside tourist areas and at night coverage drops. ★★

Theft Against Cruisers

Data from Caribbean Safety and Security Net (CSSN — thecssn.org ★★★) + cross-checked advisories, checked 28/08/2026:

  • Barbados trend: no wave of violent armed attacks on yachtsmen reported in sources over the last 5 years; cases concern almost exclusively opportunistic night theft of dinghies/outboards and items left in the cockpit or on the beach. Endemic across the eastern Caribbean (Martinique benchmark: 37 incidents in 5 years within 10 km of Le Marin). In Barbados hotspots are the Bridgetown/Careenage dinghy docks and the Carlisle Bay roadstead (dinghies hauled up on the beach), and to a lesser extent the northern bays (Speightstown/Port St. Charles) where large yachts lie at anchor.
  • Modus operandi: tenders not locked or with thin cable cut; outboards taken even when chained with a short chain if not through the transom; bags/phones left on the beach while swimming; hire-car break-ins.
  • Effective countermeasures reported: short chain + padlock through the outboard and the tender's ring, engine always secured with a dedicated lock, tender hoisted in davits or aboard at night, nothing visible in cockpit/dinghy, dinghy alarm/lighting, dry bag with valuables always on your person on the beach.
  • Reporting: police 211 or (246) 430-7100 · ambulance emergency 511 · Harbour Master VHF 12 · coast guard via BPI; online report to CSSN; FB group "Barbados Cruisers" for rapid alerts.

Rescue & Emergencies

  • Control centres: 211 for police · 511 for ambulance · VHF 16 always monitored by the Signal Station and coast guard. The QEH (Queen Elizabeth Hospital) in Bridgetown is the main 24h A&E (Martindales Road). For serious cases medical evacuation with dedicated insurance may be needed (helicopter/US transfer). ★★★
  • Consular assistance: USA via Embassy Bridgetown (Wildey) +1 246 227-4000 ★★★★; UK via High Commission Bridgetown +1 246 430-7800; Canada via High Commission Bridgetown +1 246 629-3550; no Italian consulate locally — contact Embassy of Italy in Port of Spain (Trinidad) +1 868 628-6506 or Consulate in Caracas. At sea: call Signal Station VHF 12 or VHF 16 for SAR coordination (BPI/Coast Guard).
  • Hurricanes: island potentially exposed (June–November); monitor Barbados Met Services + NHC + local DEM media; follow BPI/Harbour Master instructions on VHF for securing alongside.
  • Reporting cruiser crime: online report to CSSN (thecssn.org) + local VHF; FB groups "Barbados Cruisers" for rapid alerts. VHF 16 always monitored.

Provisioning

Last checked: 28/08/2026

General Price Level — Barbados

  • Currency: Barbados dollar (BBD, pegged 2:1 to USD) — groceries are imported and more expensive than in mainland Europe (+30–50%); local produce (fish, tropical fruit, bread) is better value. skiptomalouuu.com ★★★
  • Yacht logistics: for ocean passages it is better to stock up in the larger islands (Antigua, St. Martin, Trinidad) where there is large-scale duty-free distribution; Barbados has good urban distribution (Massy, Trimart, Cost U Less) but higher prices for imports. ★★

Details for Main Base — Bridgetown Careenage / Shallow Draught

  • Daily shopping on foot is feasible from Harbour Road (Massy ~500 m): folding trolley recommended; Worthing/Trimart/Cost U Less are for the weekly shop (taxi 20–40 BBD each way, agree fare beforehand).
  • Typical supermarket hours: 08:00–20:00 Mon–Sat, 08:00–14:00 Sun/holidays (Massy); local minimarts often 07:00–21:00 daily. Reduced hours on public holidays (Crop Over, Christmas). ★★
  • Delivery aboard: rare, only on request from the larger supermarkets equipped for yacht provisioning (Massy Worthing/Holetown catering); confirm by phone/email with 24h notice. ★★
  • Chandlery near the marina for basic yacht spares; prices reasonable versus the resort. ★★

Markets

  • Bridgetown Fisheries Complex (Princess Alice Hwy, south of the Careenage): fish market daily with fresh catch in the morning (flying fish, dolphin/mahi-mahi, tuna, local barracuda); stalls open 06:00–16:00, busiest early morning after the fishing boats return. ★★★
  • Cheapside Market (Bridgetown) + Browne's Beach / Fairchild Market: local fruit/veg early morning (breadfruit, sweet potato, green banana, seasonal mango); covered market with spices. ★★★
  • Oistins Fish Market / Bay Garden (Christ Church): famous Friday Fish Fry but also a daily market with fresh fish; fruit trucks along Highway 7 and at Six Roads. ★★★
  • Where there is no proper covered market, roadside stalls and fruit trucks — good local prices. ★★

Transport for Provisioning

Taxis

  • Service is not metered on most of the island: agree the fare before boarding. Fares are regulated by Barbados Tourism with an official list for tourist routes. ★★★
  • Typical fare Careenage/Shallow Draught ↔ Massy Harbour Road: 10–20 BBD (~5–10 USD); Careenage ↔ Worthing/Trimart: 40–60 BBD; Oistins ↔ Bridgetown: 50–70 BBD; Holetown ↔ Speightstown: 30–50 BBD — confirm with driver or harbour office. ★★
  • Taxi contact: ask in the marina/harbour office or at the supermarket; taxi ranks at Harbour Road, Bridgetown Bus Terminal, airport. Central number Barbados Taxi Association +1 246 426-1021 (to be verified as of 28/08/2026) — DATA MISSING if no answer, use hotel taxi.

Bus / ZR / Minibus

  • Blue government buses (BTMI) + white ZRs with red stripe (route taxis): very frequent on main routes (Bridgetown ↔ Holetown/Speightstown via Highway 1; Bridgetown ↔ Oistins via Highway 7), every 5–15 min by day, fare 3.50 BBD (~1.75 USD) per ride (flat fare since 2020, exact change). BTMI ★★★
  • Nearest stop to the marina: Princess Alice Hwy / Harbour Road 100–300 m from the Careenage/Shallow Draught; for Port St. Charles stop Highway 1 at Six Men's Bay (100 m). ★★
  • Inconvenient with heavy loads: better to take a taxi for water cases or the weekly shop; bus useful for reconnaissance without loads.

Practical Tips

  • Folding trolley + insulated bags: essential if shopping on foot with the dinghy (beach landing at Carlisle, quayside at the Careenage).
  • Bottled water: stock up where dock water is doubtful or non-potable; keep bagged ice for passages to Saint Lucia/Grenada.
  • Always check holiday hours and ice availability before long passages (180–240 M).
  • For ocean provisioning (transatlantic): best to do one big shop at Bridgetown (Massy Harbour Road + Cost U Less Warrens) by taxi; for daily top-ups use Holetown/Speightstown if anchored in the north.

Cruising Guide to Anchorages

Last checked: 28/08/2026 · coordinates approximate, navigate with official charts

General Anchoring Rules (first of all)

  • Free anchoring over sand, EXCEPT in the prohibited areas below and over protected coral/reef (Carlisle Bay Marine Park with wrecks, fringing reef south/east): anchor and chain must not lie on coral — where reef is present, anchor only over clearly visible white sand patches or on buoys where provided. ★★★
  • IALA-B throughout the Caribbean: red to starboard when entering harbour (reversed versus Europe). Always call Bridgetown Signal Station VHF 12 ("8P") for entry into the harbour and for any movement inside the Bridgetown basin. Barbados Port Inc. ★★★★★
  • Barrier reef and reefs: always keep >0.5 M off the fringing reef in the north-west (Six Men's Bay surf) and >1 M off the Atlantic east coast (continuous surf); enter a bay only in good light following the 10 m contour; at night only with verified waypoints and sounder. ★★
  • Jet skis and daytime traffic: Carlisle Bay is very busy with jet skis and snorkel tours 09:00–17:00 — keep clear, chain well laid out, marker buoy if swimming over the wrecks. ★★

⛔ Strictly Prohibited Areas (official / practical)

Area Prohibition Source
Carlisle Bay Marine Park — wreck area (6 wrecks + artificial reef) Anchoring on the wrecks and protected structures is forbidden; anchor only on free sand in dedicated areas; respect marker buoys and diver corridors Barbados Port Inc. — Yacht Masters Guide ★★★★ · Dive Barbados ★★★
Folkestone Marine Park (Holetown, St. James) Marine park with protected reef: anchoring on coral forbidden, only on sand outside the reef or on buoys where installed; respect bathing markers Barbados Coastal Zone Management ★★★★ · local guides ★★
Bridgetown Deep Water Harbour basin and channel Anchoring prohibited in the dredged channel and in the commercial/cruise basin; berthing only on Signal Station instructions Barbados Port Inc. ★★★★★
Private buoys and bathing corridors (west/south) Charter/hotel buoys (Sandy Lane, Holetown, Carlisle) and beach corridors not to be used without permission; respect bathing buoys local guides ★★
Atlantic east coast (Bathsheba → Consett Bay → Ragged Point) No practicable anchorage — not listed as a formal prohibited zone but to be excluded for danger: surf, continuous swell, reef with no shelter safetyanchoralarm.com — Barbados South & East Coast ★★

Full texts and brochures: BPI Yacht Masters Guide (PDF on barbadosport.com) and charts BA 1042 (Barbados) + BA 2482 (Windward Islands). The Carlisle/Folkestone buoys are charted and locally marked.

  • There are marine parks with mandatory or recommended mooring buoys (Carlisle wrecks, Folkestone): using the buoy where present is preferable to anchoring on reef. Check local colours (yellow/blue day-use).
  • IALA-B buoyage reversed versus Italy. ★★★

  • BA charts show the marine park limits and Carlisle wrecks; buy from authorised dealers (Admiralty, NV Charts PoD). ★★★★
  • Free administrative chart: BPI Yacht Masters Guide PDF + Barbados Coastal Zone Management brochure with Folkestone/Carlisle perimeters. ★★★★
  • For day-to-day navigation: official electronics on the plotter + paper BA 1042 as mandatory backup; IALA-B buoyage everywhere.

Not Included (for now)

  • Holetown / Paynes Bay / Sandy Lane (central west): long leeward beaches with possible anchoring over sand 3–8 m, but with many private hotel buoys and jet skis — detailed data and waypoints insufficient for a dedicated card, to be verified with satellite (200 m off Sandy Lane) ★★
  • Six Men's Bay / Maycock's Bay (north-west near Port St. Charles): sheltered leeward roadsteads but with fringing reef close to the entrance — approach only in good light, to be verified for depth/buoys ★★
  • Silver Sands / Long Beach / Bottom Bay (south-east): bays open to S/SE, sand but exposed to swell, rocky patches — day stop only in settled weather, not for overnight ★★
  • St. Lawrence Gap / Worthing Beach: theoretical anchorage but off a reef and hotels — not recommended overnight, Carlisle 2 M to the north is better.

Anchor Checklist for Barbados

  1. Signal Station VHF 12 ("8P") called before entering Bridgetown and Q flag flying ✓
  2. Chart BA 1042 + updated electronics + IALA-B (red to starboard on entry) in mind ✓
  3. Anchor over sand verified (not on Carlisle coral/wrecks) — mask inspection if in doubt ✓
  4. Distance from reef/bathing buoys respected; jet skis watched by day at Carlisle ✓
  5. Dinghy secured with chain + padlock, outboard locked (theft at Carlisle/Bridgetown) ✓
  6. Forecast BMS + NHC checked (easterly swell even with moderate trades) ✓
  7. Zarpe and travelform/SailClear receipts ready for any inspection in the roadstead ✓

Marine Trades & Chandlers

Local hub is limited: Barbados is not a technical hub — for major work many owners rely on regional hubs (Antigua — English Harbour/Jolly Harbour, Sint Maarten — Simpson Bay, Trinidad — Chaguaramas). In Bridgetown freelancers work in the marina (mechanics, electrics, composites) but without a structured network like Le Marin (Martinique). Contact is typically by phone/WhatsApp; English is spoken. For significant jobs always request a written quote and confirm lead times in high season (Dec–Apr), when the few trades are fully booked.

Other Useful Operators (regional hubs for a serious refit)

  • Antigua — English Harbour (North Sails, Sanders Sails, Jolly Harbour marine services): sail lofts, riggers, composites — ~240 M NW, the nearest for structured work.
  • Sint Maarten — Simpson Bay (Budget Marine, FKG Composites, 100 t travelift): duty-free, immediate spares.
  • Trinidad — Chaguaramas (Power Boats, Peakes, Coral Cove, 70–300 t travelifts): outside the hurricane belt, hurricane hub.
  • Saint Lucia — Rodney Bay Marina: intermediate services ~95 M away, good alternative to Bridgetown for a technical stop.
  • In Barbados: basic chandlery + town hardware stores (Bay Street, Harbour Road); for paint/antifoul ask in the harbour.

Where to Find What

  • Engines/refrigeration/welding: freelancers working at Bridgetown Shallow Draught / Careenage — ask in the harbour office; often ex-fishermen with a workshop in St. Michael. ★★
  • Sails / rigging: sailmaker often not resident — mobile service from Antigua/St. Martin on call (1–2 weeks). Keep a spare sail aboard. ★★
  • Antifouling/haul-out: check travelift/crane availability in the marina — data not published; alternative is Chaguaramas/Antigua for hauling.
  • Liferafts / safety: servicing at regional hubs — not documented in Barbados as of 28/08/2026.

Note: Barbados does not have a 20,000-item "Caraïbe Marine" like Le Marin; the range is basic. For lithium/solar/inverter components order online (Victron etc.) for delivery to the marina stating yacht name and berth; duty payable on arrival. ★★

Practical Notes

  • Payment: many trades accept local BBD/USD bank transfer or cash; for small jobs cash/card. Always ask for an invoice (useful for customs/insurance). If the job is >500 BBD ask for a deposit only once work has started and balance on completion.
  • Lead times: spares from Europe/USA = 1–3 weeks (DHL/Colissimo) + customs; workshops often order via Miami. High season (Dec–Apr) = workshops busy even in regional hubs — book weeks ahead.
  • On-board power: electrical components (battery chargers, inverters, solar controllers) limited availability in Barbados — better to order before the Barbados leg or stock up in Antigua/St. Martin.
  • Antifoul: available at the harbour hardware/chandlery and at Port St. Charles; a proper haul-out is done in Chaguaramas or Antigua if a certified travelift is needed.
  • For AMEL / French yachts: local firms work on all makes; for original aluminium rigging and AMEL-specific spares contact first the Antigua hubs (riggers with AMEL experience) or Caraïbe Marine Martinique before the crossing.

Yacht Customs Clearance

Last checked: 25/08/2026 · Sources: portauthority.bz ★★★★★ · msatt-equivalente locale/belizemegayacht ★★ · oldbelize.com ★★

Procedure standard (tutti i 4 porti)

  1. SailClear ≥48h prima + APIS su caricomeapis.org
  2. All'avvicinamento: VHF 16/68 → Belize Port Authority (presidio attivo solo a Belize City)
  3. Q flag; bordo di 5 ufficiali (Customs, Health, Immigration, Quarantine BAHA, BPA); trasporto officer a carico
  4. Documenti: clearance ultimo porto, registro nave, CSR, P&I, ISSC, crew/passenger list, stores list, NIL list (stowaways/armi/narcotici), ports of call ★★★★
  5. Permit Port Authority: BZ$240 / primi 30 gg [Old Belize] ★★
  6. Immigration: timbro 30 gg per l'equipaggio ★★★★

Estensioni

Chi Come Costo
Equipaggio Immigration Office, +30 gg US$25/pax (o BZ$25) ★★★
Yacht Customs (retro Ships Report), +30 gg — ★★★

Particolari

  • 24h di grazia per completare la clearance ★★★
  • Dopo il check-in: navigazione libera sulla barriera e nelle cayes; nessun despacho interno ★★★★
  • Uscita: clearance internazionale dal porto di partenza; Belize City richiede pilota/waiver ★★★
  • Overtime serale/festivo degli ufficiali a carico ★★

← Bonaire

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 28/08/2026

Status

Bonaire is a special municipality (openbaar lichaam) of the Netherlands in the Dutch Caribbean BES (Bonaire, St. Eustatius and Saba) — part of the Kingdom of the Netherlands but outside the EU and outside the Schengen Area, with entry and customs rules distinct from Aruba, Curaçao and Sint Maarten (constituent countries of the Kingdom). BES rules are neither EU nor Schengen rules.

For EU / Italian Citizens — No Visa for Short Stays

Item Rule Source
Visa No visa required for Italy and other visa-exempt nationalities (EU, USA, Canada, UK, Australia, etc.) — Italy is on the official exempt list NetherlandsWorldwide — Visa-exempt list for the Caribbean parts of the Kingdom ★★★★★
Tourist stay (foreign nationals / “aliens”, including non-Dutch Italians) Max 90 days in any 180-day period, counted cumulatively across Bonaire + St. Eustatius + Saba. No residence permit needed for that period; the stay may be shortened at the border by the Royal Marechaussee (KMar) based on purpose and means RijksdienstCN — Tourist stay (EN) ★★★★★; RijksdienstCN — Travel with non-Dutch passport ★★★★★
Dutch nationals (European or Curaçao / Aruba / Sint Maarten) and US nationals Max 180 days in any 365-day period visa-free; if they work or do an internship the limit is max 90 days in any 365 without a Verklaring van rechtswege RijksdienstCN — Tourist stay ★★★★★
Documents Passport valid for the entire stay (must still be valid on departure); Italian national ID card not accepted for the BES Islands RijksdienstCN — Travel with non-Dutch passport ★★★★★; bonaire.com — Visa & Entry Requirements, 07/07/2026 ★★★
Entry conditions Return/onward ticket, accommodation address (hotel/apartment or boat with mooring/marina assignment), proof of sufficient means: baseline US$ 1,000 per week if you already hold an outbound ticket; alternatively a resident guarantor with demonstrable means. Clear purpose of visit (tourism/family visit) RijksdienstCN — Travel with non-Dutch passport ★★★★★
Transit Airside transit at Bonaire within 48 h without a visa if you hold documents for the onward destination; by sea → see clearance NetherlandsWorldwide — Airport transit BES ★★★★★

Note for crews coming from an island hop in the Caribbean: the 90/180 count is a rolling window across the entire BES. Official example: 45 days already spent in the previous 180 → 45 days remain; 95 days already spent → overstay of 5 days. [RijksdienstCN — Travel with non-Dutch passport ★★★★★]

Important Note for Arrival by Sea

  • People checks (Immigration/IND + KMar) are separate from the boat formalities (Customs / Belastingdienst Caribisch Nederland): even with a valid EU passport you must complete mandatory clearance for the boat on entry and on departure → see 01 — Clearance.
  • Only port of entry: Kralendijk — Customs and Immigration share the same building at Fort Oranje / Plasa Wilhelmina (Harbour Office area). The entire island is a Marine Park: anchoring is forbidden, use only STINAPA moorings (overnight two-tone moorings) or a marina berth. Ocean Posse — Bonaire ★★★; STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★
  • Have ready for each person: passport, crew list, outbound ticket / proof of onward passage, address of stay (mooring number/marina), proof of means; for the boat: registration/nationality, proof of ownership, crew list and the mandatory outbound document (zarpe/clearance) from the previous port — without proof of the port of departure entry may be refused. SailClear pre-notification has been expected by Customs since 2023: there is no computer on the quay, file it before departure at sailclear.com. Cruising sources aggregate ★★★; [CruisersWiki / Ocean Posse] ★★

Beyond 90 Days? (Italian / EU and Other Nationals)

Situation Rule Source
Tourist stay beyond 90/180 A residence permit is required. Apply to IND Caribisch Nederland — Bonaire, Kaya Gresia 11, Kralendijk (information desk Mon–Thu 08:00–11:30; collection Mon–Thu 13:30–16:00 Fri 08:00–11:30; tel +599 715 8330, IND@rijksdienstCN.com, info line Mon–Thu 08:00–12:00) RijksdienstCN — Contact IND Bonaire ★★★★★
Dutch/US nationals beyond 180/365 (or 90/365 if working) A Verklaring van rechtswege (Declaration of Admittance by Law) is required by appointment at IND RijksdienstCN — Tourist stay ★★★★★
Work / internship during the stay Even if you start work after arriving as a tourist, the 90/365 cap immediately applies to Dutch/US nationals and a work permit is required; for other foreign nationals a specific permit is required — work is not permitted on a tourist entry alone RijksdienstCN — Tourist stay ★★★★★
Overstay Possible penalties: fine, removal, re-entry ban (decision by KMar/IND) — the period may already have been shortened at the border RijksdienstCN — Travel with non-Dutch passport ★★★★★

In practice: with an Italian passport you enter without a visa but within a 90/180 window across the entire BES and with checks on return ticket/means/accommodation. To stay longer or to work you need a local IND application — indicative processing 2–4 weeks according to a secondary non-governmental source (DATA MISSING for official Bonaire processing time).

The Boat: Taxes, Park and Temporary Admission

Item Rule Source
Temporary admission for non-resident yachts Private use allowed with report to Customs within 24 h of arrival; standard practice max 6 months with extension only in exceptional circumstances on request to Customs (Punda/BCN); charter/sale and commercial use prohibited; beyond the term import duties apply plus possible fine/precautionary seizure Practice documented for Curaçao/BES in Curaçao Customs brochure “Pleziervaartuigen” (Art. 102 LVTI, 24h/6 months) — Bonaire-specific BES wording DATA MISSING for verbatim BCN confirmation ★★★; Belastingdienst CN — Customs ★★★★★ (general import/export framework)
STINAPA Nature Fee (Marine Park + Washington Slagbaai) US$ 40 per person per calendar year (1 Jan–31 Dec), mandatory as soon as you enter the water or enter Washington Slagbaai; free for under-13s and BES/ABC residents with valid sedula; Washington Slagbaai day visitors US$ 10/day. QR code + ID required; pay at stinapa.bonairenaturefee.org STINAPA — Nature Fee / Annual Report 2022 ★★★★★; bonaire.com — Nature Fee 2026 ★★★; STINAPA FAQ ★★★★★
Visitor Entry Tax (government entry levy) US$ 75 adults (13+) / US$ 10 children 0–12, residents of the former Netherlands Antilles and cruise passengers US$ 10; Bonaire residents exempt with sedula. Per visit, valid 1 month, payable within 48 h before arrival at tourismtax.bonairegov.com (no cash on arrival). Separate from and additional to the Nature Fee. Two different payment portals tourismtax.bonairegov.com ★★★★★; bonaire.com — Tourist Tax 2026 ★★★
Customs / Immigration for the boat Free of charge during normal office hours Cruising sources aggregate ★★★; [CruisersWiki — Bonaire] ★★
Overnight mooring Only STINAPA two-tone moorings for visitors, US$ 35/night, max 18 m (55–58 ft), first-come first-served, payment and allocation via Harbour Village Marina; no tying directly to the buoy, use your own line (≥6 m), one boat per mooring STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★; Annual Report STINAPA 2022 ★★★★; 5730169490767872" target="_blank" rel="noopener">InfoBonaire / NoForeignLand — Kralendijk ★★★

Vaccinations

No mandatory vaccination for arrivals direct from Europe/USA. Yellow fever vaccination required only if you come from or have transited >12 h in a country at risk of transmission (Amazon basin, sub-Saharan Africa — WHO list). In that case an International Certificate valid for life since 2016 is required for travellers aged ≥9 months, to be shown on entry; vaccination at least 10 days before arrival.

Yacht Customs Clearance

Last checked: 28/08/2026 · Main sources: Belastingdienst Caribisch Nederland (Customs CN) ★★★★★, RijksdienstCN/IND ★★★★★, STINAPA ★★★★★, Cruising sources aggregate/Ocean Posse/CruisersWiki ★★★

Who Must Clear

All leisure craft, any flag and nationality, that: - enter BES waters (Bonaire) coming from a foreign port/territorial sea or the high seas; - depart for a foreign port/sea or the high seas. BES residents returning from foreign passages must also report. Movement within Bonaire ↔ Saba/St. Eustatius is inside the same BES territory but, after a passage through international waters, reporting on entry is still required. Belastingdienst CN — Douane Caribisch Nederland ★★★★★

Leisure and sport vessels are exempt from cargo import/export clearance (no goods declaration if not carrying commercial cargo), but the obligation to report to Customs and Immigration for people and vessel and to obtain a departure permit remains. Belastingdienst CN — Export clearance: leisure vessels exempt ★★★★★

Before Arrival: SailClear and Papers

  1. SailClear pre-notification expected by Customs (since 2023) — file the notification at sailclear.com before you set sail: on the quay at Kralendijk there is no computer available to complete it. It shortens time in the office but does not replace appearing in person. Cruising sources aggregate ★★★; SailClear FAQ ★★★
  2. Prepare a folder (originals + 2 copies):
  3. passports for all crew (valid for the entire stay);
  4. vessel registration/nationality, proof of ownership/insurance;
  5. crew list / passenger manifest (full name, date of birth, nationality, passport number);
  6. outbound document (zarpe/despacho) from the previous port — mandatory: without proof of the country of departure entry may be refused (check also enforced on arrivals from Venezuela/Los Roques). Cruising sources aggregate ★★★; Doyle Guides — Bonaire Updates 30/05/2017 ★★
  7. receipts for Visitor Entry Tax and STINAPA Nature Fee if already paid online (recommended within 48 h before arrival for the Entry Tax).
  8. Notify Harbour Village Marina about your mooring: VHF 17 (mooring management) or 12 for availability before entry per secondary sources; tel +599 717 7419. Overnight moorings cannot be reserved, allocation is first-come first-served. InfoBonaire — Yachting & Cruising ★★★; 5730169490767872" target="_blank" rel="noopener">NoForeignLand — Kralendijk ★★★

On Arrival at Kralendijk — Quayside Procedure

Only port of entry: Kralendijk — 12°09.1′ N 068°16.7′ W (off Fort Oranje). Ocean Posse — Bonaire ★★★

  1. Never anchor: the entire island perimeter down to the drop-off is Bonaire National Marine Park — anchoring is prohibited (exception only for traditional fishing boats using stones). Use only the two-tone overnight moorings (white/red, rugby-ball shape with yellow pendant) between 12°09.44′ N 068°17.09′ W (south of Harbour Village entrance) and 12°09.06′ N 068°16.41′ W (off Karel's Bar). STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★; STINAPA — Boating PDF ★★★★★
  2. Once secured, go by dinghy to the dinghy dock at Karel's Bar (bar/restaurant, free berthing with a drink) or directly to the Customs/Immigration jetty (200 m south of the dinghy dock, berths reserved for official craft — keep clear). CruisersWiki — Bonaire ★★
  3. Report immediately and in person — all hands (Immigration headcount) at the Customs + Immigration office in the same building at Fort Oranje / Plasa Wilhelmina 3 — Immigration desk hours Mon–Thu 08:00–11:30 and 13:30–16:00, Fri 08:00–11:30; Harbour Customs tel +599 715 8591. Fill in entry forms, show zarpe and vessel papers, declare weapons. RijksdienstCN — Contact IND ★★★★★; Belastingdienst CN — Contact / Customs Bonaire Kaya L.D. Gerharts 12, tel +599 715 8585, harbour Plasa Wilhelmina 3 tel +599 715 8591 ★★★★★
  4. Weapons and similar: pistols, rifles, flare guns, spear guns are treated as weapons: they must be declared and deposited with Customs for the duration of your stay, collected on departure. InfoBonaire — Yachting & Cruising ★★★; CruisersWiki — Bonaire ★★; Doyle Guides 2017 ★★
  5. Pay on the spot if not already done online: STINAPA Nature Fee US$ 40 (calendar year) and Visitor Entry Tax US$ 75/10 (see 00). Customs and Immigration charge no clearance fee during normal hours. Annual Report STINAPA 2022 ★★★★; tourismtax.bonairegov.com ★★★★★
  6. STINAPA/mooring formalities: registration at the Customs Office and Harbour Village Marina, mooring assignment, briefing on mooring use (use your own line ≥6 m, do not tie off directly, max 18 m / ~55–58 ft, one boat per mooring, no commercial activity on board, respect visa duration). STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★

Handy Tip (Cruiser Experience)

If you arrive outside office hours (e.g. Sunday), take a free overnight mooring and report first thing the next morning when the office opens — do not remain unannounced via VHF/marina. If you temporarily leave your mooring for a daytime dive (max 2 h on the yellow day-use moorings), leave a fender/pendant on your mooring to signal occupation. 5730169490767872" target="_blank" rel="noopener">NoForeignLand — Kralendijk ★★★; STINAPA — Boating PDF ★★★★★

Departure (Outbound Clearance)

  • Return to the same Customs/Immigration office before slipping your mooring, with passports and vessel papers; request zarpe/departure declaration and a duplicate departure card if needed where the next country requires it. Collect any deposited weapons. Belastingdienst CN — Export clearance: duplicate departure card on request ★★★★★
  • Advise Harbour Village Marina when you vacate the mooring; pump-out and waste disposal are included in the mooring fee — rangers may require a pump-out based on holding-tank capacity, people on board and length of stay. 5730169490767872" target="_blank" rel="noopener">NoForeignLand — Kralendijk ★★★

Regional Customs Authority

Belastingdienst Caribisch Nederland — Douane Caribisch Nederland, Kaya L.D. Gerharts 12, Postbus 329, Kralendijk · +599 715 8585 · english.belastingdienst-cn.nl ★★★★★ For legislation: Douane- en Accijnswet BES (BWBR0029236) — permanent supervision of import/export/transit and domestic excise. ★★★★★

Moorings and Anchoring Ban (Impact on Clearance)

The Bonaire National Marine Park surrounds the entire island: anchoring is prohibited on coral/protected bottom. The only legal overnight stops for visitors are the STINAPA overnight moorings or a marina berth. Private moorings (white/yellow/orange) are reserved for residents with a STINAPA permit (waiting list ~3 years) — do not use them. Public yellow/blue day moorings are day-use only max 2 h, one boat >4 m per mooring (or up to 3 tenders <4 m). STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★

Cruisers' Experiences

  • Entry described as “easy and friendly, free of charge, efficient; everyone must appear for headcount” — Customs holds flare/spear guns without hassle and returns them on departure. ★★ [CruisersWiki — Bonaire; Doyle Guides 2017]
  • Harbour Village very responsive on VHF for mooring allocation; in high season moorings fill up — call before entry and have a long line ready (≥6 m). ★★★ [NoForeignLand — Kralendijk; InfoBonaire]
  • Since 2023 Customs expect a pre-filed SailClear: those arriving without it find only paper forms and longer processing. ★★★ [Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  • Failure to report / missing zarpe / undeclared weapons: entry refused, precautionary seizure of the weapon, possible detention of the vessel pending regularisation, import duties if temporary admission is breached (commercial use, exceeding 6 months without extension). Belastingdienst CN — permanent supervision ★★★★★; Curaçao practice 24h/6 months ★★★
  • Overstay (people): fine, removal and re-entry ban (KMar/IND); the period granted may already have been shortened at the border for insufficient means. RijksdienstCN — Travel with non-Dutch passport ★★★★★
  • Pollution / black-water discharge without holding tank: working holding tank required to use the moorings; otherwise you must berth in a marina or leave Bonaire. [NoForeignLand — Kralendijk] ★★★

To Verify Before Your Cruise

  • Availability of overnight moorings in high season (Dec–Apr) and updated marina rates; contact Harbour Village before the passage.
  • Updated WHO yellow-fever risk list if coming from South America/Africa.
  • Any updates to SailClear/BES platform or VHF channel (17 vs 12) and IND/Customs hours — check english.rijksdienstcn.com and belastingdienst-cn.nl before departure.

Ports & Marinas

Last checked: 28/08/2026 · Coordinates in decimal degrees / N-W as per source · datum WGS84

Bonaire is entirely surrounded by the Bonaire National Marine Park: anchoring is prohibited everywhere (coral bottom) except for traditional fishing boats <4 m using a coral stone. Legal stops are only on STINAPA moorings or alongside in a marina. All clearance takes place at Kralendijk (the only port of entry). STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★; STINAPA Boating PDF ★★★★★; InfoBonaire — Yachting & Cruising ★★★

Leeward (West) Coast — The Only Workable, Sheltered Side

The entire west coast from Harbour Village to south of Kralendijk lies in the lee of the trades, with flat water and depth that drops away quickly. Here you find the two full-service marinas and the 30–51 two-tone overnight moorings (white/red, rugby-ball shape with yellow pendant) for visitors between 12°09.44′ N 068°17.09′ W (south of Harbour Village entrance) and 12°09.06′ N 068°16.41′ W (off Karel's Bar). STINAPA ★★★★★

Kralendijk — Harbour Village Marina ⚓ sole port of entry

  • 12°09.83′ N 068°17.08′ W · VHF 17 (town mooring allocation) and 12 (marina office) · VHF 16 listening watch · harbourvillage.com/marina ★★★★
  • Only BES port of entry: Customs/Immigration at Plasa Wilhelmina 3 / Fort Oranje (200 m south of Karel's Bar dinghy dock); SailClear pre-notification expected before departure, all crew must report in person (headcount). See 01 Clearance. Belastingdienst CN ★★★★★
  • Full-service marina: 60 berths for yachts up to 60 ft + a mega-yacht pier for vessels up to 240 ft (Ambar Point); 30/50 A and 50 Hz, water, diesel/petrol, bunker >10,000 l via Curoil, pump-out, WiFi, showers, laundry, parking, security. Harbour Village Marina ★★★★
  • Management of STINAPA overnight moorings for visitors: allocation first-come first-served via Harbour Village Marina, payment on site; use your own line ≥6 m (do not tie directly to the buoy), one boat per mooring, max 18 m (55–58 ft), holding tank mandatory, no commercial activity on board, stay limited to visa duration. STINAPA ★★★★★
  • Dinghy dock: take the tender to Karel's Bar (a drink appreciated) or the Customs/Immigration jetty (berths reserved for official craft — keep clear). Always lock dinghy and outboard. ★★
  • Contact: tel +599 717 7419 / WhatsApp +599 701 7500 · dockmaster@harbourvillage.com · Office hours: Mon–Fri 08:30–12:00 & 13:30–17:00, Sat 08:00–13:00. Harbour Village Marina ★★★★
  • Shelter: good protection from the trades; exposed to north/west swell — check the local forecast before entering, especially with winter cold fronts. ★★

Plaza Marina (Van der Valk Plaza Beach & Dive Resort)

  • J.A. Abraham Blvd 80, Kralendijk (~12°08.6′ N 068°16.5′ W — DATA MISSING verified official coordinate) · tel +599 717 2500 / marina@bonaire.valk.com · VHF DATA MISSING ★★★
  • Resort marina a few minutes' walk from central Kralendijk; floating berths for leisure and charter boats (Bonaire Yacht Charters), with resort access (pools, PADI 5★ dive centre). Ideal if you are staying at the resort or for a short stop with hotel facilities. Plaza Resort — Marina ★★★
  • Berths managed via Plaza Boat Club: 24/7 surveillance, gated access, haul-out and hurricane protection, fuel/water/power alongside. Rates see below. Plaza Boat Club ★★★

Klein Bonaire

  • Uninhabited island 0.8 km (0.4 NM) to leeward of Kralendijk, a nature reserve and turtle nesting ground. Only yellow/blue day-use moorings max 2 h (one boat >4 m per mooring or up to 3 tenders <4 m), overnight stay prohibited; max 13 m. Respect the reef and underwater trails. STINAPA ★★★★★

Other West-Coast Moorings (Day-Use)

  • Dozens of public yellow/blue moorings along the dive coast (Buddy Dive, Harbour Village, Eden Beach etc.): max 2 h, first-come first-served, not for overnight stays. Private moorings (white/yellow/orange) are reserved for residents with a STINAPA permit (waiting list ~3 years) — not available to visitors. STINAPA ★★★★★

Windward (East) Coast, Lac Bay and Washington Slagbaai — Not Tenable Overnight

  • The windward east coast is exposed to the Atlantic, with continuous reef, surf and no shelter: no harbour, no moorings, no recommended anchorage for cruising yachts. Lac Bay (south-east lagoon, RAMSAR/mangroves) is a reserve and kiteboarding area with very shallow water — unsuitable for sailing yachts. Washington Slagbaai (north-west) is a land park with no nautical facilities. Approach only in settled weather with local support, never for an overnight stay. ★★

Seasonality & Weather

Last checked: 28/08/2026

Climate

  • Mean temperature ~27–30 °C (max 30–32 °C, min 24–27 °C); semi-arid BSh/BS climate in the southern Dry Zone, moderate to fresh E/ENE trades, humidity ~75%. ★★★★★
  • Average rainfall 350–450 mm/year over ~65 days (peak Oct–Jan), highly variable; sea temperature 27 °C mean (25.9 °C Feb–Mar, 28.2 °C Sep–Oct); diurnal range exceeds seasonal range. ★★★★★

Seasons

Period Characteristics
February – May Dry season, steady trades and mostly clear skies: best time for cruising
October – January Rainy season with brief showers in the morning/early evening; peak Oct–Dec; Jul–Sep transitional

★★★

Hurricane Preparedness (Official ★★★★)

Bonaire has no French-style cyclone plan; follow KNMI Caribisch Nederland and Meteo Curaçao (MDC) warnings via knmidc.org and VHF; the local disaster committee activates an annual plan; no berth is guaranteed 100% in a cyclone.

Hurricanes

Season 1 June–30 November, peak mid-Aug to mid-Oct. Bonaire sits on the southern edge of the hurricane belt (12°N): a cyclone within 100 NM ~1 in 11 years; a direct hit historically ~1 in 38.5 years; northern fringes possible. Past events: Ivan (2004, 65 NM north Cat.4), Felix (2007, 30 NM north), Bonnie (2022, Code Red 3–5" rain), Beryl (2024, 121 km north of Rincon). [meteo.cw ★★★★★; KNMI ★★★★★; bonaire.com ★★★]

Local Winds

  • Trades from E/ENE 12–20 kt, mean ~7–8 m/s stronger in the dry/transition season and lighter in the rainy season; acceleration gusts between the ABC Islands and in the lee of low ground. ★★★★★
  • Saharan dust (SAL) and Venezuelan upwelling suppress cloud; high pressure can bring E–NW seas 4–7 ft with small-craft advisories (≥6 Bft) on exposed coasts. ★★★★

Typical Weather Windows

Short passages Bonaire–Curaçao (~35 NM) or Bonaire–Aruba (~105 NM) are workable with trades ≤18–20 kt, best at dawn; channels: confused seas — avoid >20 kt. Long passages towards Colombia/Venezuela: wait for a stable post-tropical-wave window. ★★

Safety & Security

Last fully checked: 28/08/2026 · Next monthly check: 28/09/2026

Safety Rating: 4 / 5

Aspect Score Reason
Personal safety (visitors / cruisers) 4/5 Violence against visitors is rare; violent crime is concentrated among locals and in domestic settings
Theft from boats 3/5 Dinghy/outboard at moderate risk (8 CSSN incidents in 5 years within 10 km); theft from cars at dive sites persists
Overall island context 4/5 Low-crime island but with a rise in armed youth violence and drink-driving in 2025

Scale: 0 = terrible → 5 = very safe. Our own assessment, synthesising the sources below; updated at every monthly check.

Why not 5: opportunistic theft (unlocked dinghies, valuables left in cars at dive sites) and growth in armed youth violence and alcohol-related road accidents in 2025. No targeted violent attacks on cruisers reported in the last 5 years in the aggregated sources.

General Overview

  • Canadian government advisory (updated 29/07/2026 ★★★★): “Take normal security precautions” — the lowest level. Petty crime (pickpocketing, purse snatching, theft from vehicles/hotels) present; avoid isolated places and unpatrolled beaches after dark.
  • US State Department (reissued 19/08/2024 ★★★★): Level 1: Exercise Normal Precautions — Bonaire low-crime, non-violent opportunistic crime; do not leave items unattended.
  • NetherlandsWorldwide (updated 17/06/2026 ★★★★): green code — “U kunt erheen reizen” — petty crime possible, drugs (including soft drugs) prohibited with penalties harsher than in the European Netherlands.
  • UK FCDO (★★★): petty theft/street crime, avoid isolated areas including beaches after dark, keep valuables out of sight; drug-smuggling transit via Bonaire.
  • KPCN annual report 2025 (presented 06/02/2026 ★★★★★): 712 property crimes (theft 175, vandalism 139, burglary 104, theft from vehicles 102, theft at dive sites 57) — scooter/motorcycle theft −85%, bicycle (e-bike) theft +33%; 327 violent crimes (domestic violence 112, assault 55, threats 46, death threats 43) concentrated in Antriol/Playa/Nikiboko peaking Fri–Sun; 32 arrests for weapons, 10 weapons seized, 64% of weapons suspects aged 15–25; 1,401 road accidents, 1,179 fines, 206 arrests for drink-driving.
  • Local press / BES Reporter 07/02/2026 ★★★★: trend confirmed — scooter theft down but e-bikes up; robberies/thefts most frequent in Playa (scooter/business/house break-ins), Antriol (theft from vehicles, house burglaries), Nikiboko (business burglaries); extra patrols at dive sites for theft from tourist cars.

Theft Targeting Cruisers

Data from the Caribbean Safety and Security Net (thecssn.org ★★★), checked 28/08/2026:

  • 8 incidents in the last 5 years within 10 km of Kralendijk (Green dock/Kralendijk moorings/Port Bonaire/Plaza Resort): almost all dinghy/outboard thefts, 3 attempted thefts with boarding.
  • Case detail: 2022-05-03 Plaza Resort dinghy theft; 2022-05-07 Kralendijk moorings 10ft Arimar + 8HP Mercury stolen at night (lines cut, not locked); 2024-06-17 Port Bonaire 2 dinghies/40HP Yamaha stolen same night from canal dock (even though chain-locked, one recovered at Klein Bonaire); 2019-07-26 Budget Marine floating dock locked dinghy stolen and found at Klein Bonaire minus fuel tank; 2024-10-06 Kralendijk moorings dinghy/20HP Tohatsu not locked — attempted theft foiled by neighbour; 2025-10-14 Green dock Talamex Highline/9.8HP Suzuki not locked stolen (found without engine); 2026-03-19/20 Kralendijk moorings 3 attempted thefts/boardings at night by swimmers coming aboard, threats, police attended but no arrest.
  • Recurring hotspots: Green dock jetty, Kralendijk moorings, Port Bonaire canal homes, Budget Marine dock by the Venezuelan consulate.
  • Even chained dinghies have been taken (June 2024, 2 cases).
  • Effective countermeasures reported by cruisers/KPCN: short chain + padlock through the transom, engine secured with dedicated bar-lock, dinghy hoisted aboard at night, nothing left on view in car/dinghy/boat, targeted KPCN patrols at dive sites/marinas (2025: increased surveillance).
  • Reporting incidents: CSSN online report, KPCN 911, Coast Guard 913 (VHF 16), Harbour Village Marina Ch 17. Local cruisers' net / VHF for quick alerts ★★.

Anchorage Pilot

Last checked: 28/08/2026 · indicative coordinates — navigate with official charts

⚠️ SPECIAL CASE — ANCHORING PROHIBITED AROUND THE ENTIRE ISLAND. The whole perimeter of Bonaire, Klein Bonaire and Lac Bay is the Bonaire National Marine Park (BNMP, managed by STINAPA) — from the shallows to the 60 m / 75 m depth contour depending on the administrative definition: anchoring is prohibited everywhere. Only exception: traditional fishing boats ≤4 m using a coral stone. Overnight stays only on STINAPA two-tone overnight moorings (visitors, max 18 m) operated by Harbour Village Marina, or in a marina. Penalty up to US$ 2,800 and up to 1 month in prison ★★★ · Sources: STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★ · STINAPA — Boating ★★★★★ · InfoBonaire — Yachting & Cruising ★★★ · 5730169490767872" target="_blank" rel="noopener">NoForeignLand — Kralendijk ★★

General Mooring Rules (Read First)

  • Never drop anchor in the Park: never lower an anchor on sand/coral/seagrass — not even “for a moment” for a swim or the tender. Mooring lines are light double lines on concrete blocks: inspect them by diving and, if needed, add your own safety line ★★★ · Cruising sources aggregate ★★★
  • Speed in the Park: 10 km/h inside the BNMP; 20 km/h outside up to 12 NM from the coast; 5 km/h in mooring fields and in harbours/basins; minimum distance 50 m from any moored boat ★★★★★ · STINAPA — Boating ★★★★★
  • Stay seaward of the buoys: in the BNMP always remain on the seaward (dark-blue water) side of the yellow mooring/dive buoys; never pass between the buoys and the shore (protected light-blue water) and never beach the boat ★★★★★ · STINAPA — Boating ★★★★★ · Blue Bay Bonaire — Instructions on the Water ★★★
  • Public yellow/blue moorings (day-use): max 2 h, first-come first-served, one boat >4 m per mooring (or up to 3 tenders <4 m), max 13 m ★★★★★ · STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★
  • Two-tone overnight moorings (visitors): for visitors only, registration mandatory at Customs + Harbour Village Marina (VHF 17/12), use allowed only for the duration of your visa, no commercial activity on board, use your own line ≥6 m (do not tie directly), max 18 m (≈55–58 ft), no dinghy speeding ★★★★★ · STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★
  • Private moorings (residents): white/yellow/orange, reserved for residents with sedula and STINAPA permit — waiting list ~3 years, US$ 1,000/year, max 18 m — not available to visitors ★★★★★ · STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★
  • Nature Fee mandatory: US$ 40 p.p./calendar year for anyone entering the water or entering Washington Slagbaai; QR + ID on board ★★★★★ · stinapa.bonairenaturefee.org ★★★★★
  • IALA-B (US buoyage): red to starboard on entry — opposite to Europe ★★★

⛔ Absolute No-Go Zones (Official)

Area Prohibition Source
Entire BNMP — Bonaire + Klein Bonaire + Lac Bay (from the waterline to the drop-off, clear-water zone) Anchoring prohibited everywhere — STINAPA moorings only; only traditional fishing boats ≤4 m with a stone anchor excepted STINAPA — Mooring ★★★★★ · STINAPA — Boating ★★★★★
Klein Bonaire — No Name Beach and reef Strict uninhabited reserve: only yellow day-use moorings max 2 h, max 13 m, overnight stay and camping/fires prohibited STINAPA — BNMP/Bonaire National Marine Park ★★★★ · bonaire.com — Klein Bonaire ★★★
Lac Bay — RAMSAR/mangrove lagoon (east coast) Reserve and very shallow kite zone: no overnight mooring, approach only with tender/minimum draught and settled weather STINAPA — Lac Bay ★★★★
Washington Slagbaai (north-west, land park) Coast with no nautical facilities, continuous fringing reef: no harbour/mooring/anchorage recommended for yachts STINAPA — Washington Slagbaai ★★★
Mooring fields and harbours No towed watersports and no trolling inside the Park; keep 50 m from moored boats and from boats with divers STINAPA — Boating ★★★★★
Customs penalties Administrative/criminal penalty up to US$ 2,800 + 1 month for illegal anchoring; seizure on repeat offence 5730169490767872" target="_blank" rel="noopener">STINAPA — Mooring via BES Reporter / CruisersWiki ★★★

Full texts and official brochures: STINAPA — Boating PDF ★★★★★ and STINAPA — Rules and Regulations ★★★★★ · Interactive dive/mooring map: STINAPA — Dive Map ★★★★

  • The French Caribbean ZMEL system does not exist here: management is centralised under STINAPA + Harbour Village Marina on behalf of the Public Entity Bonaire (Openbaar Lichaam Bonaire).
  • There are dozens of public yellow moorings along the west coast (Buddy Dive, Eden Beach, Harbour Village, Salt Pier etc.) for daytime dives — max 2 h, not for overnight stays.

  • Free administrative chart: STINAPA brochure + interactive buoy/dive map at stinapabonaire.org + mooring management at Harbour Village Marina. ★★★★★
  • For day-to-day navigation: official electronic chart on the plotter + the paper chart above as mandatory backup; always stay on the seaward side of the buoys in the BNMP.

Not Included (For Now)

  • Windward east coast (Boca Onima–outer Lac Bay) and northern Washington Slagbaai: continuous fringing reef, no shelter, surf and swell — no mooring recommended for cruising yachts; approach only in settled weather, shoal draught and with local support → see 06 Safety & Security
  • Inner Lac Bay (kite lagoon): depth <2 m, RAMSAR mangroves, kiteboarding/tender only — unsuitable for sailing boats
  • Plaza Marina / Bonaire Nautico / Ocean Breeze (leisure basins): floating berths for leisure/charter by reservation, not public mooring fields — contact directly; details in 03 Ports

Mooring Checklist (Anchoring = Prohibited)

  1. STINAPA Nature Fee paid (QR + ID) and Visitor Entry Tax valid (30 days) ✓ — stinapa.bonairenaturefee.org + tourismtax.bonairegov.com
  2. Working holding tank + Y-valve to deck fitting (rangers may require a pump-out based on people/days/capacity) + pump-out at Harbour Village included (or US$40 per pump-out on the moorings) ✓
  3. Soft mooring line ≥6 m ready (no chain), fender to protect the line at the buoy; one boat per mooring, max 18 m / 55–58 ft ✓
  4. Contact Harbour Village Marina VHF 17 (and 12) before entry for mooring allocation; if Sunday/closed: take a free mooring and report the next morning; leave a pendant if you leave the mooring for a day-use dive (max 2 h) ✓
  5. Up-to-date electronic chart + IALA-B in mind + stay seaward of the buoys; check for north/west swell before entering (field exposed to winter cold fronts) ✓
  6. SailClear pre-notification filed before departure (no PC on the quay) + original zarpe from previous port ✓
  7. Dinghy dock identified: Karel's Bar (buy a drink) or Customs jetty — short chain + bar-lock padlock, hoist the tender aboard at night (frequent dinghy theft → 06 Safety & Security) ✓

Marine Trades & Chandlers

Last checked: 28/08/2026

The local hub is small and scattered around Kralendijk: for major refits, haul-out and composite work many owners rely on regional hubs (Curaçao — Caracasbaai / Curaçao Marine, Aruba — Oranjestad, St. Martin/Antigua). For day-to-day needs (outboards, electrics, antifouling, hardware) Kralendijk offers 3–4 solid addresses a few minutes' walk from the moorings. Contact is typically by phone/WhatsApp; languages spoken are Dutch, English, Papiamento and Spanish (Swedish/German at Budget Marine). For major jobs always ask for a written quote and confirm lead times in high season (Dec–Apr); spares = 1–3 weeks if ordered via Miami/Europe.

Where to Find What

  • Outboard/inboard engines: Boto Blanku (Yamaha) + Bonaire Marine Center (Suzuki/Simrad) + ABC Marine → see table above and 04 Services. Diagnostics also via Harbour Village.
  • On-board refrigeration/air conditioning: DATA MISSING dedicated technician on Bonaire — ask Budget Marine or Harbour Village for a freelancer; structured support in Curaçao.
  • Electronics/power (lithium batteries, panels, inverters): Bonaire Marine Center (Simrad/Navico, Uflex) + Budget Marine (wiring, corrosion protection) → limited availability, better to order in advance via Miami/Netherlands.
  • Sails: no resident sailmaker — urgent repairs with itinerant sailmaker in season; serious work at Le Marin (Martinique) or Curacao Marine ★★
  • Rigging: mobile professionals from Curaçao/Aruba; check references before work aloft.
  • Antifouling/careening: Seajet via Bonaire Marine Center, paints/antifouling from Budget Marine / Carene Shop equivalent, light careening at Ocean Breeze / Bonaire Nautico / El Navegante; 35 t travelift / 700 t dock at Marina Bas-du-Fort (Guadeloupe) or Curaçao for larger boats.
  • Gas/cylinders: propane refill in the marina (Harbour Village US$4.50/lb) ★★★★ — check local adapters.

Practical Notes

  • Payments: cash USD (official currency), cards widely accepted; bank transfer for special orders via Budget Marine Group. Always ask for an invoice (useful for customs/insurance).
  • Lead times: spares from Europe/USA = 1–3 weeks (DHL via Miami/Amsterdam); shops often order from distributors in St. Maarten (Budget Marine Cole Bay) or Curaçao.
  • On-board power: lithium/Victron/Mastervolt — limited availability, order ahead for delivery care of the marina stating boat name and mooring position.
  • Antifouling: available from Budget Marine (Seajet International) and Bonaire Marine Center; application by ABC Marine or El Navegante yard.
  • Hours: almost everything closed on Sunday; Budget Marine closes at 12:00 on Saturday — plan purchases for Friday.
  • For Amel and French-built boats: the dealers above work on all brands; for specific spares (e.g. Volvo/Yanmar) ask Boto Blanku/BMC and, if needed, order via Budget Marine St. Maarten or Curaçao.
