Provisioning

Last checked: 24/08/2026

General Price Level

  • Parco marino protetto senza insediamenti: nessun negozio, nessun ristorante a terra, nessun servizio. Tutto va portato da fuori (Union Island/Bequia). I boat-boys vendono solo fresco a prezzi alti per il trasporto, logica opposta alla Martinica. ★★★
  • Più caro di Martinica per qualsiasi cosa comprata in rada (trasporto in barge). Portare scorta completa è l'unico modo economico. ★★★

Supermarkets

Negozio Ubicazione Distanza dall'ancoraggio A piedi? Telefono Consegna a bordo? Note Fonte
NESSUN supermercato nelle Cays — — — — — Parco marino disabitato: divieto di costruzioni/negozi Parco Tobago Cays ★★★★
Rifornimento più vicino: Clifton, Union Island Clifton Harbour, Union Island ~3–4 NM (~30–45 min di barca) ❌ solo via barca propria o water taxi Vedi Union Island 07 ✅ sì — molti shop di Clifton consegnano via taxi-boat su accordo telefonico Fare spesa completa prima di entrare nel parco ★★★
Barge / Boat-boys in rada Passano tra le barche (Baradal, Petit Bateau) A fianco della barca — VHF 68 / a voce ✅ sì — vendita diretta in banchina Frutta/verdura, pane, pesce, aragosta (in stagione), ghiaccio occasionale, souvenir; prezzi da contrattare, qualità variabile Cruiser reports ★★
Alternative a nord: Mayreau / Canouan / Bequia — 5–15 NM — — — Per grande scorta meglio Bequia (Doris/Knights) — qualità superiore a Clifton ★★

Markets

  • Nessun mercato. Unici venditori: boat-boys autorizzati dal parco con braccialetto, che passano al mattino con barge di frutta/verdura/pesce. Chiamata su VHF 68 “1-2-1” o a vista. ★★★
  • Pesce/aragosta: i pescatori locali vendono direttamente in rada (verificare rispetto delle regole del parco — aragosta fuori stagione vietata). ★★

Water & Fuel

Service Where Notes
Acqua ASSENTE Nessuna banchina, nessun dissalatore a terra — portare pieno da Union/Bequia → 03
Carburante ASSENTE Stazione più vicina: Clifton (Union Island)
Ghiaccio Solo via boat-boys / bar ristorante galleggiante occasionale Disponibilità incerta, prezzo alto — portare da Clifton
Gas DATA MISSING — assente Rifornirsi prima → 04
Elettricità Nessun servizio a terra Gestione batterie/dissalatore a bordo

Taxisss / Water taxi / Bus

Service Detail Costo indicativo Note
Taxi terrestri Inesistenti — isolette disabitate — —
Water taxi Taxi-boat da Union Island (Clifton) / Mayreau per trasporto spesa/persone EC$ 150–300 a barca Clifton–Tobago Cays ★★ Prenotare via VHF 68 o tramite shop di Clifton; utile se si è senza tender potente
Boat-boys / Park rangers Servizio mooring balls + controllo parco US$ 10–15/giorno mooring fee ★★ Pagamento ai rangers, non è taxi ma gestisce ormeggio
Dollar bus / Bus Non esiste — Nessun trasporto pubblico — solo barca
Bus stile Martinica Assente — —

Practical Tips

  • Arrivare autonomi: acqua, carburante, cambusa per tutti i giorni previsti + 1 giorno extra; non contare sui boat-boys per basi. ★★★★
  • Contanti piccoli EC$/USD per boat-boys e fee del parco (nessun ATM, nessuna carta). ★★★
  • Ghiaccio: comprare blocchi a Clifton e conservare in freezer — in Cays si trova raramente. ★★
  • VHF 68: canale di chiamata boat-boys/rangers — chiamare al mattino presto per frutta/pane. ★★
  • Rifiuti: riportare tutto a Union Island — nel parco non si lascia nulla. ★★★

Yacht Customs Clearance

Last updated: 23/08/2026

Procedure SVG (valida per tutte le Grenadine)

  • Pre-registrazione SailClear obbligatoria prima dell'arrivo — sailclear.com ★★★★
  • Al banco servono: nº notifica SailClear, zarpe del porto precedente, passaporti, documenti nave ★★★★
  • Cruise tax: EC$35 a persona/mese (over 12 anni) — oppure EC$5/giorno fino a max 7 giorni (Bequia Tourism) ★★★★
  • Yacht a noleggio fuori SVG: tassa EC$5 per piede + eventuale licenza ★★★
  • Cruising permit 30 giorni al check-in, estendibile mensilmente; soggiorno up to 6 months senza visto per molti paesi — Cruising sources aggregate/Compass ★★★★
  • Uffici doganali SVG: Chateaubelair, Wallilabou, Kingstown, Blue Lagoon, Bequia, Canouan, Union Island — tutti su SailClear ★★★★
  • Orari standard: 08:00–12:00 / 13:00–16:00; extra-orari a tariffa maggiorata ★★★★
  • Uscita: stessa procedura a un porto d'ingresso ★★★

A Union Island (Clifton)

  • Porto d'ingresso: Clifton Harbour — customs + immigration ★★★★
  • Post-Beryl (2025): uffici pienamente operativi — Dream Yacht update ★★★
  • Uscita comoda per sud: Grenada spesso si sdogana più in fretta a Tyrell Bay (Carriacou) — Guida CCA nov 2025 ★★★

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 21/08/2026 · official sources verified

Status

Guadeloupe is a French overseas department (DROM): part of the EU as an outermost region but outside the Schengen Area, exactly like Martinique. Same regime for people; single EU customs territory for yachts.

EU Citizens — No Visa Required

Item Rule Source
Visa Not required for EU citizens for overseas territories immigration.interieur.gouv.fr, "Les visas pour l'outre-mer" ★★★★★
Documents Valid national ID card or passport — ID card suffices for Guadeloupe/Martinique Service-Public F591, checked 10/12/2024 ★★★★★
Stay ≤3 months "You may enter and stay up to 3 months in France (including overseas) without special formalities" [orig.: vous pouvez entrer et séjourner jusqu'à 3 mois en France, y compris outre-mer] Service-Public F10610, checked 20/11/2024 ★★★★★

⚠️ Transit warning: if the route transits a non-EU country (e.g. Sint Maarten, Antigua), a passport is required. [Service-Public F591 ★★★★★]

Important Note for Arrival by Sea

  • People checks (police) are separate from yacht clearance (customs): clearance is mandatory for all vessels to/from abroad → see 01 — Clearance.
  • When arriving directly from a foreign island (Dominica, Antigua, Montserrat) have ID documents for all crew ready: the online declaration requires them one by one. [2024, martinique.gouv.fr ★★★★★]

Beyond 3 Months? (EU Citizens)

No formalities to complete: there is no permit to renew nor extension to request.

Situation Rule Source
Tourist stay beyond 3 months For EU/Swiss citizens there is no specific limit on tourist stays; the carte de séjour in France is optional Les Îles de Guadeloupe (official tourist board), FAQ 04/06/2025 ★★★★; Service-Public F22116 ★★★★★
Schengen 90/180 quota Does not apply: Schengen rules apply only to the European territory of France (Art. 138 Schengen Implementing Convention). Days spent here do NOT count toward the European quota; conversely a Schengen visa does not allow entry into the Antilles immigration.interieur.gouv.fr ★★★★★; Service-Public F10610 ★★★★★
Long stays As everywhere in the EU (Directive 2004/38): sufficient means and health insurance; no document required unless you voluntarily apply for a title Service-Public F10610 ★★★★★

In practice: you may stay indefinitely (as a tourist) with a valid ID card alone. For local work or permanent residence, tax and residency rules change — seek dedicated advice.

The Yacht: No Time Limit

Yacht Rule Source
EU VAT-paid (typical case: Italian-flagged yacht) EU customs territory → free movement, no time limit, no cruising permit. Only online declarative clearance on arrival/departure from outside the EU douane.gouv.fr ★★★★★
Non-EU Temporary Admission (TA): max 18 months within the EU customs territory (Arts. 250–253 UCC); renewable by exiting EU territory (call at a third-country port in the logbook = proof); 10-year cumulative cap. In the Antilles also valid within the Single Market of the Antilles/OECS douane.gouv.fr "Régime particulier : l'admission temporaire", updated 15/02/2024 ★★★★★; EU Customs Code Art. 251 ★★★★★; bateaux-antilles.fr ★★★

⚠️ Non-EU yacht under TA: no charter and no sale within the EU, private use by non-EU residents only — violation triggers immediate taxation. ★★★★★

Vaccinations

No mandatory vaccination from the EU. Mosquito protection recommended (dengue present). ★★★★

Yacht Customs Clearance

Last checked: 21/08/2026

Who Must Clear

All pleasure craft, any nationality and flag, that: - enter French Antillean waters coming from a foreign port / foreign territorial waters or the high seas; - depart for a foreign port / foreign waters or the high seas; - move between the French islands of the Antilles (mandatory also Guadeloupe ↔ Martinique etc. since 01/09/2024). [martinique.gouv.fr 30/01/2026 ★★★★★]

Online Procedure (Mandatory Since 09/2024)

All the French Antilles use the same portal: https://www.demarches-simplifiees.fr/commencer/declaration-clearance-antilles — entry and departure declaration for vessels to/from abroad. [/ ★★★★; 2024, martinique.gouv.fr ★★★★★]

  1. Complete the online form (vessel, crew, origin/destination) before arrival or immediately after.
  2. Keep the PDF receipt sent by email: it is the document to show if inspected.
  3. No stamp, no queue: points agréés are only needed if you want assistance or have no internet.

After the first clearance in a French Antillean port, movements between Martinique, Guadeloupe, Saint-Barth and Saint-Martin are free and without formalities (same customs territory). ★★★★★

Stamped Paper Copy

  • Until other Caribbean states recognise the electronic declaration, print the attestation: a paper copy is required to check in to NON-French countries (e.g. Antigua, Dominica). [martinique.gouv.fr ★★★★★]
  • The stamp (if required) is obtained at a Point agréé Clearance for €5; with the online form alone you are not obliged to enter an official port. ★★★

Fees

Item Cost Source
Online declaration Free martinique.gouv.fr ★★★★★
Print + stamp of attestation at a Point agréé (optional) €5 Aggregated yachting sources ★★★

Regional Customs

Cruisers' Reports

  • Les Saintes (ISM): simple check-in, 14:00–16:00; internet and laundry available on site. ★★★
  • Deshaies: quick procedure but staff sometimes absent during advertised hours — avoid lunchtime. ★★★
  • Pointe-à-Pitre (Bas-du-Fort): office crowded in the morning and at lunchtime; electronic clearance at the harbour office 08:00–17:30 (08:00–13:00 / 14:00–17:30 off-season), Sun/public holidays 08:00–12:00. ★★★

Penalties

Failure to declare arrival/departure to/from outside the EU is a customs offence: financial penalties and possible seizure until regularised. With the online system there is no excuse: file before leaving the anchorage. [Code des douanes Art. 411 et seq. ★★★★★]

To Verify Before Your Cruise

  • Updated list of points agréés (new versions published by customs).

Ports & Marinas

Last updated: 21/08/2026

The archipelago can be cruised in 1–2 weeks with trade-wind windows. Routing logic: the Atlantic coast of Grande-Terre is exposed to the NE trades — sail clockwise or anti-clockwise, choosing leeward anchorages.

South — The Jewel

Area Character
Les Saintes Iconic bay, moorings, village; unmissable
Marie-Galante Rum, empty beaches; exposed, needs a weather window
Petite Terre Nature reserve, moorings only; top snorkelling

West Basse-Terre — Leeward Coast

Area Character
Deshaies Village, clearance, restaurants; rolls with NW swell
Malendure / Cousteau Snorkelling/diving; anchor outside the reserve
Ravine Paul Thomas Cruisers' top-rated anchorage
Anse à la Barque / Rivière Sens Hurricane holes with marina (Sud Ancrage, Barracuda)
Basse-Terre town Convenient roadstead for town stops

South Grande-Terre — Services

Area Character
Îlet du Gosier Easy staging post to/from Martinique–Dominica
Sainte-Anne Tourist beaches, sand bottom
Saint-François Full-service marina, clearance, sheltered lagoon

Pointe-à-Pitre & Jarry

Marina Bas-du-Fort = technical/logistics hub. The roadstead is regulated; the Grand Cul-de-Sac Marin (mangroves) offers quiet anchorages with a local pilot.

Atlantic Coast (Exposed)

Le Moule, Port-Louis, Anse-Bertrand: surf and rough seas in the trades; anchor only in settled conditions (Nov–Apr more manageable in the north). Port-Louis rated ★4.4 but mosquitoes at sunset. ★★★

La Désirade

Baie Mahault is the only truly sheltered bay; the rest of the island is exposed to the trades.

Operated by Compagnie Générale Portuaire (CGP). ★★★★

Service Detail
Berths 1200 (70 visitors + 40 moorings); depth 4.5 m
Travelift 35 t + 2.5 t crane
Haul-out Careening centre + 700 t floating dock (45×20 m); 6,000 m² technical area
Ashore Water, power 110–220–380 V, ice, wifi, laundry, showers/WCs, black-water pump-out, waste-oil collection
Security CCTV, night guard in season
Fuel dock 08:00–12:00 / 14:00–18:00
Contacts VHF 9 (07:00–09:00) · +590 590 936 620 · contact@marinaguadeloupe.com · marinaguadeloupe.com
Concierge Guadeloupe Yacht Concierge +590 690 72 88 09

Cruisers' notes: well-sheltered harbour but sewage smell reported at times; northern pontoons closed until further notice. ★★★★

Caraïbes Docks Services (Boatyard)

Careening, repair and marine maintenance. Tel +590 690 61 78 25 ·. Mixed reviews on cleanliness of facilities; staff not always English-speaking. ★★★

Jarry (Baie-Mahault)

The largest industrial/commercial zone in the Caribbean (3,500 businesses): industrial suppliers, refrigeration, electronics, dealerships. This is where you find parts that are unavailable elsewhere in the Lesser Antilles. ★★

Gas & Cylinders

Exchange for standard French bottles (butane/propane) at Jarry and at Super U outlets; watch the fittings. No refilling. ★★

Fresh Water

Water dock at Marina Bas-du-Fort (included with berth), Saint-François, Deshaies (town pontoon), Rivière Sens. ★★

Strategic Notes

  • Comparison with Martinique: for major works (full re-rig, heavy engine work, professional painting) many cruisers still use Le Marin: 70 t travelift vs 35 t, more specialist trades. Guadeloupe wins on position (further north towards Antigua/Saint-Martin) and slightly lower costs.
  • Winter storage: limited hard-standing; book well ahead for June–November; insurers require a written hurricane plan (floating dock or ashore).

Seasonality & Weather

Last updated: 21/08/2026

Climate

Hot and humid year-round: 24–30 °C, sea 26–29 °C. Dry season (carême) December–April; wet season (hivernage) July–November with heavy showers and increased cyclonic activity. [Météo-France ★★★★★]

Seasons

Period Conditions
Dec–Apr High season: NE trades 15–25 kn, variable sky, 26–29 °C, lower humidity
May–Jun Transition: lighter and more unsettled winds, hot and humid, first tropical waves
Jul–Nov Hurricane season (peak Aug–Sep): trades often light, sea >28 °C, real cyclonic risk

Cyclone Instructions (Préfecture ★★★★★)

Prefectoral hurricane plan: nautical instructions (consignes nautiques) are published daily during the cyclone season (alert levels 1–4, navigation bans and mandatory securing of yachts). Source: Préfecture de Guadeloupe + Météo-France.

Hurricanes

Guadeloupe lies in the heart of the hurricane belt: Maria (September 2017) devastated the archipelago (notably Deshaies and Basse-Terre). A lay-up plan is mandatory: Bas-du-Fort floating dock, ashore at Caraïbes Docks or run south (Grenada). Insurers require a written plan by set dates (usually 1 June).

Local Winds

  • NE trade wind steady year-round, accelerated along the south coast of Grande-Terre (funnelling between Pointe des Châteaux and Marie-Galante).
  • Les Saintes Channel: gusts between the islands and Sec Pâté; short, confused seas.
  • West Basse-Terre: leeward, flat sea, but afternoon valley breeze.
  • South-westerly swell: rare but makes every anchorage on the west coast roll (Deshaies, Malendure, Ravine Paul Thomas).

Typical Windows

Crossings Guadeloupe→Dominica or →Antigua: 30–40 M, feasible with trades ≤20 kn; best early morning when wind is lightest. The Guadeloupe–Martinique channel (110 M S) is best sailed on a post-frontal window in the dry season.

Local Weather Links & Charts

  • Météo-France Guadeloupe, St-Martin and St-Barth ★★★★★ — official site: forecasts by commune (incl. Les Saintes, Marie-Galante, La Désirade), vigilance, real-time cyclonic activity.
  • Météo Marine Guadeloupe ★★★★★ — coastal and offshore bulletins, active warnings, wind/sea-state charts.
  • Vigilance Météo ★★★★★ — official departmental alert map.
  • Sargassum Stranding Forecasts ★★★★ — dedicated "Sargasses" section on the official site (Guadeloupe and Îles du Nord).
  • CROSS Antilles-Guyana: gale/hurricane warnings on VHF 16 ★★★★★
  • NOAA National Hurricane Center ★★★★★ — Atlantic hurricane bulletins and tracks (June–November).
  • Windy · PassageWeather · PredictWind ★★★ — wind/swell models for passage planning.
  • Nautical instructions (consignes nautiques) published daily during the cyclone season [Préfecture de Guadeloupe ★★★★★]

Safety & Security

Last updated: 21/08/2026 · next media check: by 21/09/2026

Safety Rating: 4 / 5

Violent crime against tourists and cruisers is rare; main risk = theft (dinghies, outboards, items left on board). Slightly more caution needed than in Martinique: Guadeloupe has somewhat higher general crime figures, but concentrated in urban areas away from anchorages.

General Picture

  • *: incidents reported in Guadeloupe in recent years, mainly night-time thefts aboard and attempted break-ins in marinas; typical case: man scaled the locked guest-dock gate at *Marina Bas-du-Fort at night (cruisers raised the alarm, security intervened). Documented theft in 2025 (incident no. 3893). ★★★
  • Official statistics: prefectural report confirms crime concentrated in the urban districts of the Pointe-à-Pitre conurbation (Les Abymes, northern Pointe-à-Pitre, Baie-Mahault); drug trafficking generates inward-directed violence not aimed at tourists. [Préfecture de Guadeloupe, bilan annuel ★★★★★]
  • Canada advisory: normal precautions only; caution advised on isolated beaches and night transport. ★★★★

Zone Map — Offline

📍 16°06'00" N 61°23'24" W · WGS84

Orange = caution (evening theft / mugging). No red zone documented against yachts.

Safe Places / Places Requiring Caution

✅ Safe ⚠️ Caution
Les Saintes (very safe) Dinghy left unattended in the evening at Saint-François and Pointe-à-Pitre
Petite Terre (wardened reserve) Walking at night in Pointe-à-Pitre outside the harbour area
Deshaies, Malendure by day Les Abymes / Raizet districts even by car
Marina Bas-du-Fort (CCTV) Isolated beaches with valuables left unattended

Theft Targeting Cruisers

  • Dinghy/outboard: recurring incidents in Grande-Terre harbours; cut-proof chain + engine removed at night remain the standard.
  • Break-in aboard: favour well-lit yachts, secondary locks, valuables hidden; cases occur almost always between 01:00 and 04:00.
  • In marinas: report strangers on the pontoons to the guard; the Bas-du-Fort case was resolved precisely thanks to cruisers reacting promptly.

Aboard and Ashore

  • Documents and cash in the safe; digital copies.
  • Car: nothing on display, use supervised car parks; avoid stopping in sensitive districts.
  • Excursions: La Soufrière and waterfalls only on official trails; do not leave items in the car at trailheads.

Navigation

  • Fish traps and nets on the Atlantic coast of Grande-Terre (Le Moule, Port-Louis, Anse-Bertrand): marker buoys with near-invisible lines even beyond 3 miles — stay south of them or navigate with high sun. ★★★
  • North-westerly swell: rare but makes every anchorage on the west coast roll (Deshaies, Malendure, Ravine Paul Thomas); check swell (houle) before stopping. ★★★★
  • Nature reserves (Cousteau, Petite Terre): anchoring regulated/prohibited, active wardening → see 08 Pilot of Anchorages.

Provisioning

Last updated: 21/08/2026

General Price Level

  • Groceries approx. +30–40% vs mainland France, in line with Martinique; cheaper than the Grenadines according to cruisers. ★★
  • Good value on local produce: fish from fishermen, fruit/veg from markets, bread/boulangerie. ★★★

Supermarkets

Shop Where Notes
Hyper Casino Jarry Baie-Mahault Largest in the archipelago; everything, best prices
Carrefour Jarry Baie-Mahault Excellent French/imported selection
Super U / Leader Price Pointe-à-Pitre, Le Gosier, Sainte-Anne, Saint-François, Basse-Terre Found everywhere
Supermarkets Bas-du-Fort next to the marina Handy for quick top-ups

The Jarry area (3,500 businesses) is the largest commercial hub in the Caribbean: virtually everything is available here, including industrial parts and spares. ★★

Markets

  • Marché de la Darse (Pointe-à-Pitre, on the quay): fruit, veg, fish, spices — mornings, best on Saturday. Iconic yellow-and-green building.
  • Marché Saint-Antoine (Pointe-à-Pitre) and municipal markets at Basse-Terre, Saint-François, Capesterre (Marie-Galante).
  • Fresh fish: approach fishermen in the harbours (Deshaies, Saint-Louis de Marie-Galante) when boats return (~10:00).

Water & Fuel

Service Where
Water dock Marina Bas-du-Fort (included with berth), Saint-François, Deshaies (town pontoon), Rivière Sens
Fuel dock Bas-du-Fort 08:00–12:00 / 14:00–18:00; Saint-François; roadside stations at Jarry with jerry can
Gas (butane/propane) Standard French bottle exchange at Jarry and Super U outlets; watch the fittings

Practical Tips

  • Big shop = Jarry (car/taxi from the marina, 15 min); daily fresh produce = Darse market.
  • On the smaller islands (Les Saintes, Petite Terre, La Désirade) selection is limited: stock up beforehand.
  • Deliveries: some Jarry supermarkets deliver to the marina for phone orders ⚠️ to be verified case by case.

Pilot of Anchorages

Last updated: 21/08/2026 · positions approximate, navigate with official charts

General Anchoring Rules (First and Foremost)

  • Yachts up to 50 m: free anchoring permitted everywhere EXCEPT the reserves below and regulated harbour areas.
  • IALA-B buoyage — reversed compared with Europe (IALA-A). ★★★
  • Coral bottoms in the National Park: anchor and chain must not rest on coral.

⛔ Reserves & Prohibitions

Area Rule
Réserve Cousteau (Îlets Pigeon) Heart of the National Park: anchoring prohibited, mooring buoys only (for vessels <8 m); snorkelling/diving regulated ★★★
Petite Terre National nature reserve: anchoring prohibited, mooring buoys only (9×10 t + 1×30 t), advance booking advised ★★★
Grand Cul-de-Sac Marin / Petit Cul-de-Sac National Park: protection zones, anchoring regulated over coral
Harbours and channels Mooring regulated in the Pointe-à-Pitre roadstead

  • Petite Terre east coast: no shelter.

Anchor Checklist for Guadeloupe

  1. Clearance done? → 01
  2. NE trades forecast ≤20 kn on exposed passages?
  3. NW swell coming? (rolls entire west coast)
  4. Inside a reserve? → rules table above
  5. Fish traps reported on the Atlantic route?
  6. SHOM/Navionics chart up to date + IALA-B in mind
  7. Petite Terre buoy booked?

Deshaies

← All anchorages

📍 16°18'23" N 61°47'47" W · WGS84

Picture-postcard village (set of "Death in Paradise"), clearance point. Anchorage in 5–7 m over sand off the village or at Grande Anse to the north; swell causes rolling with north-westerly. Town dinghy dock for water; supermarkets, bakery, restaurants (La Kaz du Douanier). Deshaies Botanical Garden 10 min away. ★★★

Last updated: 22/08/2026

Désirade — Baie Mahault

← All anchorages

📍 16°19'45" N 61°00'31" W · WGS84

The oldest geological island in the world: wild plateau, colourful villages, abandoned leper hospital. Baie Mahault is sheltered from the NE trades, sand/weed bottom in 4–7 m; rolls with southerly. Ferry from Saint-François. Small shops and restaurants.

Official Charts

SHOM series Guadeloupe/Dominica (check shom.fr for updated editions) + Navionics/C-MAP. Buoyage IALA-B (reversed vs Europe). Beware the Mouchoir Carré shoals off Bas-du-Fort and the Petite Terre pass.

Not included (for now)

  • North Atlantic coast (Anse-Bertrand, Port-Louis, Le Moule): anchorage only in settled conditions, fishing pots → see 06 Safety & security.
  • Grand Cul-de-Sac marin (mangroves): quiet anchorages but local pilot needed for the passes.
  • Petite Terre east coast: no shelter.

Anchor Checklist for Guadeloupe

  1. Clearance done? → 01 Clearance
  2. NE trade ≤20 kn forecast on exposed passages?
  3. NW swell coming? (rolls the entire west coast)
  4. Inside a reserve? → table of rules above
  5. Fishing pots reported on the Atlantic route?
  6. SHOM/Navionics chart updated + IALA-B in mind
  7. Petite Terre mooring booked?

Îlet du Gosier

← All anchorages

📍 16°11'56" N 61°29'28" W · WGS84

Islet with lighthouse 20 min from the marina: turquoise water, sand, sheltered from the trades by the mainland. Sandy bottom in 3–6 m, good holding. Crowded on local weekends and with charter boats at lunchtime. Ideal first/last stop when arriving from or departing for Martinique or Dominica.

Les Saintes — Bourg de Terre-de-Haut

← All anchorages

📍 15°52'05" N 61°34'55" W · WGS84

The most photographed bay in the French Caribbean: Creole village, Fort Napoléon, beaches. Sandy bottom in 6–12 m, good holding; rolls with south-westerly. Moorings at Cabrit/Pain de Sucre €13–18/night. Services: ISM (clearance), shops, restaurants, water at the dinghy dock. Very crowded in high season: arrive before 14:00. ★★★

Malendure — Îlets Pigeon (Cousteau Reserve)

← All anchorages

📍 16°10'19" N 61°46'48" W · WGS84

The best snorkelling in the archipelago: Cousteau Reserve, turtles, coral. Anchorage on sand outside the reserve off Plage de Malendure (4–8 m, moderate holding); reserve moorings only for <8 m boats. Rolly with south-westerly. Ashore: dive centres, supermarket, laundry, petrol station 5 min on foot. ★★★

The island “as it used to be”: rum distilleries (Bielle, Poisson/Père Labat), caves, empty beaches. Saint-Louis: dinghy dock, clearance (Chez ZELES/customs by appointment), shops. Anse Canot (east) is the top-rated anchorage but exposed; pick a weather window. ★★★

Petite Terre

← All anchorages

📍 16°10'12" N 61°06'36" W · WGS84

Nature reserve: iguanas, turtles, dream seabeds. Mooring buoys only (9×10 t + 1×30 t), book in advance; entering via the pass with swell needs caution and high sun overhead. Spectacular snorkelling after the day-trippers leave. No services ashore: bring water and provisions. ★★★

Logistics base: clearance, 35 t travel lift, 700 t dock, Jarry 15 min away. Entrance between Pointe Fouillole and Presqu'île à Monroux; watch the Mouchoir Carré shoal (East cardinal) and the East pass only for draft <7.4 m. VHF 9. Town: Darse market, Memorial ACTe. ★★★★

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 28/08/2026

Status

Haiti è uno Stato insulare indipendente (Hispaniola occidentale). Contesto instabile: Dipartimento di Stato USA Level 4 — Do Not Travel al 10/07/2026 per rapimenti, criminalità violenta e servizi sanitari limitati; Labadee (enclave crocieristica) sospesa da Royal Caribbean fino a giugno 2027 ★★★★★. Vedi 06 Safety & Security e 01 Clearance.

EU Citizens / Italians — Visa & iKat

Item Rule Source
Passaporto Obbligatorio, validità residua ≥6 mesi dalla data di arrivo LegalClarity / DIE Haiti ★★★
Tourist visa Not required per italiani e molte nazionalità UE per soggiorni ≤90 giorni; soggiorno più lungo → visto/residence permit da richiedere prima della scadenza presso immigrazione haitiana. Per 9 nazionalità serve visto preventivo (verificare su ambasciata haitiana). LegalClarity / DIE Haiti ★★★
Tassa d'ingresso 10 USD all'arrivo (timbro) per esenti visto LegalClarity ★★★
iKat — carta digitale obbligatoria Obbligatoria per TUTTI (aria/mare/terra), entro 72 ore prima dell'arrivo e della partenza su https://delidoc.gouv.ht/ikat con generazione di QR code (digitale o stampato) da esibire a immigrazione/sanità/dogana. Sostituisce i 3 moduli cartacei precedenti (personali/viaggio/dogana/sanità). Modificabile con codice pratica + n° passaporto. Dal 01/05/2026 operatività completa su tutti i punti d'ingresso (decreto 31/12/2025). Se non compilata in anticipo → compilazione obbligatoria al controllo con rallentamenti. DIE Haiti / Ministère de l'Intérieur ★★★★★; InfoNation 13/03/2026 ★★★; HaitiLibre 24/02/2026 ★★★
iKat — avvertenza mare Validità anche per porti marittimi: compilare prima dell'approdo e tenere QR pronto per APN/Semanah/Douane. DIE Haiti ★★★★★

⚠️ Avvertenza Haiti — Do Not Travel: USA, Canada e Cruising sources aggregate sconsigliano viaggi via mare in Haiti per gang armate, rapimenti e colera endemico — vedi 06 Safety & Security e 01 Clearance. Chi procede lo fa a proprio rischio con aggiornamento quotidiano.

Arrivo via mare — documenti equipaggio

  • Controlli persone (immigrazione) separati da clearance barca (dogana/APN/Semanah): iKat personale è comunque obbligatorio per ogni POB (adulto e minore, pratica singola). → vedi 01 Clearance. ★★★★★
  • Tenere pronti passaporti, lista equipaggio, zarpe precedente e QR iKat.

Dopo i 90 giorni

Situation Rule Source
Soggiorno turistico oltre 90 gg Richiedere permesso di soggiorno a immigrazione prima della scadenza; oltre il termine → rischio multe, detenzione, espulsione e problemi per futuri ingressi LegalClarity / DIE Haiti ★★★
Lavoro / residenza Pratica dedicata presso DIE/immigrazione — non turistica DIE Haiti ★★★★★

The Yacht — permanenza e formalità

  • Nessun regime UE (Haiti extra-UE): permanenza barca legata a clearance e visto equipaggio; diritti portuali secondo prassi APN/Semanah — dettagli aggiornati DATA MISSING per indisponibilità di listino ufficiale online al 28/08/2026. → vedi 01 Clearance. DATA MISSING
  • Tenere a bordo: documenti barca, assicurazione, lista POB con QR iKat di ciascuno.

Vaccinations

Item Rule Source
Obbligatori Nessuno richiesto all'ingresso da UE se non transito da area a rischio febbre gialla OMS ★★★★
Raccomandati / rischio locale Colera endemico in Haiti; febbre gialla, dengue, malaria secondo aree/itinerario — consultare centro vaccinazioni before departure MSPP / OMS ★★★★

Useful Contacts visti

  • DIE Haiti — iKat ufficiale: https://delidoc.gouv.ht/ikat · https://immigration.mict.gouv.ht/formulaire-electronique-dentree-et-de-sortie-ikat/ ★★★★★
  • DIE Haiti: https://immigration.mict.gouv.ht ★★★★★

Yacht Customs Clearance

Last checked: 28/08/2026

⚠️ Situazione generale sconsigliata: Cruising sources aggregate e avvisi governativi segnalano per Haiti instabilità, gang armate, colera endemico e Level 4 Do Not Travel USA al 10/07/2026; navigazione da diporto fortemente sconsigliata salvo necessità con precauzioni estreme e aggiornamento quotidiano. Labadee (nord) sospesa al traffico crocieristico fino a giugno 2027 ★★★★★

Who Must Clear

  • Tutte le imbarcazioni in arrivo da/per l'estero, equipaggio incluso. iKat personale è comunque obbligatorio per ogni POB (vedi 00 Ingresso). ★★★★★

Procedure

Passo Cosa fare Source
1. iKat mare Compilare iKat su https://delidoc.gouv.ht/ikat entro 72 ore prima dell'arrivo/partenza (anche via mare) e conservare QR code per immigrazione/sanità/dogana; sostituisce i 3 moduli cartacei; modificabile con codice + passaporto; operativo su tutti i punti dal 01/05/2026 (decreto 31/12/2025) DIE Haiti ★★★★★; InfoNation 13/03/2026 ★★★
2. Approdo Presentazione a Immigrazione / Douane / APN / Semanah nel porto di ingresso con passaporti, documenti barca, lista equipaggio, QR iKat; possibile ispezione Prassi locale ★★
3. Zarpe / despacho Rilascio despacho per spostamenti costieri successivi secondo prassi locale Prassi locale ★★
  • VHF di chiamata: 16 (ove presidiato). ★★

Fees

Item Importo Fonte
Tassa ingresso persone (via iKat) 10 USD a persona per esenti visto LegalClarity ★★★
Diritti portuali/APN/Semanah DATA MISSING — listino non pubblicato online al 28/08/2026; chiedere in loco ad APN/Semanah o resort (Île-à-Vache/Port Morgan) DATA MISSING
Cruising permit specifico DATA MISSING DATA MISSING

Punti d'ingresso noti

Porto / Rada Coordinate Note
Cap-Haïtien / Labadee 19°46′N 72°12′W (Labadee) Nord; Labadee enclave privata Royal Caribbean — sospesa fino a 06/2027 ★★★★
Île-à-Vache — Port Morgan 18°06.30′N 73°41.70′W Rada sud; unico punto con minima infrastruttura yacht (resort), prudenza massima
Port-au-Prince 18°33′N 72°20′W (baia) Capitale; porto commerciale, sicurezza critica — evitare
Jacmel 18°14′N 72°32′W (rada) Costa sud; rada aperta, servizi limitati
Les Cayes 18°11′N 73°45′W Sud-ovest; rada

Punti agréé / autorità

  • APN (Autorité Portuaire Nationale) + Semanah (Service Maritime et de Navigation d'Haïti) + DIE/Immigrazione + Douane: presenti nei porti commerciali; presidio intermittente per diporto. ★★

Numeri utili clearance

  • APN / Semanah / Immigrazione Haiti: recapiti ufficiali DATA MISSING per fluttuazioni operative — coordinarsi via agente locale o resort (es. Port Morgan, Île-à-Vache) e VHF 16. ★★
  • DIE Haiti — iKat: https://delidoc.gouv.ht/ikat ★★★★★

Penalties / note

  • Soggiorno oltre i 90 giorni senza permesso → rischio multe/detenzione/espulsione. ★★★
  • Navigare senza clearance/iKat → sanzioni e fermo; controlli possibili anche in rada. ★★

To be verified

  • Listino diritti APN/Semanah aggiornato e procedura di zarpe inter-porti haitiani.

Other Boatyards e supporto

  • In caso di avaria/via d'acqua in acque haitiane: trasferimento immediato in RD (Ocean World / Casa de Campo / Luperón) con despacho/zarpe internazionale e assistenza Armada RD VHF 16 / 911; tenere a bordo EPIRB/PLB. ★★

Strategic Notes per il diportista

  • I riferimenti operativi RD (Ocean World, Casa de Campo, Luperón) restano validi come hub esterno: vedi Repubblica Dominicana · Servizi e cantieri. ★★

  • Assicurazione: la maggior parte delle polizze esclude o limita la copertura in Haiti — verificare clausola territoriale prima della navigazione. ★★
  • Chandlery / ferramenta nautica in Haiti: DATA MISSING — considerare non disponibile al 28/08/2026. ★★

Seasonality & Weather

Climate generale

  • Clima tropicale marittimo sulla penisola occidentale di Hispaniola (Haiti, latitudine 18–20°N). Temperature stabili, umidità alta, alisei dominanti. ★★★★
  • Regime sinottico condiviso con la Repubblica Dominicana (stessa isola), ma le informazioni operative di questa pagina riguardano solo Haiti. ★★★
Parametro Valore tipico
Temperatura media annua 25–28 °C in costa
Stagione secca dic–apr alisei NE–E 15–20 kt, aria più fresca
Stagione umida mag–nov più calda e afosa, rovesci convettivi

Seasons

Period Characteristics Finestra per la crociera
Dicembre – aprile Stagione secca: alisei stabili NE–E, scrosci brevi. Periodo migliore per muoversi lungo la costa haitiana e per le uscite verso Turks & Caicos o Giamaica ★★★★
Maggio – novembre Stagione umida e ciclonica: caldo umido, temporali pomeridiani, rischio cicloni tropicali. Con il contesto di sicurezza haitiano, navigare solo con finestre confermate ★★

Hurricanes

📡 Aggiornamento 25/08/2026 — Stagione Atlantico 2026 sotto la media (NOAA 75% prob. sotto-normale per super El Niño; picco ASO comunque aperto fino a metà ottobre). Attenzione residua: piogge eccessive e alluvioni flash. Fonti: noaa.gov ★★★★★, rcc.cimh.edu.bb ★★★★.

  • L'isola è colpita direttamente in media ogni pochi anni; mareggiate possibili anche con cicloni di passaggio a nord (Turks, Bahamas) ★★★
  • Nessun hurricane hole certificato in Haiti: per l'ivernage ciclonico i velisti usano Luperón (RD) — vedi pagina Repubblica Dominicana ★★★★

Venti e mari locali

  • Alisei NE–E 15–20 kt (dic–apr); accelerazioni nel Canale del Vento (Windward Passage, tra Haiti e Cuba) fino a 25–30 kt con mare incrociato. ★★★
  • Swell atlantico sulla costa nord (Cap-Haïtien) da NE in inverno (dic–mar): baie nord esposte, scegliere con riparo. ★★
  • Costa sud (Les Cayes, Île-à-Vache): più riparata dall'aliseo, esposta a S in stagione umida. ★★

Typical Weather Windows per le traversate

Traversate strutturate da Haiti: DATA MISSING per contesto sicurezza. Uscite abituali dei velisti: verso Turks & Caicos/Bahamas (N, dal nord dell'isola) e Giamaica (W) — pianificare su carta ufficiale con finestra aliseo <20 kt.

Weather Links & Local Charts

Servizio Cosa offre Fonte
NOAA National Hurricane Center Bollettini uragani atlantici (01/06–30/11) ★★★★★
Meteo Haiti (Unité Hydrométéorologique d'Haïti — UHM) Bollettini haitiani ufficiali, copertura limitata ★★★
Windy · PassageWeather · PredictWind Modelli vento/onda per pianificare ★★★

Practical Tips

  • In stagione secca (dic–apr) finestre più affidabili; in stagione ciclonica seguire quotidianamente NHC + UHM, avere piano B con uscita rapida verso RD. ★★★
  • Con il quadro sicurezza attuale, evitare soste notturne lungo costa se non necessarie. ★★★
  • Marea modesta (<0,5 m); correnti rilevanti nel Canale del Vento. ★★

Safety & Security

Safety Assessment: 0,5 / 5

Area Voto Motivazione
Haiti — sicurezza generale 0,5/5 Estremo: evitare. Controllo territoriale di gang armate, rapimenti, collasso servizi, colera endemico. Sconsigliato da tutte le fonti governative e da Cruising sources aggregate ★★★★★
Furti materiali a bordo 1/5 Furti opportunistici e violenze possibili anche in rada; nessuna marina sorvegliata operativa

Scala: 0 = terribile → 5 = molto sicuro. Currencyzione nostra, sintesi delle fonti sotto.

Perché così basso: controllo territoriale di gang armate su ampie parti del territorio, rapimenti, collasso dei servizi pubblici, colera endemico. Confronto: la vicina Repubblica Dominicana è valutata 3,0–3,5/5 (vedi pagina RD).

Overview — Haiti

  • Evitare la navigazione da diporto in acque haitiane se non per emergenza. Cruising sources aggregate: "Haiti — gang, colera, sconsigliato"; servizi di soccorso e autorità portuali intermittenti. ★★★★
  • Gang armate controllano ampi quartieri di Port-au-Prince e assi stradali; posti di blocco irregolari, rapimenti mirati a stranieri, collasso servizi pubblici. Copertura polizia limitata fuori dalla capitale. ★★★★★
  • Colera endemico e carenze sanitarie; strutture ospedaliere limitate, acqua non potabile senza trattamento. ★★★★
  • In caso di emergenza umanitaria/sicurezza, contattare l'ambasciata del proprio paese accreditata per Haiti (spesso a Santo Domingo). ★★★

Safe Places / Places to Avoid

Area Giudizio Perché
Île-à-Vache — Port Morgan Prudenza — unico punto tollerabile Rada rurale fuori dalle gang, resort presidiato, ma contesto nazionale resta Level 4 ★★
Port-au-Prince, Cité Soleil, Martissant, Croix-des-Bouquets Evitare assolutamente Controllo gang, sparatorie, rapimenti ★★★★★
Cap-Haïtien centro, Route Nationale 1-2 Evitare / prudenza estrema Blocchi e banditismo stradale ★★★★
Les Cayes / Jacmel rade Evitare — non documentabile Nessun presidio yacht, servizi intermittenti

Theft Against Cruisers (CSSN / rete sicurezza diportisti)

  • Furti opportunistici e violenze possibili anche in rada; nessuna marina sorvegliata operativa in Haiti continentale. Casi segnalati a terra e su yacht in rada non protetta — rete CSSN sconsiglia sosta prolungata. ★★
  • Currencyre sorveglianza notturna, luci, chiusura pozzetto anche in rada riparata; evitare esposizione di attrezzatura costosa. ★★

On Board & Ashore — precauzioni

  • A bordo: tender issato e lucchettato, fuoribordo assicurato, pozzetto chiuso di notte, niente contante a vista, documenti in cassaforte. ★★
  • A terra: spostamenti solo di giorno con referente locale fidato (resort/agente), mai da soli, evitare assembramenti e manifestazioni. ★★★★
  • Sanità: acqua solo imbottigliata/trattata, profilassi colera/dengue, zanzariere, kit medico con reidratanti/antibiotici. ★★★★

Navigation — rischi

  • Blocco e abbordaggi: rischio rapina armata sotto costa continentale; mantenere distanza dalla costa haitiana fuori da Île-à-Vache, navigazione diurna vicino a riva solo se necessario. ★★★★
  • Pescatori / linee galleggianti: innumerevoli linee <45 m su costa sud — elica/ancora a rischio (vedi 08 Ancoraggi). ★★
  • Carte e fari: cartografia datata, segnalamenti intermittenti — usare elettronica + satellite + vedetta. ★★

Rescue & Emergencies in mare

  • MRCC Haiti (Semanah): VHF 16, copertura limitata; in pratica i soccorsi gravi vengono spesso coordinati con l'Armada RD dal lato est. Tenere a bordo coordinate WGS84 pronte e lista POB. ★★
  • Kit consigliato: EPIRB registrato, PLB, AIS, zattera revisionata, cassetta medica con antibiotici/antidolorifici (colera/dengue risk in area haitiana). ★★
  • Coordinamento alternativo: MRCC Repubblica Dominicana (VHF 16 / 911) più reattivo; JRCC USA (Miami) su 2182 kHz / VHF 16 per emergenze gravi in area Hispaniola. ★★

Monthly Monitoring (per agenti)

  • Fonti da ricontrollare ogni 30 gg: travel.state.gov (advisory Haiti), gov.uk/foreign-travel-advice/haiti, voyage.gc.ca, Cruising sources aggregate, CSSN (safetyandsecuritynet.org), stampa locale haitiana, gruppi FB cruisers Hispaniola. Practical Tips del diportista

  • Non pianificare la cambusa in Haiti: considerare RD come unico hub affidabile; entrare in Haiti solo con scorte complete per 7–10 giorni. ★★★★
  • Acqua: dissalatore o taniche sigillate; evitare acqua di rubinetto. ★★
  • Contanti: USD piccoli tagli + gourdes, senza esporre somme; niente gioielli. ★★
  • Lista cambusa minima (se si tocca Port Morgan): riso, farina, olio, conserve, frutta locale, pesce dai pescatori — tutto il resto da RD. ★★

Schede ancoraggi

Île-à-Vache — Port Morgan

Coordinate: 18°06.30′N 73°41.70′W (porto/rada NW isola, 5,5 M da Les Cayes) — Cruising sources aggregate / Port Morgan ★★ · WGS84. Profondità: 3–16 m (8 m centro baia, 3 m sottocosta) ★★. Fondo: sabbia. Riparo: buono da E/NE, esposto a S-W.

Descrizione: isola rurale a SW di Haiti, fuori dalle zone gang della terraferma; rada NW nota come “Ferret Bay”, storica pirateria/morganesco. Resort Port Morgan con marina naturale, posti in banchina e boe (pescaggio max ~3 m) e servizi di sosta; villaggio Cay Coq/Cacor adiacente. Avvicinamento da sud/ovest con transizione rapida oceano→shelf (6–8 m a ridosso isola, attenzione a linee pesca galleggianti <45 m) — incrociare con Navionics/Free Cruising Guides Haiti ★★

📍 18°06'18" N 73°41'42" W · WGS84

Mediterranean Coast — Overview

La costa israeliana si estende per circa 270 km sul Mediterraneo orientale, da nord (confine libanese, area di Nahariya) a sud (Striscia di Gaza, area di Ashkelon), con principali marine/porti turistici a Haifa, Tel Aviv–Herzliya e Ashkelon. DATA MISSING su regolamenti per diporto — da verificare su Israel Port Authority / marinas.

Status

Madera è una regione autonoma del Portogallo: parte dell'UE (regione ultraperiferica) e inside the Schengen Area.

EU Citizens — Visa-Free

Item Rule Source
Visto Non richiesto per soggiorni fino a 90 giorni in 180 Service-Public F10610, verificato 20/11/2024 ★★★★★
Documenti Carta d'identità o passaporto in corso di validità Service-Public F398, verificato 26/08/2025 ★★★★★
Soggiorno Fino a 90 giorni in 180 senza formalità particolari; conta nella quota Schengen immigration.interieur.gouv.fr "Les visas pour l'outre-mer" ★★★★★

⚠️ Attenzione: Madera conta nella quota Schengen 90/180 (come Azzorre e continente). [immigration.interieur.gouv.fr ★★★★★]

Important Note for Arrival by Sea

  • I controlli persone (police/GNR) sono separati dalla clearance della barca (dogane/Capitania): la clearance è obbligatoria per TUTTI i natanti che arrivano da/portano verso l'estero Schengen, indipendentemente dalla nazionalità dell'equipaggio → see 01 — Clearance.
  • In caso di arrivo diretto da un paese extra-Schengen (es. Canarie, Marocco, Caribbean), tenere pronti documenti identità di tutto l'equipaggio: la dichiarazione li richiede (nome, data nascita, nazionalità, n° documento). [madeirayachtclearance.com 2026 ★★★]

Beyond 90 Days? (Italian/EU Citizens)

Registrazione obbligatoria presso la Câmara Municipal (Comune) del luogo di residenza per ottenere il Certificado de Registo de Cidadão da União Europeia (CRUE).

Situation Rule Source
Soggiorno oltre 90 giorni Registrazione CRUE entro 30 giorni dal 91° giorno; requisiti: risorse sufficienti, assicurazione malattia, alloggio mcs.pt 11/05/2026 ★★★★; Service-Public F22116 ★★★★★
Quota Schengen 90/180 Si applica pienamente: i giorni a Madera consumano la quota europea immigration.interieur.gouv.fr ★★★★★

In pratica: si può restare 90 giorni come turisti con carta d'identità. Per soggiorni più lunghi serve registrazione CRUE (non "permesso di soggiorno", ma certificato UE).

The Yacht: regime doganale UE

Yacht Rule Source
UE con IVA pagata (caso tipico: barca italiana) Territorio doganale UE → libera circolazione, nessun limite di tempo, nessun cruising permit. Solo clearance dichiarativa all'arrivo/partenza extra-UE douane.gouv.fr, regime UE ★★★★★; madeirayachtclearance.com 2026 ★★★
Extra-UE Admission Temporaire (AT): max 18 mesi nel territorio doganale UE (artt. 250–253 CDU); si rinnova uscendo dal territorio UE; tetto cumulativo 10 anni douane.gouv.fr "Régime particulier : l'admission temporaire" 15/02/2024 ★★★★★; Codice Doganale UE art. 251 ★★★★★

⚠️ Barca extra-UE sotto AT: niente noleggio, niente vendita in UE, uso esclusivamente privato da parte di residenti extra-UE — la violazione comporta tassazione immediata del natante. ★★★★★

Vaccinations

Nessun vaccino obbligatorio per ingresso da paesi UE. Raccomandata protezione antilarvale (zanzare presenti, rischio dengue basso). ★★★

Numeri emergenza

112 (unico numero europeo, funziona anche per Polícia Marítima e protezione civile). ★★★★★

← Madeira

Yacht Customs Clearance

Last checked: 24/08/2026 · Fonti: madeirayachtclearance.com 2026 ★★★, APRAM (Portos da Madeira) 2025 ★★★★, Capitania do Porto do Funchal 2025 ★★★★, Polícia Marítima 2024 ★★★

Who Must Clear

Tutti i natanti da diporto, qualsiasi nazionalità e bandiera, che: - entrano nelle acque di Madera provenendo da porto/mare territoriale extra-Schengen (es. Canarie, Marocco, Caribbean, USA); - escono verso porto/mare extra-Schengen; - si spostano tra Madera e Porto Santo solo se provenienza/destinazione extra-Schengen (movimenti intra-Schengen = nessuna clearance doganale, solo eventuale reporting Capitania).

[madeirayachtclearance.com 2026 ★★★; APRAM 2025 ★★★★]

Procedure arrivo da extra-Schengen (transatlantico, Canarie, Marocco)

  1. Contattare la Capitania do Porto do Funchal prima dell'ingresso (VHF Ch 16, poi canale operativo; o telefono/email).
  2. Presentarsi fisicamente alla Capitania (o punto designato GNR/Polícia Marítima) per:
  3. Controllo passaporti equipaggio (GNR/SEF/AIMA)
  4. Clearance doganale (Alfândega / Autoridade Tributária e Aduaneira)
  5. Crew list e dichiarazione merci
  6. Porti di ingresso designati (con presenza dogana/polizia confermata):
  7. Funchal (Marina/Cais da Pontinha) — hub principale, aeroporto, GNR, Polícia Marítima, Capitania, APRAM
  8. Porto Santo (Marina/Porto) — Capitania propria, APRAM, GNR; clearance autonoma
  9. Caníçal (Porto Comercial) — solo commerciali, non diporto abituale
  10. Altre marine (Quinta do Lorde, Calheta, Machico): coordinare la clearance attraverso Funchal o Porto Santo prima di procedere. [madeirayachtclearance.com FAQ 2026 ★★★]

Documenti richiesti

  • Passaporti/documenti identità tutto l'equipaggio
  • Certificato di bandiera / registrazione barca
  • Assicurazione RC valida
  • Patente nautica skipper (adeguata a bandiera/stazza)
  • Precedente clearance/uscita (se da porto extra-Schengen)
  • Eventuale prova status IVA/AT (barca extra-UE)
  • Crew list completa (nome, data nascita, nazionalità, n° documento, ruolo)

Fees

Item Cost Source
Clearance doganale/passaporti Gratuita (servizio pubblico) madeirayachtclearance.com 2026 ★★★
Taxa de farolagem e balizagem (fari/boe nazionali) Da confermare localmente (processata da Capitania) madeirayachtclearance.com 2026 ★★★
Servizi agente/assistenza (opzionale) Variabile, ~50–150 € madeirayachtclearance.com 2026 ★★

Departure verso extra-Schengen

Stessa procedura inversa: presentarsi alla Capitania del porto di uscita per checkout doganale/passaporti. Rilascio documento di uscita (necessario per ingresso destinazione successiva).

Cruisers' Experiences

  • Funchal: Capitania efficiente, abituati a transatlantici; marina 210 posti, baia riparata; aeroporto 20 min. ★★
  • Porto Santo: Marina 140 posti, più tranquillo; clearance autonoma; traghetto Lobo Marinho per Funchal 2,5h. ★★
  • Canarie → Madera: rotta comune (250 NM), alisei NE, finestra mag–giu; clearance a Funchal o Porto Santo. ★★

To Verify Before Your Cruise

  • Attuale operatività GNR/Polícia Marítima a Funchal e Porto Santo (turni, orari, preavviso richiesto)

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 21/08/2026

Status

Martinique is a French overseas department (DROM): part of the EU as an outermost region but outside the Schengen Area.

EU Citizens — No Visa Required

Item Rule Source
Visa Not required for stays up to 3 months Service-Public F10610, checked 20/11/2024 ★★★★★
Documents Valid national ID card or passport Service-Public F398, checked 26/08/2025 ★★★★★
Stay Up to 3 months with no special formalities; a valid ID is enough if checked Service-Public F10610 ★★★★★

⚠️ Transit warning: if your route to/from Martinique transits a non-EU / non-Schengen country (e.g. Sint Maarten, United Kingdom), you need a passport even if you remain airside. [Service-Public F398 ★★★★★]

Important Note for Arrival by Sea

  • People checks (Police aux Frontières) are separate from yacht clearance (Customs): clearance is mandatory for ALL vessels arriving from / departing to abroad, regardless of crew nationality → see 01 — Clearance.
  • If arriving directly from a foreign island (e.g. Saint Lucia), have ID documents for all crew ready: the online declaration requires them (full name, date of birth, nationality, document number). [2024, martinique.gouv.fr ★★★★★]

Beyond 3 Months? (EU Citizens)

No formalities required: there is no residence permit to renew nor a limit to extend.

Situation Rule Source
Tourist stay beyond 3 months For EU/Swiss citizens there is no specific limit on tourist stays; the carte de séjour in France is optional, never mandatory Les Îles de Guadeloupe (official tourist board), 04/06/2025 ★★★★; Service-Public F22116 (EU carte de séjour optional) ★★★★★
Schengen 90/180 quota Does not apply: the French Antilles are outside the Schengen Area (Art. 138 Schengen Implementing Convention) — days spent here do NOT count toward the European quota; conversely a Schengen visa is not valid for the Antilles immigration.interieur.gouv.fr, "Visas for overseas territories" ★★★★★
Conditions for long stays As everywhere in the EU (Directive 2004/38): sufficient means and health insurance for the period; no document to file unless you voluntarily request a title Service-Public F10610 ★★★★★

In practice: you can stay indefinitely (as a tourist) with a valid ID card. If you take local employment or establish residence, tax/residency rules change — seek specific advice.

The Yacht: No Time Limit

Yacht Rule Source
EU VAT-paid (typical case: Italian/French-flagged yacht) EU customs territory → free movement, no time limit, no cruising permit. Only the online declarative clearance on arrival/departure from outside the EU douane.gouv.fr, EU regime ★★★★★
Non-EU Temporary Admission (TA): max 18 months within the EU customs territory (Arts. 250–253 UCC); renewed by exiting EU territory (call at a third-country port = proof); 10-year cumulative cap. In the Antilles also valid within the Single Market of the Antilles/OECS douane.gouv.fr "Régime particulier : l'admission temporaire", updated 15/02/2024 ★★★★★; EU Customs Code Art. 251 ★★★★★; bateaux-antilles.fr ★★★

⚠️ Non-EU yacht under TA: no charter, no sale inside the EU, strictly private use by non-EU residents — breach triggers immediate taxation of the vessel. ★★★★★

Vaccinations

No mandatory vaccination for entry from EU countries. Mosquito protection recommended (dengue present). ★★★

Yacht Clearance

Last checked: 21/08/2026 · Main source: martinique.gouv.fr (updated 30/01/2026) ★★★★★

Who Must Clear In / Out

All pleasure craft — any nationality and flag — that: - enter French Antillean waters (Martinique, Guadeloupe, St-Barth, St-Martin) from a foreign port/territorial waters or from offshore; - depart for a foreign port/waters or offshore; - move between the French islands (mandatory even for Martinique↔Guadeloupe etc. since 01/09/2024). [martinique.gouv.fr 30/01/2026 ★★★★★]

Online Procedure (since 01/09/2024)

  1. Create an account on the portal and keep it — your documents remain saved and reusable.
  2. Current URL: https://demarche.numerique.gouv.fr/commencer/declaration-clearance-antilles [martinique.gouv.fr 30/01/2026 ★★★★★]
  3. Legacy URL still working: https://www.demarches-simplifiees.fr/commencer/declaration-clearance-antilles ★★★★★
  4. Complete the declaration with: vessel details (name, registration, flag, MMSI, type, length, tonnage…), owner, crew/passenger list (full name, date of birth, nationality, passport/ID no.), declarable stores, previous and next country, date/time/place of arrival and departure, intended length of stay, skipper's signature.
  5. Submit: the attestation arrives by email and is saved to your account.

Useful Tip (Feb 2025 ★★★)

On the platform you can duplicate a previous declaration and change only dates/ports — for departure, duplicate the inbound declaration and just update the date. Saves re-typing everything.

Stamped Hard Copy

  • Until the other Caribbean states recognise the electronic declaration, print the attestation: you need the paper copy to clear in at NON-French countries (e.g. Saint Lucia). [martinique.gouv.fr ★★★★★; Feb 2025 ★★★]
  • With the online form alone you do not have to call at an official port, unless you need the stamp. ★★★
  • The stamp is obtained at an Approved Clearance Point (Point agréé Clearance, official list v15/12/2025): take the file on your phone/tablet or log in on their computer; they print and stamp it. Cost €5. ★★★

Fees

Item Cost Source
Online declaration Free martinique.gouv.fr ★★★★★
Print + stamp of attestation at Approved Point (optional) €5 Cruisers' aggregated sources ★★★ + SDSA Feb 2025 ★★★

Penalties

Failure to declare is punishable under Art. 410 code des douanes, Art. 43 Ord. 2016-1687, Art. L.5242-2 code des transports. The attestation must be kept aboard and produced on demand to any French or foreign authority. ★★★★★

Ports & Marinas

Last checked: 21/08/2026 · Coordinates in decimal degrees or N/W as per source

South Coast — The Main Cruising Base

Le Marin ⚓ Main Harbour

  • 14°28.14'N 60°52.01'W · VHF 09 · www.marina-martinique.fr ★★★★
  • The largest marina in the eastern Caribbean: 830 alongside berths + 100 mooring buoys, up to 60 m LOA and 4.80 m draught, 220/400 V, black/grey water pump-out at the berth, medical centre, laundry, supermarkets, restaurants, hurricane shelter. ★★★
  • Typical berthing: stern-to pontoon, bow to mooring buoy; staff assist with manoeuvres. ★★
  • Clearance at the capitainerie (see 01).
  • Fuel: Station-service CAP Ponton N°3, +596 596 765 161, daily 07:30–13:00 / 14:00–17:00. ★★★★★
  • Boatyard recently upgraded with travel lift; many marine trades on site. ★★ → details in 04

Sainte-Anne

  • Huge, straightforward anchorage on a gently shoaling sandy bottom: room for hundreds of yachts. Good shelter from the trades; swell is rarely felt. ★★★
  • Dinghy dock: take care the hull doesn't slide under the pontoon in a swell; better to keep the bow raised or set a stern anchor. ★★
  • Clearance: Snack BOUBOU next to the church. ★★★★★

Pointe du Bout / Trois-Îlets

  • Marina Pointe du Bout (opposite Fort-de-France): +596 596 660 774 · marina.3ilets@marina3ilets.fr. Clearance at the marina. ★★★★★

West Coast

Fort-de-France

  • Capital. Visitor buoys in Baie de Fort Saint-Louis on a first-come, first-served basis ("turn up and see"), or anchor. ★★★
  • Port de plaisance de l'Étang Z'Abricots: +596 596 751 157 · contact@portetangzabricots.fr · attends 06:00–18:00. ★★★★★
  • Centre de carénage DCML Baie des Tourelles (clearance + boatyard): +596 596 717 464.
  • ⚠️ In town beware at the dinghy dock: tampering incidents reported; lock your tender. ★★

Anses d'Arlet (Grand Anse)

  • Picturesque bay; anchoring rules have varied in recent years — the installed buoys proved unworkable and you can still anchor close to the beach (respecting swimmers). Often rolly on the first night: tuck in as close inshore as you can. Customs patrol the entrance but do not board routinely. ★★★
  • Clearance: Cyberbase on the seafront (former Petits Bateaux / Grand Anse point NO LONGER active). ★★★★★

Saint-Pierre

  • Beneath Mont Pelée. Mooring buoys bookable only via the Navily app (new from 2025), payment in-app, easy to extend. ★★★
  • French buoys have rigid metal rings: you must thread your line through the ring (a long boathook such as Osculati / Magic boathook helps). Anchoring possible south of the buoy field (narrow shelf but well used). ★★★
  • Clearance: Office de tourisme Villa Sainte-Anne (rue Victor Hugo) or L'Alsace en Kay. ★★★★★

Atlantic (East) Coast

Le François — Pointe Bateau

  • Capitainerie marina, daily 08:00–18:00: +596 596 542 954. Clearance on site. ★★★★★

La Trinité / Havre de la Trinité

  • Official port of entry; clearance at the Brigade des douanes, Quartier Raisinier: +596 596 581 790. ★★★★★
  • ⚠️ East / south-east coast: numerous strings of fish traps with almost invisible floating lines, reported even more than 3 miles offshore. Keep a sharp lookout. ★★

North

Le Prêcheur / Northern Saint-Pierre

  • Open roadstead; only in settled weather. (word on the dock ★ — to be verified)

Seasonality & Weather

Last checked: 21/08/2026

Climate

  • Average temperature 26 °C year-round, maritime climate with moderate trades and heavy showers. ★★★

Seasons

Period Characteristics
December – April/May Dry, cooler season with steady trades: best time to cruise
July – November Hurricane season: many insurers impose area restrictions; Le Marin has a trou à cyclone (hurricane hole) but no shelter is guaranteed

★★★

Hurricane Instructions (official ★★★★)

Pontoon and mooring construction standards are compliant, BUT the harbour cannot be held liable for damage from failure of moorings/ground tackle caused by a cyclone. Document: Consignes aux usagers en cas de cyclones (Instructions to users in the event of a cyclone) (marin.marina-martinique.fr).

Hurricanes

Season June–November, peak August–October. Martinique has been struck by major cyclones in 1891, 1963 (Edith), 1979 (David), 2007 (Dean Cat. 2). Hurricane plan: préfecture consignes and harbour offices publish securing procedures; Marina du Marin requires contracts in advance for winter storage. [Météo-France ★★★★★; préfecture ★★★★★]

Local Winds

  • ENE trades typical of the Windwards; gusty katabatics off the high ground in west-coast bays. ★★
  • Inter-island passages (Saint Lucia Channel): beware collisions with cetaceans — a catamaran holed by a whale in the channel in 2017, the third such case in a few months according to the harbourmaster. ★★

Typical Weather Windows

Passages Martinique→Saint Lucia (22 M S) or →Dominica (30 M NW): feasible with trades ≤20 kt, best in the early morning when the wind is lightest. The Saint Lucia Channel (110 M towards Guadeloupe) is best with a post-frontal window in the dry season. ★★★★

Weather Links & Local Charts

  • Météo-France Martinique ★★★★★ — official site: forecasts by commune, vigilance, live cyclone activity.

  • Vigilance météo Antilles ★★★★★ — official alert map (green/yellow/orange/red).
  • Radar and satellite animations on the same site (Martinique radar) — Antilles radar mosaic 50/200 km, Antilles-Guiana satellite imagery.

Security

Last fully checked: 21/08/2026 · Next monthly check: 21/09/2026

Security Rating: 4 / 5

Aspect Rating Reason
Personal safety (visitors / cruisers) 4/5 Violent crime against visitors rare; no armed attack on yachts reported in sources in the last 5 years
Theft from yachts 2/5 Dinghy/outboard = endemic problem around Le Marin and Sainte-Anne (37 incidents recorded in 5 years within 10 km)
General island context 4/5 Overall crime below the French average; armed violence linked to drug trafficking, concentrated in Fort-de-France neighbourhoods and among locals

Scale: 0 = terrible → 5 = very safe. Our assessment, synthesising the sources below; updated at each monthly check.

Why not 5: recurring theft of dinghies/outboards (even when chained) and an escalation of drug-related armed violence in Fort-de-France. Neither category has so far targeted cruisers with physical violence.

General Picture

  • Canadian government advisory (updated 29/07/2026 ★★★★): "Take normal security precautions" (Prenez des mesures de sécurité normales) — lowest alert level. Petty crime (pickpocketing, snatch theft, car break-ins) concentrated in Fort-de-France; avoid deserted beaches and isolated spots after dark.
  • Préfecture annual report 2025 (presented 04/02/2026 ★★★★★): property crime (atteintes aux biens) −6.3%, burglaries −10%, vehicle theft −9%; overall rate 20.51 incidents/1,000 inhabitants vs 27.71 French average — exception: violent theft (vols avec violence) above average; assault +5.1%.
  • Drug-related homicides: 29 by firearm in 2024, 17 in H1 2025; attempted murders 88 (2023) → 199 (2024). Victims almost exclusively within trafficking circles, concentrated in Fort-de-France ★★★.
  • Local press 2025–2026: armed robberies in Fort-de-France (Terres-Sainville, Dillon, rue Lamartine, city centre with RAID intervention Sep 2025), restaurant at Sainte-Luce (Nov 2025), gunfire on the beach at Anse Moustique and Anse Meurnier during after yoles Aug 2026 (young local victims) ★★★.
  • No restrictive French advisory; tourist island with European-standard infrastructure.

Theft Targeting Cruisers

Data Caribbean Safety and Security Net (the.org ★★★), checked 21/08/2026:

  • 37 incidents in the last 5 years within 10 km of Le Marin: almost all dinghy and outboard theft, some burglaries aboard at anchor, vandalism. No violence against persons.
  • Recurring hotspots: Leader Price / Carrefour dinghy dock (2022×2, 2023, 2024), Indigo dock (2019, Jun 2026), marina (Apr 2022, Oct 2024, Aug 2025 ×2), Le Marin anchorage (burglary Jun/Sep 2022, Sep 2025, May 2026), Carenantilles yard (Nov 2024), Sainte-Anne (series 2022–2026), Baie des Anglais (Jul 2021).
  • Even chained dinghies have been taken (Sep 2022, Aug 2024).
  • Effective countermeasures reported by cruisers: short chain + padlock through the transom, engine always locked to the tender with a dedicated outboard lock, tender hoisted aboard at night, alarm on the dinghy, nothing left on view either in the dinghy or on deck.
  • Reporting incidents: (online report), gendarmerie maritime, CROSS. FB group "Martinique Cruisers" for rapid alerts ★★.

Pilot of Anchorages

Last checked: 21/08/2026

General Anchoring Rules (Read First)

  • Yachts up to 50 m: free anchoring allowed anywhere, EXCEPT the prohibited areas below and except over protected coral (arrêté of 25/06/2017): anchor and chain must not rest on reef. ★★★★
  • Yachts over 50 m: only at the exact positions in arrêté R02-2018-11-22-002 in 8 regulated bays: Saint-Pierre, Fort-de-France, Anses d'Arlet, Le Marin, Vauclin, François, Robert, Trinité. ★★★★

⛔ Absolute No-Anchoring Zones (Official)

Area Prohibition Source
Réserve naturelle des îlets de Sainte-Anne Anchoring prohibited within 300 m of every islet (Hardy, Percé, Burgaux, Poirier); moor only on site buoys Arrêté 09-00872 ★★★★
Wrecks off Saint-Pierre Anchoring prohibited over the historic wrecks off the town Observatoire ★★★★
Trous à cyclone in Cul-de-Sac du Marin (3 zones) Anchoring prohibited, temporary and permanent, except with an AOT (public maritime domain authorisation) Arrêté préfectoral ★★★★
Careening area at Le Marin Prohibited north of the line mouth of Ravine Trou Manuel → eastern quay of the fishing harbour Arrêté 27/07/2016 ★★★★
Marine protected area at Sainte-Luce (from south of Pointe Borgnèse to Pointe Philippeaux) Anchoring prohibited everywhere and at all times; moor only on buoys at the edge of the zone Arrêté 18/02/2000 ★★★★
Baie du Trésor (Caravelle) Anchoring prohibited throughout the bay except by day in the northern part of the beach bight; personal watercraft prohibited Arrêté ★★★★
Baie des Flamands – Fort-de-France Prohibited: access/swinging area for cruise terminal, Pointe Simon ferry channel, strip along Fort Saint-Louis (between the shore and points D–E) Arrêté 26/10/2006 ★★★★
RNRM du Prêcheur (Albert Falco reserve) Anchoring only in APID harbour areas and in existing professional sectors; prohibited elsewhere (except emergency) Délibération CR972 ★★★★

Full texts and official charts: page "Les zones d'interdiction de mouillage" (No-anchoring zones) on the Observatoire de l'eau (downloadable PDFs).

  • There are also ZMEL (organised mooring fields) and communal buoyage plans: charting is on the Observatoire site (Mémento réglementaire de la mer — Regulatory Handbook of the Sea) and on the commune-by-commune pages of the Direction de la Mer. ★★★★
  • Buoyage is IALA-B — reversed compared with mainland Europe. ★★★

Anchor Checklist for Martinique

  1. Official mooring chart downloaded (Mémento ODE) ✓
  2. Main anchor suitable for sand/mud (holding excellent almost everywhere)
  3. Long boathook for rigid French buoy rings
  4. Watch for near-invisible fishing buoys along the ENTIRE west–south coast
  5. Navily app installed if heading for Saint-Pierre

Marine Artisans & Chandlers

The undisputed hub is the port of Le Marin: mechanics, riggers, sailmakers, refrigeration engineers and electricians are clustered between the marina, Bd Allègre and the Carenantilles yard (Usine du Marin). Contact is typically by phone or WhatsApp; French is spoken and almost always English. For major jobs always ask for a devis (written quote) and confirm lead times in high season (Dec–Apr), when workshops are fully booked.

Carene Shop Antifouling, marine paints (7,000 colours mixed in-house), composite materials, hardware, anchors, chain — 0596 74 74 80 via website form / FB Usine du Marin (Carenantilles yard), 200 m² shop in the careening centre · ~08:00–13:00 · contacts: Hervé Ferrari (manager), Pierre ★★★★
Centrale du Bateau General chandlery, boat sales/charter, maintenance — 0696 43 70 11 via centraledubateau.fr Bd Allègre (Marina), Le Marin · since 2012 ★★★
Le Grenier du Marin Second-hand nautical gear — — — — ★★★

Practical Notes

  • Payment: many trades accept French bank transfer; for small jobs cash/card. Always ask for an invoice (useful for customs/insurance).
  • Lead times: spares from Europe = 1–3 weeks (DHL/Colissimo); workshops often order from metropolitan distributors. Common cruiser practice: order online (Victron, lithium, AMEL spares etc.) for delivery to Marina du Marin marked with boat name and berth number.
  • Onboard power: electrical components (battery chargers, inverters, solar controllers) available from Caraïbe Énergie (Caraïbe Marine division); complex installations also handled by Martinique Nautic and YES.
  • Antifouling: available from yard shops (Carene Shop) and chandlers; haul-out at Carenantilles or the yard areas in Le Marin.
  • For AMEL yachts: the firms above work on all brands; for the original aluminium mast rigging and AMEL-specific spares contact Caraïbe Marine (rigger) and Mécanique Plaisance (Yanmar/Volvo engine on AMEL yachts) first.

Official Charts

Chart Coverage Notes
SHOM 6738L La Martinique – Partie Sud Marin, Sainte-Anne, Anses d'Arlet, Sainte-Luce · ~€45 folded
SHOM 7041L La Martinique – Partie Nord Saint-Pierre, Prêcheur, Caravelle, Trinité · ~€45
SHOM 6892L Baie de Fort-de-France Scale 1:15,000, includes prohibited area Baie des Flamands · ~€45
SHOM 6898 (GA) Mer des Caraïbes Passage planning inter-island
NV Charts Caribbean pack Full Antillean arc Leisure alternative, WGS84, ~€95
  • SHOM charts show regulated areas and channels; available from authorised dealers (Picksea, Eau Bleue, NV Charts PoD). ★★★★
  • Free administrative charting: interactive maps from the Direction de la Mer + ODE “Mémento réglementaire de la mer” (regulatory handbook) PDF with all ZMEL/closed zones. ★★★★
  • For everyday navigation: official SHOM/Navionics electronic chart on the plotter + the paper charts above as mandatory backup.

Not Covered (for now)

  • Baie des Anglais (south, Cap Salomon): often quoted as wild and beautiful → insufficient data, to be verified
  • Anse Couleuvre / Le Prêcheur (north): exposed, only in settled weather ★★★
  • Baie du Vauclin / Robert / Trinité (Atlantic coast): attractive but exposed to the trades and full of fish pots → see 06 Safety

Martinique Anchor Checklist

  1. Official mouillage chart downloaded (Mémento ODE) ✓
  2. Main anchor sized for sand/mud (excellent holding almost everywhere)
  3. Long boat hook for French rigid mooring rings
  4. Watch for nearly-invisible transparent fish-pot buoys all along the west–south coast
  5. Navily app installed if heading for Saint-Pierre

Sainte-Anne — the classic

← All Anchorages 14°26.3′N 60°53.1′W ★★

Field Detail
Depth ~5 m off the village, gentle shelving over sand; room for hundreds of boats ★★
Holding Excellent holding on sand ★★★
Shelter Good shelter from E/ENE trades, limited swell; “Sainte-Anne Nord” variant even more swell-free ★★★
Hazards Dinghy dock: hull can slip underneath in a chop (anchor astern or lift the bow); fishing lines reported; dinghy theft possible ★★
Crowding High in season (Dec–Apr) — arrive early; local weekends busy
Restrictions ⛔ Réserve naturelle des îlets: anchoring forbidden within 300 m of Îlets Hardy, Percé, Burgaux and Poirier, land only at site moorings ★★★★; regulated zone >50 m ★★★★; swim zones off the beach ★★
Ashore Village with shops/restaurants a few minutes’ walk from the dinghy dock; clearance at Snack BOUBOU

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

Last checked: 25/08/2026

Status (cittadini UE/italiani)

Territorio d'oltremare britannico; la Exclusion Zone vulcanica condiziona anche navigazione e sbarchi.

EU Citizens — Visa-Free, fino a 180 giorni

Italiani/UE senza visto per soggiorni fino a 180 giorni: passaporto valido per tutta la permanenza (prassi UK: 6 mesi residui), possibili controlli su biglietto di ritorno e mezzi economici. gov.uk ★★★★★

Important Note for Arrival by Sea

  • Porto d'ingresso UNICO: Little Bay. Contatto h24 su VHF 16 con "Montserrat Port" (security); sbarco al molo, dogana nel terminal. Orari dogana lun–ven 8:00–16:00; fuori orario tramite security, con supplemento. visitmontserrat.com ★★★★★
  • Pre-arrivo DOPPIO: (1) SailClear (oppure il suo terminale all'ingresso del porto); (2) portale governativo Online Immigration & Customs, disponibile da 72 h prima, con ricevuta via email da mostrare all'arrivo. Guida dogana MCRS ★★★★★
  • Per la crociera costiera serve un'autorizzazione Coastal Cruising: sbarchi solo nelle spiagge autorizzate fuori dalla Exclusion Zone, max 7 giorni.
  • Pratica d'ancoraggio: il dragaggio (dal 2023) rende l'ancora poco tenace a Little Bay; alternative Rendezvous/Carr's Bay, con il capitano solo in dinghy per le formalità. Cruising sources aggregate ★★★

E dopo i 180 giorni?

Procedura di proroga oltre il periodo standard: DATA MISSING.

Unità Costi

Vaccinations

Nessuna vaccinazione obbligatoria dall'Europa; febbre gialla richiesta solo provenendo da paesi a rischio (gov.uk ★★★★★).

Yacht Customs Clearance

Last checked: 25/08/2026 · Fonti: Cruising sources aggregate ★★★ · Ocean Posse ★★★ · cruiserswiki ★★★

San Juan del Sur (POE più usato)

  1. At the entrance to the bay (0.5 mi wide, white buoy Fl(6)3s on the P-shaped reef): anchor south, linea dei 10 m, mai entro 91 m dalla riva (swell mag-ott)
  2. Board of the representatives of the Captaincy (Bavarian-style office on the hill): processo dello zarpe d'ingresso, ricerca leggera armadi possibile
  3. Costi riscontrati: ingresso immigrazione US$15 barca + ~$2/pax · zarpe internazionale d'uscita US$25 (qualche discussione su $25 vs $40) ★★★
  4. Immigrazione e Capitaneria sono adiacenti al molo: 20-30 minuti totali ★★★

Puesta del Sol (Marina, Pacifico nord)

POE attivo; clearance d'uscita interna US$15 riportata dai cruiser ★★★

Caribbean

El Bluff/Bluefields, Corn Island, Puerto Cabezas: POE ma permesso speciale da Managua per visitarle; costa caraibica con servizi minimi ★★★

Entry, Documents & Visas

📥 Download offline: GPX waypoint · ZIP paese — WGS84, guida in Offline & GPX

🚨 ALLERTA 25/08/2026

Rischio criminalità su yacht in aumento sul lato Caribbean. Aggressione ARMATA a Portobello (21/04/2026: 7-8 uomini mascherati armati hanno sequestrato l'equipaggio per ~20 min cercando stupefacenti) e furti ripetuti di dinghy/barche a Linton Bay e Bocas del Toro (feb-mag 2026). Corridoi del narcotraffico marittimi pericolosi di notte. Prudenza rafforzata: evitare soste notturne a Portobelo, doppie chiusure e luci, Verificato da agente il 25/08/2026 · Rivalutazione prevista entro il 24/09/2026

Scheda comune a tutto Panama: vale sia per il Canale che per San Blas/Guna Yala (che aggiunge regole proprie della comarca → vedi Panama · San Blas). Fonte principale: ★★★ aggiornata 2025–2026, ★★, ★★★★★.

Passo Dettaglio

Opzione Costo

Yacht Customs Clearance

Who Must Clear

Chi Obbligo
Tutte le barche straniere Entro 72 h dall'arrivo: Migración (persone) + Capitaneria/AMP (barca) + Permiso de Navegación oltre 3 giorni
Chi vuole transitare il Canale In più: registrazione PCA (Panama Canal Authority), admeasuring, agente/transit advisor

Procedure online

Passo Dettaglio
Preavviso email Fino a 72 h prima dell'arrivo: zarpe, licenza, passaporti → regionalcolon@migracion.gob.pa (lato Atlantico) ★★
Migración Ufficio principale Colón/Cristóbal o succursali (Balboa YC, Flamenco, Linton Bay): le succursali danno solo il timbro 72 h ★★★
Capitaneria + AMP Permiso de Navegación 1 anno US$185–193 (+agenzia ~US$235–240 tot) ★★★
PCA (transito) Registrazione su pancanal.com, admeasuring della barca, pagamento pedaggi e deposito, assegnazione slot ★★★★★

Transito del Canale — procedura

Passo Dettaglio
1. Admeasuring Ufficiale PCA misura la barca (LOA) a Cristóbal o Balboa; da qui dipendono tariffe
2. Pagamento Pedaggi + deposito cauzionale rimborsabile; si paga in anticipo presso banca autorizzata/online
3. Slot Assegnata data/ora; i piccoli possono condividere il transito con altre barche (rafting)
4. Equipaggio Richiesti line handler a bordo (minimo 4 persone totali consigliato); si possono noleggiare
5. Advisor Un transit advisor PCA sale a bordo alle chiuse (obbligatorio); prevedere pasti/letti per lui
6. Attrezzatura 4 cime lunghe ≥38 m (125'), 8 parabordi grandi (gusci noleggiabili a Shelter Bay/Flamenco)
Durata tipica 1–2 giorni; notte possibile in lago Gatún ancorati

Fees

Item Data
Pedaggi yacht ≤19,8 m (65 ft) Toll fisso ~US$1.935 (dic 2024) → ~US$2.130 (2025); struttura congelata fino a 30/09/2026; fascia 65–80 ft più alta
Deposito cauzionale ("buffer") US$988 rimborsabile se nessuna infrazione/danno; rimborso in poche settimane
Agenzia locale (opzionale ma comune) ~US$350–500 gestisce carta, slot, advisor, noleggio attrezzatura ★★

Paper Copy & Stamp

Conservare: zarpe d'ingresso, timbri passaporti, Permiso de Navegación, ricevute PCA — richiesti a ogni capitaneria e all'uscita.

Uffici utili

Ufficio Dove
Migración Atlantico Colón/Cristóbal (principale); succursali Linton Bay, Shelter Bay
Migración Pacifico Diablo/Panama City (principale); succursale Flamenco/Balboa YC
AMP (Permiso) Colón (Atlantico) · Diablo (Pacifico)
PCA Admeasuring Cristóbal (Atlantico) · Balboa (Pacifico)

Cruisers' Experiences

Fonte Sintesi
Fonti diportiste aggregate ★★★ 2024–2025 Succursali comode ma limitate: per visti lunghi serve l'ufficio principale; agenti accelerano tutto
Forum ★★ Transito piccolo ben organizzato; prenotare con settimane di anticipo in alta stagione (gen–apr)

Penalties

Violazione Sanzione
Nessun timbro entro 72 h Fino a US$1.000/persona ★★★
Barca senza Permiso >3 giorni Multa AMP + obbligo regolarizzazione

To Verify Before Your Cruise

  • Tariffa PCA aggiornata e depositi → Maritime Tariff ACP (toll <65 ft ~US$2.130 '25, congelato FY2026) ★★★★
  • Current average times for the slot (variables with drought congestion 2024–25)
  • Disponibilità noleggio cime/parabordi a Shelter Bay e Flamenco

AYS Panama (Associated Yacht Services, dal 2000/gruppo ASA 1975) ayspanama.com · uffici su ENTRAMBI i lati del canale 4.500+ transiti; formalità, permit, booking, bunker. Testimonianza capitano SY Acadia: «livello professionale eccezionale, comunicazione onesta» sito ★★★★
Orca Ships Agents 507 383-5937 · cel 6932-1136 · Santa Elena, Panama City · orcashipsagents.com Agente autorizzato ACP, 24/7/365; anche servizi yacht ★★★

⚠️ Avvertimento sicurezza: il servizio non autorizzato "Panama Canal Linehandler Exchange" è segnalato dall'agente Centenario come privo di licenza portuale e status migratorio legale — usare solo agenti autorizzati o line-handler forniti dall'agente stesso. ★★★

💡 Con un agente: niente deposito-cauzione per il transito, organizza ispezione, pedaggi, cime/galleggianti e line-handler. ★★★★

Fees del transito per uno yacht (verificati 2024–2026)

Voce Costo indicativo
Pedaggio ACP <65 ft ~2.130 US$ (tariffa gen 2025; era 1.935 nel 2024) ⚠️ aggiorna su pancanal.com
Pedaggio 65–80 ft da ~2.640 US$
Ispezione transito ~120–150 US$
Safety & Security ~165 US$
Admeasurement PC/UMS prima volta ~1.100 US$ ⚠️ da confermare con agente
Agente 350–500 US$
Line handlers ×4 ~100–150 US$ cad.
Noleggio cime ≥125 ft + mega-galleggianti ~75–100 US$
TOTALE tipico 3.000–5.000 US$

💡 Rimborso fino a 1.000 US$ post-transito se non servono motovedette di scorta. 💡 Con agente: nessun deposito-cauzione richiesto.

Praticità del transito

  • Servono 4 line handlers a bordo + timoniere; cime ≥125 ft ×4 in ottime condizioni.
  • ACP Advisor boarded for yachts <65 ft; minimum speed 8 kn (under 5 deny transit).
  • Programmare l'ispezione → transito normalmente 4–6 giorni (alta stagione ARC: 2–3 settimane).
  • Raft-up comune: catamarano al centro, monoscafi ai lati.
  • Balboa YC (Pacifico): boe e ritorno cime/galleggianti via taxi boat VHF 06 («Tito»).

Strategic Notes

  • Preparare il transito da Shelter Bay (Atlantico) o Balboa/Flamenco (Pacifico): attrezzatura noleggiabile, agenti presenti.
  • Lavori strutturali importanti: solo Panama City; Shelter Bay per tutto il resto.
  • Ricambi spedibili via Miami/Houston più rapidamente che dall'Europa.

Seasonality & Weather

Climate

Tropicale umido; Atlantico più piovoso del Pacifico. Temperatura aria 26–32 °C tutto l'anno, acqua 27–29 °C.

Seasons

Periodo Regime
Gen–apr (secca) Alisei NE 15–25 kn lato Atlantico; Pacifico: "Papagayo" da NE nel mattino, mare teso nel Golfo di Panama pomeriggio
Mag–dic (umida) Raffiche frequenti, venti variabili; Pacifico più coperto e piovoso (ott–nov picco)

Hurricanes

Panama is **outside the hurricane belt ** (lat <10°N): almost zero direct risk; residual waves possible from systems to the north.

📡 Aggiornamento 25/08/2026 — Stagione 2026: Atlantico sotto la media (NOAA 75% prob., super El Niño; CSU: 9 tempeste/1 maggiore) ma Pacifico orientale SOPRA la media (15-22 tempeste): il versante Pacifico di Panama guarda a quella stagione. Rischio principale in ASO: piogge eccessive e alluvioni flash (CariCOF). Fonti: noaa.gov ★★★★★, tropical.colostate.edu ★★★★, rcc.cimh.edu.bb ★★★★.

Local Winds

Vento Note
Alisei Atlantico costanti NE, raffiche sui pass tra Portobelo/Isla Grande
Papagayo/brisa Pacifico forte nel primo pomeriggio gen–apr sul Golfo di Panama
